Reorder a custom-field definition on a project by ID.

PUT /project/move-field/id/{id}

Moves a custom field to just before the before field, or to the end if before is omitted, and returns it as in Project.fields, plus its name.

Requires a user who is an admin of the project, and an app authorized with the Manage profiles permission; otherwise 403.

A missing field, or a missing before field, returns 404.

id: string
in path

Project ID.

name: string
in query

Name of the field to move. Percent-encode it, e.g. Billable%20Amount for Billable Amount; a + in the name must be %2B, since + means a space in a query.

before: string
in query

(Optional) Name of the field to insert before. If omitted, the field is moved to the end. Percent-encode it, e.g. Billable%20Amount for Billable Amount; a + in the name must be %2B, since + means a space in a query.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) for the field definition, or compact for just {"name": …}. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

200 OK
FieldDefinitionWithName

OK — moved custom-field definition.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — name missing.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the user isn't an admin of the project, or the app lacks the Manage profiles permission.

404 Not Found

Not Found — project, field or before field does not exist.

Response Content-Types: application/json
Response Example (200 OK) 
{
  "name": "Priority",
  "currency": "USD",
  "percent": false,
  "private": false,
  "lookup": "object",
  "options": [
    {
      "color": "13",
      "name": "High"
    }
  ],
  "hidden": false,
  "clearOnDup": false,
  "viewMembers": "[{\"oid\":\"iDsPd.QP_qM.hN.Trymukn8b\",\"id\":\"john\",\"name\":\"John\"}]",
  "editMembers": "[]",
  "locked": false,
  "withTime": false,
  "ndecimal": 2,
  "durationFormat": "hh:mm",
  "formula": "SUM(Subtask.Amount)",
  "resultType": "number",
  "lookupType": "User",
  "multiple": true,
  "conditionFormat": [

      "op": ">=",
      "first": "#/definitions/Number"

  "type": "number"
}

Rename a custom-field definition on a project by ID.

PUT /project/rename-field/id/{id}

Renames a custom field and returns it as in Project.fields, plus its name (the new name). The definition is kept, and task values move to the new name.

Requires a user who is an admin of the project, and an app authorized with the Manage profiles permission; otherwise 403.

A missing field returns 404; a new-name already in use, 409; an invalid new-name, 400 — it must be non-empty, without }, " or \, and at most 1,280 characters.

id: string
in path

Project ID.

name: string
in query

Current field name. Percent-encode it, e.g. Billable%20Amount for Billable Amount; a + in the name must be %2B, since + means a space in a query.

new-name: string
in query

New field name. Percent-encode it, e.g. Billable%20Amount for Billable Amount; a + in the name must be %2B, since + means a space in a query.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) for the field definition, or compact for just {"name": …}. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

200 OK
FieldDefinitionWithName

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — name missing, or new-name missing or invalid.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the user isn't an admin of the project, or the app lacks the Manage profiles permission.

Not Found — project or field does not exist.

409 Conflict

Update an approval category on a project by ID.

PUT /project/update-appv-cat/id/{id}/{catId}

Partial update: any of name, claimers, or approvers may be supplied; omitted keys preserve their current values. At least one key must be present, or it returns 400. claimers and approvers are lists of user OIDs; omit them or pass null for anyone, [] for the project's admins only.

Requires a user who is an admin of the project, and an app authorized with the Manage profiles permission; otherwise 403.

Response body is the updated category, or an empty object if the category no longer exists (e.g. removed concurrently). A plan without approvals returns 402.

id: string
in path

Project ID.

catId: string
in path

Category id.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) for the category, or compact for just {"id": …}. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

claimers: string[]

(Optional) New claimers list — users allowed to request approval in this category.

  • null: anyone can request.
  • [] (empty list): admins only.
  • List of user OIDs: those specific users.
approvers: string[]

(Optional) New approvers list — users allowed to approve, reject, or request changes in this category.

  • null: anyone can respond.
  • [] (empty list): admins only.
  • List of user OIDs: those specific users.
name: string

(Optional) New display name.

Request Example
{
  "claimers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "approvers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "name": "Legal Review"
}
200 OK
AppvCat

OK — updated approval category.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — body validation failed.

402 Payment Required

Payment Required — the plan doesn't include approvals.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the user isn't an admin of the project, or the app lacks the Manage profiles permission.

404 Not Found

Not Found — project does not exist.

project

Update a custom-field definition on a project by ID.

PUT /project/update-field/id/{id}

Updates the named custom field's definition and returns it as in Project.fields, plus its name. type is immutable: if supplied, it must match the current type. Omitted keys, flags such as hidden and locked included, keep their current values. A key that doesn't apply to the field's type returns 400. options and conditionFormat replace the whole list, and [] removes every entry.

To rename a select option, give its current name in from; tasks set to it get the new name. Example — rename High to Critical and keep Low:

{"options": [{"name": "Low"}, {"name": "Critical", "from": "High"}]}

Without from, nothing is treated as a rename: a current option that no entry names, in name or from, is removed, and tasks set to it lose that value. An entry without color keeps the current color of the option it matches; a new option gets one assigned. A from that names no current option, two entries matching the same option (by name or from), a duplicate name, or a name over 1,280 characters returns 400.

Requires a user who is an admin of the project, and an app authorized with the Manage profiles permission; otherwise 403.

Example — hide the field and lock its values: {"hidden": true, "locked": true}.

To rename a field, use PUT /project/rename-field/id/{projectId}?name={fieldName}&new-name={newName}; to reorder, PUT /project/move-field/id/{projectId}?name={fieldName}.

A missing field returns 404.

id: string
in path

Project ID.

name: string
in query

Name of the field to update. Percent-encode it, e.g. Billable%20Amount for Billable Amount; a + in the name must be %2B, since + means a space in a query.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) for the field definition, or compact for just {"name": …}. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

currency: string

(Optional, money/formula only) Currency symbol. Pass $ to reset a money field to its default.

percent: boolean

(Optional, number only) Format the value as a percentage.

private: boolean

(Optional) Hide this field and its values from guests and from the visitors of a public project or of a share link. A choice only without viewMembers; with it, the field is always hidden from them, so false is rejected with 400.

lookup: object

(Optional, lookup only) Map from lookup key to numeric value. Keys are OIDs of the configured lookupType entity. Replaces the entire map.

options: UpdateFieldOption

(Optional, select only) Replacement option list, each an object with name, an optional color, and an optional from. It replaces the entire set; [] removes every option. To rename an option, give its current name in from, e.g. {"name": "Critical", "from": "High"}; tasks set to it get the new name. Without from, nothing is treated as a rename: a current option that no entry names, in name or from, is removed, and tasks set to it lose that value. An entry without color keeps the current color of the option it matches (by from, else by name).

hidden: boolean

(Optional) Hide this field from the task detail panel.

clearOnDup: boolean

(Optional) Clear this field when duplicating a task.

viewMembers: string[]

(Optional) Users who can view this field's values; an admin not named sees the definition, not the values. Each entry is a user ID, OID, or email, or "me" for the authenticated user, and must be a member of the field's owner, an external team's member included. Pass [] for the admins only, or null for everyone private allows.

editMembers: string[]

(Optional) Users who can edit the values, in the same form as viewMembers; an admin not named can't. Editing also requires viewing the field. Pass [] for the admins only, or null for anyone who can edit the task. locked stops editing in Quire regardless of this list; the API ignores the lock, so this list still applies to API writes.

locked: boolean

(Optional) Lock the values: no one can edit them in Quire, admins included, while the API still can, e.g., to push values from another system.

withTime: boolean

(Optional, date only) Include time-of-day in addition to the date.

ndecimal: integer -1, 0, 1, 2, 3

(Optional, number/money only) Number of decimal digits. -1 means no rounding.

durationFormat: string hh:mm:ss, hh:mm, 1h1m, 1h, 1d1h, dd:hh:mm:ss, dd:hh:mm, dd:hh

(Optional, duration/formula only) Duration display format.

formula: string

(Optional, formula only) Formula expression, at most 5,120 characters.

resultType: string text, number, money, date, duration, checkbox

(Optional, formula only) Expected result type.

lookupType: string User, Task, Project, Organization

(Optional, lookup only) Source type for lookup keys.

multiple: boolean

(Optional) Allow multiple values. Applies to select, user, task, and file (always true for file).

conditionFormat: FieldConditionFormat

(Optional) Replacement conditional-format rules. It replaces the entire list; [] removes every rule.

type: string text, number, money, date, duration, select, checkbox, user, task, hyperlink, email, formula, file, lookup

(Optional) Field type. Immutable on update — if supplied, must match the existing field's type. Usually omitted; include only to verify the stored type. A project's field is one of text, number, money, date, duration, select, checkbox, user, task, hyperlink, email, formula and file; an insight's field is formula or lookup. A key for another type, such as options on a number field, returns 400.

Request Example
{
  "currency": "USD",
  "percent": false,
  "private": false,
  "lookup": "object",
  "options": [
    {
      "from": "High",
      "color": "13",
      "name": "High"
    }
  ],
  "hidden": false,
  "clearOnDup": false,

project

Update a custom-field definition on a project.

PUT /project/update-field/{oid}

Updates the named custom field's definition and returns it as in Project.fields, plus its name. type is immutable: if supplied, it must match the current type. Omitted keys, flags such as hidden and locked included, keep their current values. A key that doesn't apply to the field's type returns 400. options and conditionFormat replace the whole list, and [] removes every entry.

To rename a select option, give its current name in from; tasks set to it get the new name. Example — rename High to Critical and keep Low:

{"options": [{"name": "Low"}, {"name": "Critical", "from": "High"}]}

Without from, nothing is treated as a rename: a current option that no entry names, in name or from, is removed, and tasks set to it lose that value. An entry without color keeps the current color of the option it matches; a new option gets one assigned. A from that names no current option, two entries matching the same option (by name or from), a duplicate name, or a name over 1,280 characters returns 400.

Requires a user who is an admin of the project, and an app authorized with the Manage profiles permission; otherwise 403.

Example — hide the field and lock its values: {"hidden": true, "locked": true}.

To rename a field, use PUT /project/rename-field/id/{projectId}?name={fieldName}&new-name={newName}; to reorder, PUT /project/move-field/id/{projectId}?name={fieldName}.

A missing field returns 404.

oid: string
in path

Project OID.

name: string
in query

Name of the field to update. Percent-encode it, e.g. Billable%20Amount for Billable Amount; a + in the name must be %2B, since + means a space in a query.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) for the field definition, or compact for just {"name": …}. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

currency: string

(Optional, money/formula only) Currency symbol. Pass $ to reset a money field to its default.

percent: boolean

(Optional, number only) Format the value as a percentage.

private: boolean

(Optional) Hide this field and its values from guests and from the visitors of a public project or of a share link. A choice only without viewMembers; with it, the field is always hidden from them, so false is rejected with 400.

lookup: object

(Optional, lookup only) Map from lookup key to numeric value. Keys are OIDs of the configured lookupType entity. Replaces the entire map.

options: UpdateFieldOption

(Optional, select only) Replacement option list, each an object with name, an optional color, and an optional from. It replaces the entire set; [] removes every option. To rename an option, give its current name in from, e.g. {"name": "Critical", "from": "High"}; tasks set to it get the new name. Without from, nothing is treated as a rename: a current option that no entry names, in name or from, is removed, and tasks set to it lose that value. An entry without color keeps the current color of the option it matches (by from, else by name).

hidden: boolean

(Optional) Hide this field from the task detail panel.

clearOnDup: boolean

(Optional) Clear this field when duplicating a task.

viewMembers: string[]

(Optional) Users who can view this field's values; an admin not named sees the definition, not the values. Each entry is a user ID, OID, or email, or "me" for the authenticated user, and must be a member of the field's owner, an external team's member included. Pass [] for the admins only, or null for everyone private allows.

editMembers: string[]

(Optional) Users who can edit the values, in the same form as viewMembers; an admin not named can't. Editing also requires viewing the field. Pass [] for the admins only, or null for anyone who can edit the task. locked stops editing in Quire regardless of this list; the API ignores the lock, so this list still applies to API writes.

locked: boolean

(Optional) Lock the values: no one can edit them in Quire, admins included, while the API still can, e.g., to push values from another system.

withTime: boolean

(Optional, date only) Include time-of-day in addition to the date.

ndecimal: integer -1, 0, 1, 2, 3

(Optional, number/money only) Number of decimal digits. -1 means no rounding.

durationFormat: string hh:mm:ss, hh:mm, 1h1m, 1h, 1d1h, dd:hh:mm:ss, dd:hh:mm, dd:hh

(Optional, duration/formula only) Duration display format.

formula: string

(Optional, formula only) Formula expression, at most 5,120 characters.

resultType: string text, number, money, date, duration, checkbox

(Optional, formula only) Expected result type.

lookupType: string User, Task, Project, Organization

(Optional, lookup only) Source type for lookup keys.

multiple: boolean

(Optional) Allow multiple values. Applies to select, user, task, and file (always true for file).

conditionFormat: FieldConditionFormat

(Optional) Replacement conditional-format rules. It replaces the entire list; [] removes every rule.

type: string text, number, money, date, duration, select, checkbox, user, task, hyperlink, email, formula, file, lookup

(Optional) Field type. Immutable on update — if supplied, must match the existing field's type. Usually omitted; include only to verify the stored type. A project's field is one of text, number, money, date, duration, select, checkbox, user, task, hyperlink, email, formula and file; an insight's field is formula or lookup. A key for another type, such as options on a number field, returns 400.

Request Example
{
  "currency": "USD",
  "percent": false,
  "private": false,
  "lookup": "object",
  "options": [
    {
      "from": "High",
      "color": "13",
      "name": "High"
    }
  ],
  "hidden": false,
  "clearOnDup": false,
  "viewMembers": "[\"me\", \"john\"]",
  "editMembers": "[\"me\"]",
  "locked": false,
  "withTime": false,
  "ndecimal": 2,
  "durationFormat": "hh:mm",
  "formula": "SUM(Subtask.Amount)",
  "resultType": "number",
  "lookupType": "User",
  "multiple": true,
  "conditionFormat": [
    {
      "color": "42",
      "second": "200",
      "when": "today",
      "op": ">=",
      "first": "#/definitions/Number"
    }
  ],
  "type": "number"
}
200 OK
FieldDefinitionWithName

OK — updated custom-field definition.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — body validation failed.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the user isn't an admin of the project, or the app lacks the Manage profiles permission.

404 Not Found

Not Found — project or field does not exist.

project

Update a project by ID.

PUT /project/id/{id}

Updates an existing project and returns the complete updated record.

To archive or unarchive, set archived: true or archived: false in the body.

Who may change what: name, description, archived, public, start and due need a project admin, and an app with the Manage profiles permission. Followers need edit access to the project (not as an external team member), and an app with the Manage tasks permission, except for following or unfollowing yourself. With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. A body mixing them needs the rights of each; otherwise 403.

id: string
in path

Project ID.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) for the full record, or compact for just {"oid": …, "id": …}. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

public: boolean

(Optional) Public toggle. Specify true to make this project public; specify false to make it private. Making it public needs a plan with public projects; otherwise 402 (code 469).

description: string

(Optional) New description for this project (Markdown supported). An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

followers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to replace the current followers of this project (OID, ID, or email). This replaces all existing followers. To modify incrementally, use addFollowers or removeFollowers.

Accepts the same special values as addFollowers: "me" (the current user) and "app" / "app|team" / "app|team|channel" / "app|/path" (the application).

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"].

archived: boolean

(Optional) Archive toggle. Specify true to archive this project; specify false to unarchive.

start: string

(Optional) Target start date for this project: a date only, e.g. 2024-01-02; a value with a time of day returns 400. null clears it. Needs a project admin.

due: string

(Optional) Target due date for this project: a date only, e.g. 2024-05-25; a value with a time of day returns 400. null clears it. Needs a project admin.

addFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to add to this project (OID, ID, or email). Special values:

  • "me": the current user follows the project
  • "app": the application follows (receives notifications)

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL when invoking the registered hook. Example: hook https://super.app/hooks/standard + follower app|/soc1/33456/a7 → https://super.app/hooks/standard/soc1/33456/a7

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"].

removeFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to remove from this project (OID, ID, or email). Accepts the same special values as addFollowers: "me" (the current user) and "app" / "app|team" / "app|team|channel" / "app|/path" (the application).

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"].

name: string

(Optional) New display name for this project (Markdown supported).

Request Example
{
  "public": true,
  "description": "**Great** project to start with.",
  "followers": [
    "tzufRLqCnud74dARyDSvjWDl",
    "app"
  ],
  "archived": true,
  "start": "2024-01-02",
  "due": "2024-05-25",
  "addFollowers": [
    "sfsvLbDVPvi1QMf2GkDn7VSy"
  ],
  "removeFollowers": [
    "aBuz4MwfZ5CasOae6stnFa2f"
  ],
  "name": "My Project"
}
200 OK
Project

OK — updated project record.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — body validation failed.

402 Payment Required

Payment Required — public: true on a plan without public projects (code 469).

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the user lacks the role, or the app the permission, a given field needs: an admin and Manage profiles for name, description, archived, public, start and due; edit access and Manage tasks for followers, or for adding or removing anyone else, even along with yourself.

404 Not Found

Not Found — project does not exist.

Inspect the current API rate-limit usage for an organization.

rate-limit

Get rate-limit usage by organization ID.

GET /rate-limit/id/{id}

Returns the current per-hour and per-minute API usage for the organization with the given ID.

plan and the limits are those enforced. A trial doesn't change them: during one, they stay those of the plan before the trial.

For organizations in a paid master group, counters are shared across all organizations in the group.

This call is free: it never counts against the rate limit, so you can make it even while throttled.

in path

rate-limit

Get rate-limit usage by organization OID.

GET /rate-limit/{oid}

Returns the current per-hour and per-minute API usage for the organization with the given OID.

plan and the limits are those enforced. A trial doesn't change them: during one, they stay those of the plan before the trial.

For organizations in a paid master group, counters are shared across all organizations in the group.

This call is free: it never counts against the rate limit, so you can make it even while throttled.

reminder

A reminder notifies the people it names, either before a task's start or due date or at a time of its own.

reminder

Create a reminder by owner OID.

POST /reminder/{ownerType}/{ownerOid}

Creates a reminder on the given task, or under the given project, organization, folder or smart folder.

What a reminder on a task fires from depends on the task: one with a start or due date supplies the time — its due date, or its start date if it has no due date — so send leads alone. Sending when or recurrence then is rejected with 400, since they would be ignored. On a task with neither date, when is required. Without a task, when is required: the reminder has no other time to fire from.

A guest can't create one: a reminder takes write access, which a guest lacks, so 403.

Examples:

  • POST /reminder/task/{taskOid} with {"leads": [{"days": 1, "at": "09:00"}]} — on a task with a due date, notifies you at 9:00 the day before it is due.
  • POST /reminder/project/- with {"when": "2027-01-15T09:00:00.000Z", "name": "Pay the **bill**"} — notifies you at that time, as a personal reminder.
ownerType: string
in path

What the reminder belongs to: project, organization, folder, smart-folder, or task.

Always required; it doesn't default to project.

With task, the reminder is attached to that task and belongs to the task's project. A reminder cannot be moved to another task afterwards, and the task is chosen here rather than in the body — there is no task field to send.

ownerOid: string
in path

OID of what the reminder belongs to — a project, organization, folder, smart folder, or task, per ownerType.

Pass - with ownerType project for My Tasks, i.e. a personal reminder, visible to nobody else.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape:

  • full (default): the full reminder record.
  • compact: the OID only ({"oid": "…"}). Saves payload, tokens, and a server-side reload + render, so prefer it when you only need the OID to chain follow-up calls.

Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

when: string

When this reminder fires (UTC, ISO 8601). A plain instant — there is no all-day reminder, so a bare date is midnight UTC.

Required for a reminder that has no task, or whose task has neither a start nor a due date.

Rejected with 400 when the task already has a start or due date: the reminder then fires from the task's own schedule, and a when of its own would be ignored. Send leads alone in that case.

recurrence: Recurrence

(Optional) How this reminder repeats; when is the first occurrence.

Rejected with 400 on a reminder whose task has a start or due date — it then repeats with its task's schedule, so a rule of its own would be ignored.

leads: ReminderLead

(Optional) When to notify before the fire time, one notification each. Omit it for a single notification at the fire time, which is the default ([{"minutes": 0}]).

Each entry is an object naming exactly one of minutes (an absolute offset) and days (calendar days, so a lead spanning a daylight-saving transition keeps its wall-clock time), the latter taking an optional at clock.

Neither may be negative — a lead counts back from the fire time, and nothing fires after it — nor exceed 10,000 days ahead of it, and there may be at most 30 of them.

name: string

(Optional) Text to show instead of the default message. Only inline Markdown applies: **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, `code` and links; anything else, such as a list or a heading, stays literal text. At most 1,280 characters, not counting the markup (400 otherwise).

partner: string

(Optional) OID of the external team to share this reminder with; it then reaches every member of the project and of that team.

Only a project's reminder can carry one, and it cannot be combined with a members list ([] included) — both are 400. Without a task, it must be one of the project's external teams (400 otherwise). On a reminder attached to a task, it must be the team the task is shared with — the task's partner, or the nearest parent task's if it has none — or be omitted; any other value, and any value for a task not shared with a team, is 400.

An external team member shares a reminder with every member only through their own team. With members null, they must set partner to one of their teams; on a reminder attached to a task, that is the task's team. Otherwise 400 says what to send, as it does for a team of the project that isn't theirs.

Sharing with a team is part of Shared reminders, which needs the Premium plan or above (402 otherwise). Settable only when creating the reminder.

members: string[]

(Optional) Users who can see this reminder, and the only ones it notifies. Each entry is a user ID, OID, or email, or "me" for the authenticated user.

  • Omit the field — only the authenticated user. This is the default, except with partner: then every member of the project and of that team.
  • Pass null — every member of the owner. An external team member must also set partner to one of their teams.
  • Pass [] — only the owner's admins.
  • Pass a list — only those users.

Unlike a work's members, omitting the field does not mean every member: pass null explicitly for that.

Omitting it without partner, or naming only yourself (such as ["me"]), keeps the reminder yours; anything else shares it — the Shared reminders feature, which needs the Premium plan or above (402 otherwise).

Rejected with 400 when a listed user is not a member of the owner, when a non-empty list does not include the authenticated user, or when partner is also set. On a reminder attached to a task, every listed user must also be able to see the task (400 naming those who can't): a project member sees every task, but an external team member only the tasks shared with their team. A guest sees only the reminders naming them, and creates none (403: a reminder takes write access).

Settable only when creating the reminder. It cannot be changed afterwards, so recreate the reminder to change who can see it. A personal reminder (created under -) is always its owner's alone, so no one else can be named.

Request Example
{
  "when": "2027-01-15T09:00:00.000Z",
  "recurrence": {
    "freq": "weekly",
    "interval": 1,
    "byweekday": "[1,3]",
    "byweekno": 2,
    "bydayno": 25,
    "bymonth": 10,
    "dupsubtasks": false,
    "sincelatest": true,
    "until": "2020-12-22"
  },
  "leads": [
    {
      "minutes": 30,
      "days": 1,
      "at": "09:00"
    }
  ],
  "name": "Pay the **bill**",
  "partner": "rcBHBYXZSiyDRrHrWPutatfF",
  "members": "[\"me\", \"john\"]"
}
200 OK
Reminder

OK — created reminder record.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — body validation failed, for example a partner that isn't an external team of the project, or, on a task, other than the team the task is shared with, or members naming a user who can't see the task.

402 Payment Required

Payment Required — reminders need a Professional plan or above, and Shared reminders (members other than yourself, or partner) need Premium or above.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to create a reminder here (a guest included: a reminder takes write access).

404 Not Found

Not Found — the owner does not exist, the task is in the trash, or the caller can't see the task (an external team member can't see one that isn't shared with their team).

reminder

List a task's reminders, by ID.

GET /reminder/list/id/task/{projectId}/{taskId}

Returns the reminders the caller can see on the given task.

A guest sees only the reminders naming them. A visitor of a public project who is not a member sees none, as in the project view.

projectId: string
in path

ID of the project the task belongs to.

taskId: integer
in path

ID of the task, an integer unique within its project.

limit: string
in query

(Optional) Page size, 1..1000. Omit it to return every reminder in one bare array, which is the default; pass no to ask for that explicitly.

With ?limit=N, the last item of the response carries an extra cursor field when more reminders remain; pass it back as ?cursor= for the next page. The last page carries none, which is how you know you are done. Nothing carries one in an unpaginated response.

cursor: string
in query

(Optional) Resume after this item. Pass the cursor of the last item of the previous page, verbatim.

Reminders are ordered by oid. That order is stable, but it is not chronological — do not read it as oldest-first, and sort by the field you care about after fetching.

timing: string standalone, anchored
in query

(Optional) Lists only the reminders that fire:

  • standalone: at their own when — those with no task, or on a task with neither a start nor a due date.
  • anchored: from their task's due date, or its start date if it has no due date. Their when is omitted.

Omit it to list both. ?timing=standalone&status=active lists the reminders still to fire at a time of their own, e.g. to sync them to a calendar.

status: string active, all
in query

(Optional) Which reminders to list:

  • active: only those with a notification still to come — not one whose notifications are all past, nor one on a completed or archived task.
  • all (default): every reminder.

A page still holds limit reminders while that many remain.

200 OK
Reminder

OK — list of reminder records (may be empty).

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — invalid limit, cursor, timing or status.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to read the task's project, such as one not granted to this app.

404 Not Found

Not Found — the task does not exist, is in the trash, or the caller can't see the task (an external team member can't see one that isn't shared with their team).

reminder

List reminders by owner ID.

GET /reminder/list/id/{ownerType}/{ownerId}

Returns the reminders the caller can see under the given owner (by ID).

A project's list includes the reminders on its tasks, not only the task-less ones; narrow it with timing and status. Reminders on a task that is in the trash are left out, since there is nothing to act on while it is there; they come back if the task is restored, and stay reachable by OID meanwhile.

For a single task's reminders, use GET /reminder/list/id/task/{projectId}/{taskId}.

A guest sees only the reminders naming them. A visitor of a public project who is not a member sees none, as in the project view.

ownerType: string
in path

What the reminders belong to: project, organization, folder, or smart-folder. Always required.

ownerId: string
in path

ID of what the reminders belong to. Pass - with ownerType project for My Tasks.

limit: string
in query

(Optional) Page size, 1..1000. Omit it to return every reminder in one bare array, which is the default; pass no to ask for that explicitly.

With ?limit=N, the last item of the response carries an extra cursor field when more reminders remain; pass it back as ?cursor= for the next page. The last page carries none, which is how you know you are done. Nothing carries one in an unpaginated response.

cursor: string
in query

(Optional) Resume after this item. Pass the cursor of the last item of the previous page, verbatim.

Reminders are ordered by oid. That order is stable, but it is not chronological — do not read it as oldest-first, and sort by the field you care about after fetching.

timing: string standalone, anchored
in query

(Optional) Lists only the reminders that fire:

  • standalone: at their own when — those with no task, or on a task with neither a start nor a due date.
  • anchored: from their task's due date, or its start date if it has no due date. Their when is omitted.

Omit it to list both. ?timing=standalone&status=active lists the reminders still to fire at a time of their own, e.g. to sync them to a calendar.

status: string active, all
in query

(Optional) Which reminders to list:

  • active: only those with a notification still to come — not one whose notifications are all past, nor one on a completed or archived task.
  • all (default): every reminder.

A page still holds limit reminders while that many remain.

200 OK
Reminder

OK — list of reminder records (may be empty).

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — invalid limit, cursor, timing or status.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to read this owner.

404 Not Found

Not Found — owner does not exist.

reminder

List reminders by owner OID.

GET /reminder/list/{ownerType}/{ownerOid}

Returns the reminders the caller can see under the given owner.

A project's list includes the reminders on its tasks, not only the task-less ones; narrow it with timing and status. Reminders on a task that is in the trash are left out, since there is nothing to act on while it is there; they come back if the task is restored, and stay reachable by OID meanwhile. For a single task's, use ownerType task.

A guest sees only the reminders naming them. A visitor of a public project who is not a member sees none, as in the project view.

ownerType: string
in path

What the reminder belongs to: project, organization, folder, smart-folder, or task.

Always required; it doesn't default to project.

With task, the reminder is attached to that task and belongs to the task's project. A reminder cannot be moved to another task afterwards, and the task is chosen here rather than in the body — there is no task field to send.

ownerOid: string
in path

OID of what the reminder belongs to — a project, organization, folder, smart folder, or task, per ownerType.

Pass - with ownerType project for My Tasks, i.e. a personal reminder, visible to nobody else.

limit: string
in query

(Optional) Page size, 1..1000. Omit it to return every reminder in one bare array, which is the default; pass no to ask for that explicitly.

With ?limit=N, the last item of the response carries an extra cursor field when more reminders remain; pass it back as ?cursor= for the next page. The last page carries none, which is how you know you are done. Nothing carries one in an unpaginated response.

cursor: string
in query

(Optional) Resume after this item. Pass the cursor of the last item of the previous page, verbatim.

Reminders are ordered by oid. That order is stable, but it is not chronological — do not read it as oldest-first, and sort by the field you care about after fetching.

timing: string standalone, anchored
in query

(Optional) Lists only the reminders that fire:

  • standalone: at their own when — those with no task, or on a task with neither a start nor a due date.
  • anchored: from their task's due date, or its start date if it has no due date. Their when is omitted.

Omit it to list both. ?timing=standalone&status=active lists the reminders still to fire at a time of their own, e.g. to sync them to a calendar.

status: string active, all
in query

(Optional) Which reminders to list:

  • active: only those with a notification still to come — not one whose notifications are all past, nor one on a completed or archived task.
  • all (default): every reminder.

A page still holds limit reminders while that many remain.

200 OK
Reminder

OK — list of reminder records (may be empty).

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — invalid limit, cursor, timing or status.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to read this owner.

404 Not Found

Not Found — the owner does not exist, or, for a task, it is in the trash or the caller can't see it (an external team member can't see one that isn't shared with their team).

reminder

Update a reminder by OID.

PUT /reminder/{oid}

Updates the reminder with the given OID.

Only when, recurrence, leads and name can be changed. What the reminder belongs to, the task it is attached to, its members and its partner are all fixed when it is created — recreate the reminder to change any of them.

oid: string
in path

OID of the reminder to update.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape:

  • full (default): the full reminder record.
  • compact: the OID only ({"oid": "…"}). Saves payload, tokens, and a server-side reload + render, so prefer it when you only need the OID to chain follow-up calls.

Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

when: string

(Optional) When this reminder fires (UTC, ISO 8601).

Rejected with 400 on a reminder whose task has a start or due date — it fires from the task's schedule, so a when of its own would be ignored — and also when set to null on one that has no other time to fire from.

recurrence: Recurrence

(Optional) How this reminder repeats; null stops it repeating.

Rejected with 400 on a reminder whose task has a start or due date, for the same reason as when.

leads: ReminderLead

(Optional) When to notify before the fire time, one notification each. Replaces the current list.

Each entry is an object naming exactly one of minutes (an absolute offset) and days (calendar days, so a lead spanning a daylight-saving transition keeps its wall-clock time), the latter taking an optional at clock.

Neither may be negative — a lead counts back from the fire time, and nothing fires after it — nor exceed 10,000 days ahead of it, and there may be at most 30 of them.

name: string

(Optional) Text to show instead of the default message. Pass null to fall back to the default.

Only inline Markdown applies: **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, `code` and links; anything else, such as a list or a heading, stays literal text. At most 1,280 characters, not counting the markup (400 otherwise).

Request Example
{
  "when": "2027-03-20T18:30:00.000Z",
  "recurrence": {
    "freq": "weekly",
    "interval": 1,
    "byweekday": "[1,3]",
    "byweekno": 2,
    "bydayno": 25,
    "bymonth": 10,
    "dupsubtasks": false,
    "sincelatest": true,
    "until": "2020-12-22"
  },
  "leads": [
    {
      "minutes": 30,
      "days": 1,
      "at": "09:00"
    }
  ],
  "name": "Pay the **bill** today"
}
200 OK
Reminder

OK — updated reminder record.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — body validation failed, or a field that cannot be changed was sent.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the reminder does not name the caller among those who can see it, or the caller lacks write access (a guest named in it can read but not change or delete it).

404 Not Found

Not Found — reminder does not exist.

reminder

Delete a reminder by OID.

DELETE /reminder/{oid}

Deletes the reminder with the given OID. Unlike a task or a sublist, a reminder is not moved to the trash and cannot be restored.

Note: Returns 204 No Content regardless of whether the reminder exists.

oid: string
in path

OID of the reminder to delete.

204 No Content

No Content

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the reminder does not name the caller among those who can see it, or the caller lacks write access (a guest named in it can read but not change or delete it).

Response Content-Types: application/json

status

Task statuses represent progress values for tasks.

status

Add a new task status (by project OID).

POST /status/{projectOid}

Creates a new task status in the specified project and returns it. A value already in use in the project returns 409. A name already in use, ignoring case, gets a numbered suffix, e.g. Doing (1).

Requires a user who can manage the project's statuses, and an app with the Manage statuses permission; otherwise 403. An external team's members can't.

Example: {"name": "Review", "value": 70, "color": "35"}.

A status over the plan's status limit returns 402.

projectOid: string
in path

Project OID to add the status to.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) for the full record, or compact for just {"value": …}. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

color: string

(Optional) Status color index from Quire’s predefined palette. If omitted, a color will be generated automatically. Two-digit code: first digit 0–5, second digit 0–7 (e.g., 35).

name: string

Display name of the status.

value: integer

Non-negative integer indicating progress. Must be unique within its context (e.g., project); a value already in use returns 409. Values ≥ 100 are treated as completed. When listing or searching tasks, ?status=100 (or completed) matches every completed status; values above 100 can't be filtered individually.

Request Example
{
  "color": "35",
  "name": "Doing",
  "value": 50
}
200 OK
Status

OK — newly created status.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — body validation failed.

402 Payment Required

Payment Required — plan's status limit is reached (code 469).

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the user can't manage the project's statuses, or the app lacks the Manage statuses permission.

404 Not Found

Not Found — project does not exist.

409 Conflict

Conflict — a status with this value already exists.

Response Content-Types: application/json
Response Example (200 OK) 
{
  "color": "35",
  "name": "Doing",
  "value": 50
}

status

Update a task status (by project OID).

PUT /status/{projectOid}/{value}

Updates an existing status and returns the complete updated record. Omitted body fields are left unchanged. A name already in use, ignoring case, gets a numbered suffix, e.g. Doing (1). The value of 0 (the initial status) and 100 (completed) can't change (403); changing value to one already in use returns 409. With ?return=compact, the response holds the value after the update.

Requires a user who can manage the project's statuses, and an app with the Manage statuses permission; otherwise 403. An external team's members can't.

projectOid: string
in path

Project OID.

value: integer
in path

Status value to update.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) for the full record, or compact for just {"value": …}. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

color: string

(Optional) Status color index from Quire’s predefined palette (two digits: first 0–5, second 0–7; e.g., 35).

name: string

(Optional) New display name for the status.

value: integer

(Optional) New numeric status value. Non-negative integer indicating progress. Must be unique within the project; a value already in use returns 409. Values ≥ 100 are treated as completed. When listing or searching tasks, ?status=100 (or completed) matches every completed status; values above 100 can't be filtered individually. The value of 0 (the initial status) and 100 (completed) can't change.

  "color": "35",
  "name": "Later",
  "value": 50
}

Delete a task status (by project OID).

DELETE /status/{projectOid}/{value}

Deletes the specified status; its tasks move to the next lower status. 0 (the initial status) and 100 (completed) can't be deleted (403).

Requires a user who can manage the project's statuses, and an app with the Manage statuses permission; otherwise 403. An external team's members can't.

Returns 204 No Content, also when the status doesn't exist.

storage

A simple key–value storage for application-specific data. Each value is any JSON value, kept per authorization of your app. A key is addressed as /storage/{name}: unlike other resources, there is no /storage/id/... form (404).

storage

Get a stored value.

GET /storage/{name}

Returns the value stored under name, exactly as it was stored: any JSON value, such as an object, array, string or number. 404 if there is none.

Example: after PUT /storage/latest with the body {"project": "my_project"}, GET /storage/latest returns {"project": "my_project"}.

Stored data belongs to the authorization — the user's grant to the app, behind its refresh token — not to the access token: a refreshed or new access token of the same authorization sees the same data. It is deleted when the authorization is revoked or expires, or when the user is deleted.

Limits:

  • Keys per authorization, by the user's best plan (a trial doesn't count): Free 15, Professional 100, Premium 250, Enterprise 1,000. A PUT adding a key beyond that returns 402 (code 469); delete keys or upgrade.
  • A value is at most 4 KiB as JSON; a larger one returns 413.
  • Each call costs 1 rate-limit unit, counted against the organization of that best plan; a user in no organization has a bucket of their own, at the Free plan's limits. Over the limit, 429 with Retry-After.
name: string
in path

The key. Any string except id and list, and one starting with :}>.

200 OK
StorageValue

OK — the stored value, as it was stored.

404 Not Found

Not Found — no value is stored under this key.

429 Too Many Requests

Too Many Requests — rate limit reached. Honor Retry-After.

Response Content-Types: application/json
Response Example (200 OK) 
"object"
storage

List all stored entries.

GET /storage/list

Returns the stored entries of the current authorization.

The response is one JSON object mapping each key to its value, as it was stored — at most 20 entries, by key ascending, and {} if none. There is no paging: with more than 20 keys, narrow the listing with GET /storage/list/{prefix}.

Example: {"latest": {"project": "my_project"}, "theme": "dark"}.

Stored data belongs to the authorization — the user's grant to the app, behind its refresh token — not to the access token: a refreshed or new access token of the same authorization sees the same data. It is deleted when the authorization is revoked or expires, or when the user is deleted.

  • Each call costs 1 rate-limit unit, counted against the organization of that best plan; a user in no organization has a bucket of their own, at the Free plan's limits. Over the limit, 429 with Retry-After.
200 OK
StorageEntries

OK — key-to-value object of the stored entries (may be {}).

Response Content-Types: application/json

sublist

A sublist is a collection of tasks, representing a subset of tasks from a larger scope. To list the tasks of a project's sublist, use GET /task/search/id/{projectId}?sublist={sublistId}.

sublist

Create a sublist by owner OID.

POST /sublist/{ownerType}/{ownerOid}

Creates a sublist under the given owner — a project, organization, folder, or smart-folder — and returns it.

Example — POST /sublist/id/project/my_project:

{
  "name": "Sprint 12",
  "includes": ["2MmYOpJH_ZLeehIjjytH1Rwr"],
  "due": "2026-11-30"
}

includes adds those tasks with all their subtasks. To start with every task instead, pass "all": true, then leave tasks out by updating the sublist with changes.

Returns 402 if the plan's sublist limit is reached.

ownerType: string
in path

Owner type. One of project, organization, folder, or smart-folder. If omitted, project is assumed. For example, /abc123 is equivalent to /project/abc123.

ownerOid: string
in path

OID of the owner the new sublist will belong to.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) returns the full sublist record; compact returns only {"oid": "…", "id": "…"}, which is cheaper — use it when you don't need the record back. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

all: boolean

(Optional) Whether every task belongs to the sublist by default. Default: false — only the tasks in includes are in it, with their subtasks. With true, every task of the owner is in it; leave tasks out afterwards by updating the sublist with changes ("exclude": true). Settable only when creating the sublist.

includes: string[]

(Optional) List of task OIDs to include in this sublist. All descendants of the specified tasks will be included as well.

description: string

(Optional) Description of the record (Markdown supported). An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

iconColor: string

(Optional) Icon color index from Quire's predefined palette. Two-digit code [0-5][0-7]: first digit 0-5, second digit 0-7 (e.g. 00, 37, 57). NOT a CSS hex color.

image: string icon-view-list, icon-view-kanban, icon-grid, icon-view-timeline, icon-calendar, icon-timer, icon-briefcase-o, icon-rocket-o, icon-bug-o, icon-user-o, icon-colleagues-o, icon-lightbulb-o, icon-leaf-o, icon-clapperboard, icon-sitemap-o, icon-list, icon-flash-on-o, icon-piggy-bank-o, icon-graduation-cap-o, icon-paper-plane-o, icon-globe-o, icon-music-o, icon-detail, icon-beach-o, icon-paper, icon-home-o, icon-building, icon-database-o, icon-microscope-o, icon-hamburger-o, icon-trophy-o, icon-thumbs-o-up, icon-thumbs-o-down, icon-smile-o, icon-frown-o, icon-meh-o, icon-bullseye, icon-incomplete, icon-filter-o, icon-comment, icon-view-insight, icon-view-dashboard, icon-square-dotted-o

(Optional) Icon image identifier, one of the listed values.

name: string

Display name of the record (Markdown supported).

id: string

(Optional) ID for this record, unique among the owner's records of the same kind (e.g. a project's sublists). If omitted or invalid, Quire derives one from name; if already taken, Quire changes it by appending characters. Neither is an error, so read the id back from the response.

partner: string

(Optional) OID of the external team to share this record with; it is then shared with the members of the project and of that team, and is always private.

Only a project's record can carry one — an organization, a folder or a smart folder has no external team — and it must be one of the project's external teams; any other value is 400. It cannot be combined with members either (400).

An external team member shares a record with every member only through their own team: with members omitted or null, they must set partner to one of their teams. Otherwise 400 names their teams, as it does for a team of the project that isn't theirs.

Settable only when creating the record.

private: boolean

(Optional) Hide this record from guests and from the visitors of a public project or of a share link, like a custom field's private. A choice only when members is null and partner is null; defaults to false (everyone). Otherwise it is always true: a record shared with an external team, with selected members or with the admins only is hidden from them, so false is rejected with 400.

start: string

(Optional) Target start date: a date only, e.g. 2024-01-02; a value with a time of day returns 400.

due: string

(Optional) Target due date: a date only, e.g. 2024-05-25; a value with a time of day returns 400.

members: string[]

(Optional) Users who can see this record, and the only ones it is shown to. Each entry is a user ID, OID, or email, or "me" for the authenticated user.

  • Omit the field, or pass null — every member of the owner can see it, and so can guests and the visitors of a public project or of a share link unless private. This is the default. (A reminder differs: omitting its members means only the authenticated user.) An external team member must also set partner to one of their teams.
  • Pass [] — only the owner's admins can see it.
  • Pass a list — only those users can see it.

Rejected with 400 when:

  • a listed user is not a member of the owner. Unlike a task's assignees, which silently drops a non-member, this is an error: dropping the last one would leave [], which means something else entirely.
  • the list is non-empty and does not include the authenticated user — you would not be able to see what you just created.
  • partner is also set, since an external-team record is already shared with all members of the project and of the team.

Settable only when creating the record. It cannot be changed afterwards, so recreate the record to change who can see it.

Request Example
{
  "all": false,
  "includes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "description": "**Great** record to start with.",
  "iconColor": "37",
  "image": "icon-view-kanban",
  "name": "Highlight 101",
  "id": "Highlight101",
  "partner": "rcBHBYXZSiyDRrHrWPutatfF",
  "private": false,
  "start": "2024-01-02",
  "due": "2024-05-25",
  "members": "[\"me\", \"john\"]"
}
200 OK
Sublist

OK — created sublist record.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — body validation failed, for example a partner that isn't an external team of the project (or any, when the owner isn't a project), or none from an external team member sharing with every member.

402 Payment Required

Payment Required — sublist quota reached.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to create a sublist under this owner.

404 Not Found

Not Found — owner does not exist.

(Optional) Hide this record from guests and from the visitors of a public project or of a share link, like a custom field's private. A choice only when members is null and partner is null; defaults to false (everyone). Otherwise it is always true: a record shared with an external team, with selected members or with the admins only is hidden from them, so false is rejected with 400.

start: string

(Optional) Target start date: a date only, e.g. 2024-01-02; a value with a time of day returns 400.

due: string

(Optional) Target due date: a date only, e.g. 2024-05-25; a value with a time of day returns 400.

members: string[]

(Optional) Users who can see this record, and the only ones it is shown to. Each entry is a user ID, OID, or email, or "me" for the authenticated user.

  • Omit the field, or pass null — every member of the owner can see it, and so can guests and the visitors of a public project or of a share link unless private. This is the default. (A reminder differs: omitting its members means only the authenticated user.) An external team member must also set partner to one of their teams.
  • Pass [] — only the owner's admins can see it.
  • Pass a list — only those users can see it.

Rejected with 400 when:

  • a listed user is not a member of the owner. Unlike a task's assignees, which silently drops a non-member, this is an error: dropping the last one would leave [], which means something else entirely.
  • the list is non-empty and does not include the authenticated user — you would not be able to see what you just created.
  • partner is also set, since an external-team record is already shared with all members of the project and of the team.

Settable only when creating the record. It cannot be changed afterwards, so recreate the record to change who can see it.

Request Example
{
  "all": false,
  "includes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "description": "**Great** record to start with.",
  "iconColor": "37",
  "image": "icon-view-kanban",
  "name": "Highlight 101",
  "id": "Highlight101",
  "partner": "rcBHBYXZSiyDRrHrWPutatfF",
  "private": false,
  "start": "2024-01-02",
  "due": "2024-05-25",
  "members": "[\"me\", \"john\"]"
}
200 OK
Sublist

OK — created sublist record.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — body validation failed, for example a partner that isn't an external team of the project (or any, when the owner isn't a project), or none from an external team member sharing with every member.

402 Payment Required

Payment Required — sublist quota reached.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to create a sublist under this owner.

404 Not Found

Not Found — owner does not exist.

sublist

Update a sublist by ID.

PUT /sublist/id/{ownerType}/{ownerId}/{sublistId}

Updates an existing sublist and returns the complete updated record.

To archive or unarchive, set archived: true or archived: false in the body.

ownerType: string
in path

Owner type. One of project, organization, folder, or smart-folder. If omitted, project is assumed. For example, /id/my_project/1234 is equivalent to /id/project/my_project/1234.

ownerId: string
in path

ID of the owner.

sublistId: string
in path

ID of the sublist to update.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) returns the full sublist record; compact returns only {"oid": "…", "id": "…"}, which is cheaper — use it when you don't need the record back. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

start: string

(Optional) Target start date for this record: a date only, e.g. 2024-01-02; a value with a time of day returns 400.

due: string

(Optional) Target due date for this record: a date only, e.g. 2024-05-25; a value with a time of day returns 400.

changes: Change

(Optional) Tasks to add to or remove from this sublist, applied in order. Each item is {"task": "<task OID>", "exclude": false, "single": false}:

  • exclude: true removes the task instead of adding it.
  • single: true changes only the task itself; by default its subtasks follow it.

A task that doesn't exist is skipped. Example — add one task with its subtasks and leave another out:

[
  {"task": "2MmYOpJH_ZLeehIjjytH1Rwr"},
  {"task": "q8Rn1zX5bKcT0wGvJmLd3PaE", "exclude": true}
]
private: boolean

(Optional) Hide this record from guests and from the visitors of a public project or of a share link, like a custom field's private. A choice only when members is null and partner is null; otherwise it is always true, and false is rejected with 400.

description: string

(Optional) New description for this record (Markdown supported). An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

iconColor: string

(Optional) Icon color index from Quire's predefined palette. Two-digit code [0-5][0-7]: first digit 0-5, second digit 0-7 (e.g. 00, 37, 57). NOT a CSS hex color.

image: string icon-view-list, icon-view-kanban, icon-grid, icon-view-timeline, icon-calendar, icon-timer, icon-briefcase-o, icon-rocket-o, icon-bug-o, icon-user-o, icon-colleagues-o, icon-lightbulb-o, icon-leaf-o, icon-clapperboard, icon-sitemap-o, icon-list, icon-flash-on-o, icon-piggy-bank-o, icon-graduation-cap-o, icon-paper-plane-o, icon-globe-o, icon-music-o, icon-detail, icon-beach-o, icon-paper, icon-home-o, icon-building, icon-database-o, icon-microscope-o, icon-hamburger-o, icon-trophy-o, icon-thumbs-o-up, icon-thumbs-o-down, icon-smile-o, icon-frown-o, icon-meh-o, icon-bullseye, icon-incomplete, icon-filter-o, icon-comment, icon-view-insight, icon-view-dashboard, icon-square-dotted-o

(Optional) Icon image for this record, one of the listed values.

archived: boolean

(Optional) Archive toggle. Specify true to archive this record; specify false to unarchive.

name: string

(Optional) New display name for this record.

id: string

(Optional) New ID for this record, unique among the owner's records of the same kind. If invalid, Quire derives one from the name; if already taken, Quire changes it by appending characters. Neither is an error, so read the id back from the response.

Request Example
{
  "start": "2024-01-02",
  "due": "2024-05-25",
  "changes": "[{\"task\": \"2MmYOpJH_ZLeehIjjytH1Rwr\"}, {\"task\": \"q8Rn1zX5bKcT0wGvJmLd3PaE\", \"exclude\": true}]",
  "private": false,
  "description": "**Great** record to start with.",
  "iconColor": "37",
  "image": "icon-view-kanban",
  "archived": true,
  "name": "Highlight 101",
  "id": "Highlight101"
}
200 OK
Sublist

OK — updated sublist record.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — body validation failed.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to modify this sublist.

404 Not Found

Not Found — sublist does not exist.

Response Example (200 OK)

sublist

Update a sublist by OID.

PUT /sublist/{oid}

Updates an existing sublist and returns the complete updated record.

To archive or unarchive, set archived: true or archived: false in the body.

oid: string
in path

OID of the sublist to update.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) returns the full sublist record; compact returns only {"oid": "…", "id": "…"}, which is cheaper — use it when you don't need the record back. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

start: string

(Optional) Target start date for this record: a date only, e.g. 2024-01-02; a value with a time of day returns 400.

due: string

(Optional) Target due date for this record: a date only, e.g. 2024-05-25; a value with a time of day returns 400.

changes: Change

(Optional) Tasks to add to or remove from this sublist, applied in order. Each item is {"task": "<task OID>", "exclude": false, "single": false}:

  • exclude: true removes the task instead of adding it.
  • single: true changes only the task itself; by default its subtasks follow it.

A task that doesn't exist is skipped. Example — add one task with its subtasks and leave another out:

[
  {"task": "2MmYOpJH_ZLeehIjjytH1Rwr"},
  {"task": "q8Rn1zX5bKcT0wGvJmLd3PaE", "exclude": true}
]
private: boolean

(Optional) Hide this record from guests and from the visitors of a public project or of a share link, like a custom field's private. A choice only when members is null and partner is null; otherwise it is always true, and false is rejected with 400.

description: string

(Optional) New description for this record (Markdown supported). An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

iconColor: string

(Optional) Icon color index from Quire's predefined palette. Two-digit code [0-5][0-7]: first digit 0-5, second digit 0-7 (e.g. 00, 37, 57). NOT a CSS hex color.

image: string icon-view-list, icon-view-kanban, icon-grid, icon-view-timeline, icon-calendar, icon-timer, icon-briefcase-o, icon-rocket-o, icon-bug-o, icon-user-o, icon-colleagues-o, icon-lightbulb-o, icon-leaf-o, icon-clapperboard, icon-sitemap-o, icon-list, icon-flash-on-o, icon-piggy-bank-o, icon-graduation-cap-o, icon-paper-plane-o, icon-globe-o, icon-music-o, icon-detail, icon-beach-o, icon-paper, icon-home-o, icon-building, icon-database-o, icon-microscope-o, icon-hamburger-o, icon-trophy-o, icon-thumbs-o-up, icon-thumbs-o-down, icon-smile-o, icon-frown-o, icon-meh-o, icon-bullseye, icon-incomplete, icon-filter-o, icon-comment, icon-view-insight, icon-view-dashboard, icon-square-dotted-o

(Optional) Icon image for this record, one of the listed values.

archived: boolean

(Optional) Archive toggle. Specify true to archive this record; specify false to unarchive.

name: string

(Optional) New display name for this record.

id: string

(Optional) New ID for this record, unique among the owner's records of the same kind. If invalid, Quire derives one from the name; if already taken, Quire changes it by appending characters. Neither is an error, so read the id back from the response.

Request Example
{
  "start": "2024-01-02",
  "due": "2024-05-25",
  "changes": "[{\"task\": \"2MmYOpJH_ZLeehIjjytH1Rwr\"}, {\"task\": \"q8Rn1zX5bKcT0wGvJmLd3PaE\", \"exclude\": true}]",
  "private": false,
  "description": "**Great** record to start with.",
  "iconColor": "37",
  "image": "icon-view-kanban",
  "archived": true,
  "name": "Highlight 101",
  "id": "Highlight101"
}
200 OK
Sublist

OK — updated sublist record.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — body validation failed.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to modify this sublist.

404 Not Found

Not Found — sublist does not exist.

DELETE /sublist/id/{ownerType}/{ownerId}/{sublistId}

in path

ID of the owner.

tag

A tag is a label that can be attached to a task in Quire.

tag

Create a tag.

POST /tag/{projectOid}

Creates a new tag in the specified project and returns it. With global: true, the tag belongs to the project's organization and is available in all its projects; My Tasks (-) can't have one (403).

Requires a user who can manage the project's tags, and an app with the Manage tags permission; otherwise 403. Creating a global tag, or making a tag global, also takes the right to manage the organization's tags; updating or deleting a global tag takes only that right.

projectOid: string
in path

OID of the project to add the new tag to. Specify "-" to add it to personal tasks (My Tasks, not in a specific project).

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) for the full record, or compact for just {"oid": …}. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

color: string

(Optional) Tag color index from Quire’s predefined palette. If omitted, a color will be generated automatically. Two-digit code: first digit 0–5, second digit 0–7 (e.g., 35).

global: boolean

(Optional) Whether this tag is global (available in all projects of the project's organization). If omitted, the tag is not global. true requires the right to manage the organization's tags; otherwise 403.

name: string

Display name of the tag.

Request Example
{
  "color": "35",
  "global": true,
  "name": "Later"
}
200 OK
Tag

OK — newly created tag.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — body validation failed (e.g., name missing or too long).

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the user can't manage the tags, or the app lacks the Manage tags permission.

404 Not Found

Not Found — project does not exist.

Response Content-Types: application/json
Response Example (200 OK) 
{
  "global": true,
  "color": "35",
  "name": "Later",
  "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld",
  "project": {
    "url": "https://quire.io/u/my_id",
    "id": "my_id",
    "iconColor": "37",
    "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",

    "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"

task

Tasks are the basic units of work you and your team collaborate on.

task

Add a time log to a task by ID.

POST /task/add-timelog/id/{projectId}/{taskId}

Adds a time log to the task. The new log is credited to the authenticated caller unless user is supplied in the body.

Identity of a log is the triple (user, start, end). Sub-second precision in start / end is truncated to whole seconds.

On success returns the task's full timelogs array. If the project hides time logs from guests (its default), a guest member or a non-member gets an empty array, as timelogs is omitted from the task records they get. Example:

[
  {
    "start": "2026-04-26T09:00:00.000Z",
    "end": "2026-04-26T10:30:00.000Z",
    "billable": true,
    "note": "Pair-programming session",
    "user": { "oid": "u-123", "name": "John Doe" }
  }
]
projectId: string
in path

Project ID.

taskId: integer
in path

Task ID.

end: string

End timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC). Must be on or after start. Sub-second precision is truncated to whole seconds.

start: string

Start timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC). Sub-second precision is truncated to whole seconds.

user: string

(Optional) User identifier (OID, ID, or email) the log is credited to. Omitted, null, or empty defaults to the authenticated caller. Unknown users return 400 Bad Request.

billable: boolean

(Optional) Whether this log is billable. Omitted or null defaults to true.

note: string

(Optional) Free-form note for the log. Omitted, null, or empty stores no note.

Request Example
{
  "end": "2026-04-26T10:30:00Z",
  "start": "2026-04-26T09:00:00Z",
  "user": "john.doe@example.com",
  "billable": true,
  "note": "Pair-programming session"
}
200 OK
Timelog

OK — task's full timelogs array.

400 Bad Request
ErrorResponse

Bad Request — start / end missing or malformed, end precedes start, user is unknown, or a field has the wrong type.

403 Forbidden
ErrorResponse

Forbidden — the caller can't change this task's time logs (checked before the log is looked up).

404 Not Found
ErrorResponse

Not Found — task does not exist.

409 Conflict
ErrorResponse

Conflict — a log with the same (user, start, end) already exists; use PUT /task/update-timelog/... to amend it.

Response Content-Types: application/json
Response Example (200 OK) 
[
  {
    "start": "2023-02-20T00:00:00.000Z",
    "end": "2023-02-20T00:05:35.000Z",
    "user": {
      "url": "https://quire.io/u/my_id",
      "id": "my_id",
      "iconColor": "37",
      "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",
      "name": "Foo",
      "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
    },
    "billable": true,
    "note": "A piece of cake"
  }
]
Response Example (400 Bad Request) 
{
  "code": 429,
  "message": "Something went wrong."
}
Response Example (403 Forbidden) 
{
  "code": 429,
  "message": "Something went wrong."
}
Response Example (404 Not Found) 
{
  "code": 429,
  "message": "Something went wrong."
}
Response Example (409 Conflict) 
{
  "code": 429,
  "message": "Something went wrong."
}

task

Set or transition a task's approval state.

POST /task/approve/id/{projectId}/{taskId}

Sets the task's approval, or transitions it from its current state. The ?state= query parameter selects the transition:

  • request — request approval, or roll forward from approved / rejected / changes back to awaiting.
  • approve / reject / change — approver's decision.

The caller must be a claimer (for request) or an approver (for approve / reject / change) of the category. The original requester is preserved across approve / reject / change transitions.

Request body (optional). Supply a JSON object with a description field to post a companion comment on the task as a side effect of the approval call. Same shape as POST /comment: {"description": "<markdown>", "pinned": false, "asUser": false}. description is required when the body is supplied; pinned and asUser are optional.

The stored comment is a header, a blank line, then the supplied description. The header is a plain <category>: <status> line: the category's name, left out for the default category, then the status in the authorizing user's language (Awaiting approval, Approved, Rejected or Request changes in English). Don't parse it: its wording depends on the language. For example, {"description": "Please tweak the wording."} on a state=change call for the category legal, named Legal Review, stores Legal Review: Request changes\n\nPlease tweak the wording. Don't include the header in description yourself.

Without a body, approve / reject / change still log a comment holding only the header, as the apps do; request logs nothing. The created comment is not included in the response — call GET /comment/list/{taskOid} afterward to fetch it.

To cancel an approval, use DELETE /task/revoke-approval/id/{projectId}/{taskId} (or DELETE /task/revoke-approval/{oid}) — not this endpoint.

Returns 400 Bad Request if ?state= is missing or unknown, or the body has unknown fields, an empty description, or a non-object shape; 403 Forbidden if the caller isn't a claimer / approver; 404 Not Found if the task or ?category= doesn't exist.

Examples:

POST /task/approve/id/my_project/42?category=legal&state=approve
                  (empty body — records the approval and logs a header-only comment)
                  
                  POST /task/approve/id/my_project/42?category=legal&state=change
                  {"description": "Please tweak the wording."}
                  
                  POST /task/approve/iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo?state=request
                  (by OID — requests approval in the default category)
projectId: string
in path

Project ID.

taskId: integer
in path

Task ID.

state: string request, approve, reject, change
in query

Approval transition to apply: request requests approval (or rolls forward from a decided state back to awaiting); approve / reject / change records the approver's decision.

category: string
in query

(Optional) Approval category ID. Defaults to the project's default category (id "").

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) returns the task's approval record; compact returns only the task's {"oid": …, "id": …}. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

description: string

Content of the companion comment (Markdown supported). An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead. Required if the body is supplied. The server prepends a <category>: <status> line (status in the authorizing user's language; no category name for the default category) and a blank line before this text, so this field should contain only the human-written message — do not include the header yourself.

asUser: boolean

(Optional) If true, the comment is attributed to the app rather than the authorizing user ( app-as-user, as the asUser flag on POST /comment). Default: false. Either way, the authorizing user, not the app, follows the task, as for any comment.

pinned: boolean

(Optional) Whether to pin the companion comment on the task. Default: false.

Request Example
{
  "description": "Please tweak the wording.",
  "asUser": false,
  "pinned": false
}
200 OK

successful operation

task

Upload an attachment to a task by ID.

POST /task/attach/id/{projectId}/{taskId}/{filename}

Uploads an attachment to an existing task. The request body is the raw file content.

Executable files (.exe, .com, .bat) are rejected unless the project has enabled uploading executable files.

A file over the plan's per-file size limit, or one that would take the organization past its storage quota, is rejected with 402 (code 469).

projectId: string
in path

ID of the task's project. Specify "-" for personal tasks in My Tasks.

taskId: integer
in path

Task ID.

filename: string
in path

Attachment file name, e.g., readme.txt.

Percent-encode it, e.g., My%20Report.pdf for My Report.pdf. It can't contain / or \.

Provide a meaningful extension so the browser can recognize the MIME type (e.g., revenue.pdf, contacts.json).

Alternatively, set the MIME type via the Content-Type header.

Request Example
"object"
200 OK
SimpleAttachment

OK — newly created attachment.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — filename or payload invalid, or an executable file is not allowed for this project.

402 Payment Required

Payment Required (code 469) — the file is over the plan's per-file size limit, or the storage quota is used up.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to attach to this task.

404 Not Found

Not Found — task does not exist.

Response Content-Types: application/json
Response Example (200 OK) 
{
  "url": "https://quire.io/att/Ta/sdcQOGgeUtyaFFzb9p0IwAgi/qfqVmUtC/image.png",
  "length": 20000,
  "name": "file.txt"
}
