task

Bulk-add N root tasks to a project by ID.

POST /task/bulk-add/id/{projectId}

Creates up to 300 root tasks in one transaction.

Example: POST /task/bulk-add/id/my_project?return=compact

Body is a top-level JSON array of CreateTaskBody items (no envelope) — same shape as single-task POST /task/.... Items can include nested tasks to create subtrees in the same call; only the root of each item is echoed in the response (use GET /task/list/id/{projectId}/{rootId} to enumerate the created subtree).

Example request body:

[
  {
    "name": "Design new logo",
    "priority": 2,
    "tags": ["design"],
    "assignees": ["me"]
  },
  { "name": "Write spec", "due": "2026-05-10" },
  { "name": "Review" }
]

Example response (full mode, abbreviated):

[
  { "oid": "iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo", "id": 42, "name": "Design new logo", "priority": {"value": 2, "name": "Urgent"} },
  { "oid": "abcXyzPqRs",        "id": 43, "name": "Write spec" },
  { "oid": "defLmnQrSt",        "id": 44, "name": "Review" }
]

With ?return=compact, each element is just {oid, id}.

Submitted order is preserved, whatever ?position=: given [A, B, C], the tasks end up as A, B, C from top to bottom.

Atomic: a per-item validation, permission, or DB error rolls back the whole batch and returns {code, message} with an items[i]: prefix naming the offending item. Fix the value and retry. Example error:

{ "code": 400, "message": "items[1]: Invalid value for `priority`: 99 (expected -1, 0, 1, or 2 (or one of Low/Medium/High/Urgent))" }

Dry-run: pass ?dry-run=true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same per-item validation and permission checks as a real call; same response body shape on success and same {code, message} (with items[i]: prefix) on failure. A 200 from a dry-run is a strong signal that re-issuing the identical body without ?dry-run will succeed (subject to concurrent edits between the two calls). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

Caveat — returned identifiers are not stable: the oid and id values in a dry-run response are discarded along with everything else. A follow-up real call allocates fresh identifiers, so don't persist or reference dry-run OIDs / IDs across calls.

Rate-limit cost: 1 unit per item, charged upfront — for bulk-add, per task created, nested tasks included. ?dry-run=true costs ceil(N / 2) units (minimum 1). Skipped items are charged too. See Rate Limits.

Batch size: at most 300 items per call, and no more than the plan's per-minute rate limit — e.g. 50 on the Free plan, or 25 in a personal project on the Free plan (see Rate Limits). A batch over the plan's cap is rejected with 402 (code 469), one over 300 with 400; split it. Nested tasks count as items too, for both the cost and the batch size.

projectId: string
in path

Project ID. Specify - for your personal tasks (those in My Tasks that belong to no project).

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) gives each item's full task record; compact gives only {"oid": …, "id": …} per item. Recommended for large batches. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

dry-run: string true, false
in query

(Optional) Set to true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same validation, permissions, and response shape as a real call, at half the rate-limit cost (ceil(N / 2) units). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

Request Example
[
  {
    "description": "This is a *cool* task.",
    "tasks": [
      "#/definitions/CreateTaskBody"
    ],
    "tags": [
      "X6nmx9XjEO2wKbqeB1pRT43C"
    ],
    "partner": "UI design team",
    "recurrence": {
      "freq": "weekly",
      "interval": 1,
      "byweekday": "[1,3]",
      "byweekno": 2,
      "bydayno": 25,
      "bymonth": 10,
      "dupsubtasks": false,
      "sincelatest": true,
      "until": "2020-12-22"
    },
    "assignees": [
      "6QMKkEPBVWETLWrXqws94ALU"
    ],
    "asUser": true,
    "followers": [
      "tzufRLqCnud74dARyDSvjWDl"
    ],
    "successors": "[\"#13\"]",
    "start": "2026-05-01",
    "due": "2026-05-10T17:00Z",
    "yourField": "object",
    "peekaboo": true,
    "section": true,
    "milestone": true,
    "name": "Design new **logo**",
    "status": 0,
    "etc": 0,
    "priority": 0,
    "sourceRef": "{\"github\": {\"repo\": \"acme/web\", \"issue\": 42}, \"text\": \"Source: [GitHub issue 42](https://github.com/acme/web/issues/42)\"}"
  }

200 OK
Task

OK — array of created tasks (one per submitted item, root only for nested subtrees).

400 Bad Request
ErrorResponse

Bad Request — body not a JSON array, empty, over the 300-item cap, or any per-item validation failure (whole batch rolled back).

402 Payment Required
ErrorResponse

Payment Required (code 469) — the batch would exceed the plan's task limit, or holds more items than the plan allows per call (see Batch size).

403 Forbidden
ErrorResponse

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to add tasks to the project.

404 Not Found
ErrorResponse

Not Found — project does not exist.

413 Request Entity Too Large
ErrorResponse

Payload Too Large — body exceeds the API packet size limit.

429 Too Many Requests
ErrorResponse

Too Many Requests — the caller's per-minute / per-hour API quota is already used up (see Rate Limits).

Bulk-add N tasks relative to a task by ID.

POST /task/bulk-add/id/{projectId}/{taskId}

Creates up to 300 tasks anchored at the task identified by projectId + taskId. The optional ?position= query parameter mirrors single-task POST /task/... semantics:

  • parent (default): children of the anchor task.
  • before: siblings immediately before the anchor.
  • after: siblings immediately after the anchor.

Example: POST /task/bulk-add/id/my_project/42?position=after&return=compact

Request body:

[
  { "name": "Subtask 1" },
  { "name": "Subtask 2" },
  { "name": "Subtask 3" }
]

Response (compact mode):

[
  { "oid": "abc1", "id": 100 },
  { "oid": "abc2", "id": 101 },
  { "oid": "abc3", "id": 102 }
]

All three become siblings of task 42, in submitted order, immediately after task 42.

Body is a top-level JSON array of CreateTaskBody items (no envelope) — same shape as single-task POST /task/.... Items can include nested tasks to create subtrees in the same call; only the root of each item is echoed in the response (use GET /task/list/id/{projectId}/{rootId} to enumerate the created subtree).

Example request body:

[
  {
    "name": "Design new logo",
    "priority": 2,
    "tags": ["design"],
    "assignees": ["me"]
  },
  { "name": "Write spec", "due": "2026-05-10" },
  { "name": "Review" }
]

Example response (full mode, abbreviated):

[
  { "oid": "iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo", "id": 42, "name": "Design new logo", "priority": {"value": 2, "name": "Urgent"} },
  { "oid": "abcXyzPqRs",        "id": 43, "name": "Write spec" },
  { "oid": "defLmnQrSt",        "id": 44, "name": "Review" }
]

With ?return=compact, each element is just {oid, id}.

Submitted order is preserved, whatever ?position=: given [A, B, C], the tasks end up as A, B, C from top to bottom.

Atomic: a per-item validation, permission, or DB error rolls back the whole batch and returns {code, message} with an items[i]: prefix naming the offending item. Fix the value and retry. Example error:

{ "code": 400, "message": "items[1]: Invalid value for `priority`: 99 (expected -1, 0, 1, or 2 (or one of Low/Medium/High/Urgent))" }

Dry-run: pass ?dry-run=true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same per-item validation and permission checks as a real call; same response body shape on success and same {code, message} (with items[i]: prefix) on failure. A 200 from a dry-run is a strong signal that re-issuing the identical body without ?dry-run will succeed (subject to concurrent edits between the two calls). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

Caveat — returned identifiers are not stable: the oid and id values in a dry-run response are discarded along with everything else. A follow-up real call allocates fresh identifiers, so don't persist or reference dry-run OIDs / IDs across calls.

Rate-limit cost: 1 unit per item, charged upfront — for bulk-add, per task created, nested tasks included. ?dry-run=true costs ceil(N / 2) units (minimum 1). Skipped items are charged too. See Rate Limits.

Batch size: at most 300 items per call, and no more than the plan's per-minute rate limit — e.g. 50 on the Free plan, or 25 in a personal project on the Free plan (see Rate Limits). A batch over the plan's cap is rejected with 402 (code 469), one over 300 with 400; split it. Nested tasks count as items too, for both the cost and the batch size.

projectId: string
in path

Project ID. Specify - for your personal tasks (those in My Tasks that belong to no project).

taskId: integer
in path

Anchor task ID.

position: string parent, before, after
in query

(Optional) Placement of the new tasks relative to the anchor task: parent (default) makes them its children; before / after make them its siblings, immediately before / after it. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) gives each item's full task record; compact gives only {"oid": …, "id": …} per item. Recommended for large batches. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

dry-run: string true, false
in query

(Optional) Set to true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same validation, permissions, and response shape as a real call, at half the rate-limit cost (ceil(N / 2) units). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

    ],

task

Bulk-add N tasks by OID (project or task anchor).

POST /task/bulk-add/{oid}

Creates up to 300 tasks anchored at the entity identified by oid — a project OID creates root tasks, a task OID creates subtasks (or siblings, depending on ?position=).

Examples: POST /task/bulk-add/0Mg3VQ8kWeiVbLH1PrjzUc89?return=compact adds root tasks to that project; POST /task/bulk-add/iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo?position=after&return=compact adds them right after that task, in submitted order.

Body is a top-level JSON array of CreateTaskBody items (no envelope) — same shape as single-task POST /task/.... Items can include nested tasks to create subtrees in the same call; only the root of each item is echoed in the response (use GET /task/list/id/{projectId}/{rootId} to enumerate the created subtree).

Example request body:

[
  {
    "name": "Design new logo",
    "priority": 2,
    "tags": ["design"],
    "assignees": ["me"]
  },
  { "name": "Write spec", "due": "2026-05-10" },
  { "name": "Review" }
]

Example response (full mode, abbreviated):

[
  { "oid": "iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo", "id": 42, "name": "Design new logo", "priority": {"value": 2, "name": "Urgent"} },
  { "oid": "abcXyzPqRs",        "id": 43, "name": "Write spec" },
  { "oid": "defLmnQrSt",        "id": 44, "name": "Review" }
]

With ?return=compact, each element is just {oid, id}.

Submitted order is preserved, whatever ?position=: given [A, B, C], the tasks end up as A, B, C from top to bottom.

Atomic: a per-item validation, permission, or DB error rolls back the whole batch and returns {code, message} with an items[i]: prefix naming the offending item. Fix the value and retry. Example error:

{ "code": 400, "message": "items[1]: Invalid value for `priority`: 99 (expected -1, 0, 1, or 2 (or one of Low/Medium/High/Urgent))" }

Dry-run: pass ?dry-run=true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same per-item validation and permission checks as a real call; same response body shape on success and same {code, message} (with items[i]: prefix) on failure. A 200 from a dry-run is a strong signal that re-issuing the identical body without ?dry-run will succeed (subject to concurrent edits between the two calls). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

Caveat — returned identifiers are not stable: the oid and id values in a dry-run response are discarded along with everything else. A follow-up real call allocates fresh identifiers, so don't persist or reference dry-run OIDs / IDs across calls.

Rate-limit cost: 1 unit per item, charged upfront — for bulk-add, per task created, nested tasks included. ?dry-run=true costs ceil(N / 2) units (minimum 1). Skipped items are charged too. See Rate Limits.

Batch size: at most 300 items per call, and no more than the plan's per-minute rate limit — e.g. 50 on the Free plan, or 25 in a personal project on the Free plan (see Rate Limits). A batch over the plan's cap is rejected with 402 (code 469), one over 300 with 400; split it. Nested tasks count as items too, for both the cost and the batch size.

oid: string
in path

OID of the project (root tasks) or anchor task (subtasks / siblings, per ?position=). Specify - for your personal tasks (those in My Tasks that belong to no project).

position: string parent, before, after
in query

(Optional) Placement of the new tasks relative to the anchor task: parent (default) makes them its children; before / after make them its siblings, immediately before / after it. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request. With a project OID, only parent applies; before / after are rejected with 400.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) gives each item's full task record; compact gives only {"oid": …, "id": …} per item. Recommended for large batches. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

dry-run: string true, false
in query

(Optional) Set to true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same validation, permissions, and response shape as a real call, at half the rate-limit cost (ceil(N / 2) units). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

task

Bulk-approve N tasks in a project by ID.

POST /task/bulk-approve/id/{projectId}

Applies a single approval transition (request / approve / reject / change) to all tasks in the batch. Body is a top-level JSON array of task references (OID string, integer ID, or "#<id>" string; mixed forms allowed). Up to 300 items per call; see Batch size below.

Response: one slot per item, in order — the task's full record (with its approval), or {oid, id} with ?return=compact.

Permissions — same per-task role checks as the single-task POST /task/approve/...: the caller must be a claimer (for request) or an approver (for the others) of the category.

Comments — like the single-task endpoint, approve / reject / change log a comment on each task holding only a header; request logs nothing. There is no body field for comment text. The header is a plain <category>: <status> line: the category's name, left out for the default category, then the status in the authorizing user's language (Awaiting approval, Approved, Rejected or Request changes in English). Don't parse it: its wording depends on the language.

Atomic: a per-item validation, permission, or DB error rolls back the whole batch and returns {code, message} with an items[i]: prefix naming the offending item. Fix the value and retry. A per-item permission failure is such an error.

Skip-not-found: a ref that doesn't resolve to a live task in the project (already removed, never existed, a mistyped OID, cascade-removed by an earlier item, etc.) is skipped — its response slot is null and the rest of the batch proceeds. This makes the endpoint idempotent for agents — safe to re-submit after a partial network failure without diffing state first. Only a ref that is neither a string nor an integer is rejected with 400.

Dry-run: pass ?dry-run=true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same per-item validation and permission checks as a real call; same response body shape on success and same {code, message} (with items[i]: prefix) on failure. A 200 from a dry-run is a strong signal that re-issuing the identical body without ?dry-run will succeed (subject to concurrent edits between the two calls). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

Rate-limit cost: 1 unit per item, charged upfront — for bulk-add, per task created, nested tasks included. ?dry-run=true costs ceil(N / 2) units (minimum 1). Skipped items are charged too. See Rate Limits.

Batch size: at most 300 items per call, and no more than the plan's per-minute rate limit — e.g. 50 on the Free plan, or 25 in a personal project on the Free plan (see Rate Limits). A batch over the plan's cap is rejected with 402 (code 469), one over 300 with 400; split it.

Example:

POST /task/bulk-approve/id/my_project?category=legal&state=approve
Body: [42, "#43", "iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo"]
projectId: string
in path

Project ID.

state: string request, approve, reject, change
in query

Approval transition to apply: request requests approval (or rolls forward from a decided state back to awaiting); approve / reject / change records the approver's decision. Applied to every task in the batch.

category: string
in query

(Optional) Approval category ID. Defaults to the project's default category (id "").

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) gives each item's full task record; compact gives only {"oid": …, "id": …} per item. Recommended for large batches. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

dry-run: string true, false
in query

(Optional) Set to true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same validation, permissions, and response shape as a real call, at half the rate-limit cost (ceil(N / 2) units). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

Request Example
[
  "object"
]
200 OK
TaskWithParentInfo

OK — array of updated tasks (same length as the request body; null for skipped items whose task wasn't found).

400 Bad Request
ErrorResponse

Bad Request — body shape, missing or invalid ?state=, an item that is neither a string nor an integer, or a per-item validation error (with items[i]: prefix).

402 Payment Required
ErrorResponse

Payment Required (code 469) — the batch holds more items than the plan allows per call (see Batch size).

403 Forbidden
ErrorResponse

Forbidden — caller lacks claimer / approver role on at least one item (whole batch rolled back).

404 Not Found
ErrorResponse

Not Found — project or approval ?category= does not exist.

429 Too Many Requests
ErrorResponse

Too Many Requests — the caller's per-minute / per-hour API quota is already used up (see Rate Limits).

Applies a single approval transition (request / approve / reject / change) to all tasks in the batch. Body is a top-level JSON array of task references (OID string, integer ID, or "#<id>" string; mixed forms allowed). Up to 300 items per call; see Batch size below.

Response: one slot per item, in order — the task's full record (with its approval), or {oid, id} with ?return=compact.

Permissions — same per-task role checks as the single-task POST /task/approve/...: the caller must be a claimer (for request) or an approver (for the others) of the category.

Comments — like the single-task endpoint, approve / reject / change log a comment on each task holding only a header; request logs nothing. There is no body field for comment text. The header is a plain <category>: <status> line: the category's name, left out for the default category, then the status in the authorizing user's language (Awaiting approval, Approved, Rejected or Request changes in English). Don't parse it: its wording depends on the language.

Atomic: a per-item validation, permission, or DB error rolls back the whole batch and returns {code, message} with an items[i]: prefix naming the offending item. Fix the value and retry. A per-item permission failure is such an error.

Skip-not-found: a ref that doesn't resolve to a live task in the project (already removed, never existed, a mistyped OID, cascade-removed by an earlier item, etc.) is skipped — its response slot is null and the rest of the batch proceeds. This makes the endpoint idempotent for agents — safe to re-submit after a partial network failure without diffing state first. Only a ref that is neither a string nor an integer is rejected with 400.

Dry-run: pass ?dry-run=true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same per-item validation and permission checks as a real call; same response body shape on success and same {code, message} (with items[i]: prefix) on failure. A 200 from a dry-run is a strong signal that re-issuing the identical body without ?dry-run will succeed (subject to concurrent edits between the two calls). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

Rate-limit cost: 1 unit per item, charged upfront — for bulk-add, per task created, nested tasks included. ?dry-run=true costs ceil(N / 2) units (minimum 1). Skipped items are charged too. See Rate Limits.

Batch size: at most 300 items per call, and no more than the plan's per-minute rate limit — e.g. 50 on the Free plan, or 25 in a personal project on the Free plan (see Rate Limits). A batch over the plan's cap is rejected with 402 (code 469), one over 300 with 400; split it.

Example:

POST /task/bulk-approve/0Mg3VQ8kWeiVbLH1PrjzUc89?category=legal&state=approve
Body: [42, "#43", "iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo"]
projectOid: string
in path

Project OID.

state: string request, approve, reject, change
in query

Approval transition to apply: request requests approval (or rolls forward from a decided state back to awaiting); approve / reject / change records the approver's decision. Applied to every task in the batch.

category: string
in query

(Optional) Approval category ID. Defaults to the project's default category (id "").

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) gives each item's full task record; compact gives only {"oid": …, "id": …} per item. Recommended for large batches. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

dry-run: string true, false
in query

(Optional) Set to true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same validation, permissions, and response shape as a real call, at half the rate-limit cost (ceil(N / 2) units). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

Request Example
[
  "object"
]
200 OK
TaskWithParentInfo

OK — array of updated tasks (same length as the request body; null for skipped items whose task wasn't found).

400 Bad Request
ErrorResponse

Bad Request — body shape, missing or invalid ?state=, an item that is neither a string nor an integer, or a per-item validation error (with items[i]: prefix).

402 Payment Required
ErrorResponse

Payment Required (code 469) — the batch holds more items than the plan allows per call (see Batch size).

403 Forbidden
ErrorResponse

Forbidden — caller lacks claimer / approver role on at least one item (whole batch rolled back).

404 Not Found
ErrorResponse

Not Found — project or approval ?category= does not exist.

429 Too Many Requests
ErrorResponse

Too Many Requests — the caller's per-minute / per-hour API quota is already used up (see Rate Limits).

Response Content-Types: application/json

task

Add a new root task.

POST /task/id/{projectId}

Adds a new root task to a project.

Minimal request body only needs name. A fuller example:

{
  "name": "Design new logo",
  "description": "Needs to match the brand guide.",
  "priority": 2,
  "tags": ["design", "urgent"],
  "assignees": ["me"],
  "start": "2026-05-01",
  "due": "2026-05-10",
  "Priority": 3,
  "Owners": ["alice@example.com"]
}

Priority / Owners in this example are custom-field keys from the project's own /project/add-field definitions — they are not fixed API fields and are only recognised by name. See CreateTaskBody.yourField for the rules on each custom-field type.

Tags must exist already, as tags of the project or global tags of its organization; an unknown tag is rejected with 400, not created.

Nested tasks: subtasks created in the same call. Each one costs 1 rate-limit unit, like a separate call, and a call creates at most 300 tasks, nested ones included, and no more than the plan's per-minute rate limit — e.g. 50 on the Free plan, or 25 in a personal project on the Free plan (see Rate Limits). Over the plan's cap is rejected with 402 (code 469), over 300 with 400; split it.

projectId: string
in path

ID of the project to which this new task will be added. The task will be created as a root task. Specify "-" to add it to personal tasks (in My Tasks).

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape:

  • full (default): the full task record.
  • compact: only {"oid": …, "id": …} — the task's OID and ID. Saves payload, tokens, and a server-side reload; enough to chain follow-up calls.

Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

description: string

(Optional) A description of the task. An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

tasks: CreateTaskBody

(Optional) List of subtasks to create along with this task. Each one, at any depth, costs 1 rate-limit unit and counts toward the per-call cap of 300 tasks and the plan's per-minute limit; see Rate Limits.

tags: string[]

(Optional) A list of tag OIDs or names to be added to the new task. Tag names are case-insensitive. Each must be an existing tag of the project, or a global tag of its organization; an unknown tag is rejected with 400, not created.

partner: string

(Optional) The external team to share this task with: the name or OID of one of the project's external teams (GET /partner/list/id/{projectId} lists them). The team's members then get access to the task and its subtasks. Setting it takes the right to assign tasks (403 otherwise). A name or OID that matches no team, or a value that isn't a string, such as null, is rejected with 400.

recurrence: Recurrence

(Optional) Makes the task repeat. Omit it for a task that doesn't repeat.

  • freq (required): daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.
  • interval: a positive integer; 2 with weekly means every 2 weeks. Default: 1.
  • until: end date, e.g. 2026-12-31. Default: never ends.
  • weekly needs byweekday: the days of the week as a list, where 0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday, e.g. [0, 3].
  • monthly needs bydayno, the day of the month (1–31, or "last"), or byweekno, the week of the month (1–5, or "last"), with byweekday as a single day in that week, e.g. 1 for Tuesday. If both byweekno and bydayno are given, byweekno wins.
  • yearly needs bymonth, the month (1–12, 1 = January), plus what monthly needs.
  • dupsubtasks: whether to duplicate subtasks when the task is completed. Default: true.
  • sincelatest: with daily only, whether to repeat from the last completion date. Default: false.

A property that doesn't apply to freq is ignored; an invalid value, or a missing required one, is rejected with 400.

A recurring task always has a due. If due is omitted, it is derived from the recurrence: the nearest occurrence since today. The request is rejected if the derived due precedes start; specify due explicitly in that case.

assignees: string[]

(Optional) A list of user identifiers (OID, ID, or email) to assign this task to.

  • Use "me" to indicate the current user.
  • Use "inherit" to include all assignees of the parent task.

Only project members (external-team members included) can be assigned; anyone else is silently left out. An unknown user is rejected with 400.

asUser: boolean

(Optional) If true, marks this task as created by the app. Read asUser as app-as-user: the app itself is the user, not the authorizing user. Default: false (created by the authorizing user). In bulk-add, each item has its own. A nested task's asUser must match its top-level task's (a tree is created by one author); otherwise the call is rejected with 400.

followers: string[]

(Optional) List of user identifiers (OID, ID, or email) who follow this task. Only those listed, and anyone @mentioned in the description, follow it, so include "me" for the current user to follow.

  • Use "me" for the current user.
  • Use "inherit" to include followers of the parent task.
  • Use "app" for the application itself to follow (receive notifications).

For app followers, additional syntaxes are supported:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL (e.g., .../standard/soc1/33456/a7).
successors: string[]

(Optional) List of successor task identifiers (OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

start: string

(Optional) Start date/time in UTC.

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

Notes:

  • Seconds are not supported.
  • 2020-10-30T00:00:00 is treated as 2020-10-30 (date only).
  • To specify exactly midnight UTC, use 2020-10-30T00:00 (no seconds).
due: string

(Optional) Due date/time in UTC.

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

Notes:

  • Seconds are not supported.
  • 2020-10-30T00:00:00 is treated as 2020-10-30 (date only).
  • To specify exactly midnight UTC, use 2020-10-30T00:00 (no seconds).
yourField: object

PLACEHOLDER — do NOT send a key literally named yourField. Instead, use the custom field's own name (as defined via /project/add-field) as the JSON key, with a value matching the field's type:

  • Text / Email / Hyperlink: string.
  • Number / Money: numeric value (no currency symbol).
  • Checkbox: true or false.
  • Select: option name (string).
  • Date: ISO 8601 timestamp (yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssZ) or date-only (yyyy-MM-dd).
  • Duration: number of seconds.
  • User: user OID, user ID, or email — server resolves to the user's OID.
  • Task: task OID, integer task ID, or #<id> string — server resolves to the task's OID (scoped to this project).
  • File: the attachment list as a task returns it (absolute url accepted).
  • Multi-value (fields configured with multiple: true): provide a list.

Example body fragment: {"Priority": 3, "Owners": ["alice", "bob@example.com"], "Depends": ["#42"]}.

peekaboo:
boolean
integer

(Optional) Peekaboo setting. Accepts a boolean or a positive integer:

  • true: Hide indefinitely.
  • positive integer: Number of days to hide.
  • false: Cancel previous peekaboo.

Default: false.

section: boolean

(Optional) Whether this task is a section. Default: false.

milestone: boolean

(Optional) Whether this task is a milestone. Default: false.

name: string

The name of the task.

status: integer

(Optional) Task status. Must be one of the project's status values (GET /status/list/id/{projectId} lists them); any other value is rejected with 400. Every project has 0, the initial status, and 100, completed; 100 or more means completed. Default: 0.

etc: integer

(Optional) Estimated time to complete, in seconds: an integer from 0 to 864,000,000 (10,000 days). null is the same as leaving it out.

priority: integer -1, 0, 1, 2

(Optional) Task priority: -1 Low, 0 Medium, 1 High, 2 Urgent. (The server also accepts the case-insensitive English names Low, Medium, High, Urgent, but the integer form is recommended for typed callers.) Default: 0 (Medium).

sourceRef: object

(Optional) A JSON object your app stores with the task, such as where the task came from. Quire keeps it as is and returns it as sourceRef whenever the task is read.

  • text (optional): a Markdown string Quire shows as the task's source line in the task details. Include a link to the source, e.g. Source: [GitHub issue 42](https://github.com/acme/web/issues/42).
  • Any other key: your app's own data, not shown in Quire. Put it under a key named after your app, e.g. github, so it won't clash with another app's.
  • To find these tasks later, search with ?source-ref=github: it returns the tasks whose sourceRef has that key, whatever its value.
  • Size: at most about 2,048 characters, keys and values together, and text must be a string; otherwise 400.

200 OK
Task

OK — newly created task.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — body validation failed.

402 Payment Required

Payment Required (code 469) — the plan's task limit is reached, or the call creates more tasks than the plan allows per call (see Nested tasks).

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to add a task to this project.

404 Not Found

Not Found — project does not exist.

task

Add a new task relative to another task.

POST /task/id/{projectId}/{taskId}

Adds a new task under another task, or before or after another task. See POST /task/id/{projectId} for a full request-body example — the body shape is identical.

Nested tasks: subtasks created in the same call. Each one costs 1 rate-limit unit, like a separate call, and a call creates at most 300 tasks, nested ones included, and no more than the plan's per-minute rate limit — e.g. 50 on the Free plan, or 25 in a personal project on the Free plan (see Rate Limits). Over the plan's cap is rejected with 402 (code 469), over 300 with 400; split it.

projectId: string
in path

ID of the project to which the new task will be added. Specify "-" to add it to personal tasks in My Tasks.

taskId: integer
in path

ID of the referenced task.

position: string parent, before, after
in query

(Optional) Placement of the new task relative to the task referenced by taskId:

  • parent (default): child of the referenced task.
  • before: sibling immediately before the referenced task.
  • after: sibling immediately after the referenced task.

Omitted or empty → same as parent. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape:

  • full (default): the full task record.
  • compact: only {"oid": …, "id": …} — the task's OID and ID. Saves payload, tokens, and a server-side reload; enough to chain follow-up calls.

Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

description: string

(Optional) A description of the task. An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

tasks: CreateTaskBody

(Optional) List of subtasks to create along with this task. Each one, at any depth, costs 1 rate-limit unit and counts toward the per-call cap of 300 tasks and the plan's per-minute limit; see Rate Limits.

tags: string[]

(Optional) A list of tag OIDs or names to be added to the new task. Tag names are case-insensitive. Each must be an existing tag of the project, or a global tag of its organization; an unknown tag is rejected with 400, not created.

partner: string

(Optional) The external team to share this task with: the name or OID of one of the project's external teams (GET /partner/list/id/{projectId} lists them). The team's members then get access to the task and its subtasks. Setting it takes the right to assign tasks (403 otherwise). A name or OID that matches no team, or a value that isn't a string, such as null, is rejected with 400.

recurrence: Recurrence

(Optional) Makes the task repeat. Omit it for a task that doesn't repeat.

  • freq (required): daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.
  • interval: a positive integer; 2 with weekly means every 2 weeks. Default: 1.
  • until: end date, e.g. 2026-12-31. Default: never ends.
  • weekly needs byweekday: the days of the week as a list, where 0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday, e.g. [0, 3].
  • monthly needs bydayno, the day of the month (1–31, or "last"), or byweekno, the week of the month (1–5, or "last"), with byweekday as a single day in that week, e.g. 1 for Tuesday. If both byweekno and bydayno are given, byweekno wins.
  • yearly needs bymonth, the month (1–12, 1 = January), plus what monthly needs.
  • dupsubtasks: whether to duplicate subtasks when the task is completed. Default: true.
  • sincelatest: with daily only, whether to repeat from the last completion date. Default: false.

A property that doesn't apply to freq is ignored; an invalid value, or a missing required one, is rejected with 400.

A recurring task always has a due. If due is omitted, it is derived from the recurrence: the nearest occurrence since today. The request is rejected if the derived due precedes start; specify due explicitly in that case.

assignees: string[]

(Optional) A list of user identifiers (OID, ID, or email) to assign this task to.

  • Use "me" to indicate the current user.
  • Use "inherit" to include all assignees of the parent task.

Only project members (external-team members included) can be assigned; anyone else is silently left out. An unknown user is rejected with 400.

asUser: boolean

(Optional) If true, marks this task as created by the app. Read asUser as app-as-user: the app itself is the user, not the authorizing user. Default: false (created by the authorizing user). In bulk-add, each item has its own. A nested task's asUser must match its top-level task's (a tree is created by one author); otherwise the call is rejected with 400.

followers: string[]

(Optional) List of user identifiers (OID, ID, or email) who follow this task. Only those listed, and anyone @mentioned in the description, follow it, so include "me" for the current user to follow.

  • Use "me" for the current user.
  • Use "inherit" to include followers of the parent task.
  • Use "app" for the application itself to follow (receive notifications).

For app followers, additional syntaxes are supported:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL (e.g., .../standard/soc1/33456/a7).
successors: string[]

(Optional) List of successor task identifiers (OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

start: string

(Optional) Start date/time in UTC.

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

Notes:

  • Seconds are not supported.
  • 2020-10-30T00:00:00 is treated as 2020-10-30 (date only).
  • To specify exactly midnight UTC, use 2020-10-30T00:00 (no seconds).
due: string

(Optional) Due date/time in UTC.

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

Notes:

  • Seconds are not supported.
  • 2020-10-30T00:00:00 is treated as 2020-10-30 (date only).
  • To specify exactly midnight UTC, use 2020-10-30T00:00 (no seconds).
yourField: object

PLACEHOLDER — do NOT send a key literally named yourField. Instead, use the custom field's own name (as defined via /project/add-field) as the JSON key, with a value matching the field's type:

  • Text / Email / Hyperlink: string.
  • Number / Money: numeric value (no currency symbol).
  • Checkbox: true or false.
  • Select: option name (string).
  • Date: ISO 8601 timestamp (yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssZ) or date-only (yyyy-MM-dd).
  • Duration: number of seconds.
  • User: user OID, user ID, or email — server resolves to the user's OID.
  • Task: task OID, integer task ID, or #<id> string — server resolves to the task's OID (scoped to this project).
  • File: the attachment list as a task returns it (absolute url accepted).
  • Multi-value (fields configured with multiple: true): provide a list.

Example body fragment: {"Priority": 3, "Owners": ["alice", "bob@example.com"], "Depends": ["#42"]}.

peekaboo:
boolean
integer

(Optional) Peekaboo setting. Accepts a boolean or a positive integer:

  • true: Hide indefinitely.
  • positive integer: Number of days to hide.
  • false: Cancel previous peekaboo.

Default: false.

section: boolean

(Optional) Whether this task is a section. Default: false.

milestone: boolean

(Optional) Whether this task is a milestone. Default: false.

name: string

The name of the task.

status: integer

(Optional) Task status. Must be one of the project's status values (GET /status/list/id/{projectId} lists them); any other value is rejected with 400. Every project has 0, the initial status, and 100, completed; 100 or more means completed. Default: 0.

etc: integer

(Optional) Estimated time to complete, in seconds: an integer from 0 to 864,000,000 (10,000 days). null is the same as leaving it out.

priority: integer -1, 0, 1, 2

(Optional) Task priority: -1 Low, 0 Medium, 1 High, 2 Urgent. (The server also accepts the case-insensitive English names Low, Medium, High, Urgent, but the integer form is recommended for typed callers.) Default: 0 (Medium).

sourceRef: object

(Optional) A JSON object your app stores with the task, such as where the task came from. Quire keeps it as is and returns it as sourceRef whenever the task is read.

  • text (optional): a Markdown string Quire shows as the task's source line in the task details. Include a link to the source, e.g. Source: [GitHub issue 42](https://github.com/acme/web/issues/42).
  • Any other key: your app's own data, not shown in Quire. Put it under a key named after your app, e.g. github, so it won't clash with another app's.
  • To find these tasks later, search with ?source-ref=github: it returns the tasks whose sourceRef has that key, whatever its value.
  • Size: at most about 2,048 characters, keys and values together, and text must be a string; otherwise 400.

task

Add a new root task, or relative to another task.

POST /task/{oid}

Adds a new task to a project, under another task, or before or after another task.

Nested tasks: subtasks created in the same call. Each one costs 1 rate-limit unit, like a separate call, and a call creates at most 300 tasks, nested ones included, and no more than the plan's per-minute rate limit — e.g. 50 on the Free plan, or 25 in a personal project on the Free plan (see Rate Limits). Over the plan's cap is rejected with 402 (code 469), over 300 with 400; split it.

oid: string
in path

OID of the project or task to which the new task will be added. If the OID refers to a project, the new task becomes a root task. If it refers to a task, the new task becomes its subtask. Specify - for your personal tasks (those in My Tasks that belong to no project).

position: string parent, before, after
in query

(Optional) Placement of the new task relative to the task referenced by oid:

  • parent (default): child of the referenced task.
  • before: sibling immediately before the referenced task.
  • after: sibling immediately after the referenced task.

Omitted or empty → same as parent. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request, and so do before / after when oid refers to a project.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape:

  • full (default): the full task record.
  • compact: only {"oid": …, "id": …} — the task's OID and ID. Saves payload, tokens, and a server-side reload; enough to chain follow-up calls.

Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

description: string

(Optional) A description of the task. An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

tasks: CreateTaskBody

(Optional) List of subtasks to create along with this task. Each one, at any depth, costs 1 rate-limit unit and counts toward the per-call cap of 300 tasks and the plan's per-minute limit; see Rate Limits.

tags: string[]

(Optional) A list of tag OIDs or names to be added to the new task. Tag names are case-insensitive. Each must be an existing tag of the project, or a global tag of its organization; an unknown tag is rejected with 400, not created.

partner: string

(Optional) The external team to share this task with: the name or OID of one of the project's external teams (GET /partner/list/id/{projectId} lists them). The team's members then get access to the task and its subtasks. Setting it takes the right to assign tasks (403 otherwise). A name or OID that matches no team, or a value that isn't a string, such as null, is rejected with 400.

recurrence: Recurrence

(Optional) Makes the task repeat. Omit it for a task that doesn't repeat.

  • freq (required): daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.
  • interval: a positive integer; 2 with weekly means every 2 weeks. Default: 1.
  • until: end date, e.g. 2026-12-31. Default: never ends.
  • weekly needs byweekday: the days of the week as a list, where 0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday, e.g. [0, 3].
  • monthly needs bydayno, the day of the month (1–31, or "last"), or byweekno, the week of the month (1–5, or "last"), with byweekday as a single day in that week, e.g. 1 for Tuesday. If both byweekno and bydayno are given, byweekno wins.
  • yearly needs bymonth, the month (1–12, 1 = January), plus what monthly needs.
  • dupsubtasks: whether to duplicate subtasks when the task is completed. Default: true.
  • sincelatest: with daily only, whether to repeat from the last completion date. Default: false.

A property that doesn't apply to freq is ignored; an invalid value, or a missing required one, is rejected with 400.

A recurring task always has a due. If due is omitted, it is derived from the recurrence: the nearest occurrence since today. The request is rejected if the derived due precedes start; specify due explicitly in that case.

assignees: string[]

(Optional) A list of user identifiers (OID, ID, or email) to assign this task to.

  • Use "me" to indicate the current user.
  • Use "inherit" to include all assignees of the parent task.

Only project members (external-team members included) can be assigned; anyone else is silently left out. An unknown user is rejected with 400.

asUser: boolean

(Optional) If true, marks this task as created by the app. Read asUser as app-as-user: the app itself is the user, not the authorizing user. Default: false (created by the authorizing user). In bulk-add, each item has its own. A nested task's asUser must match its top-level task's (a tree is created by one author); otherwise the call is rejected with 400.

followers: string[]

(Optional) List of user identifiers (OID, ID, or email) who follow this task. Only those listed, and anyone @mentioned in the description, follow it, so include "me" for the current user to follow.

  • Use "me" for the current user.
  • Use "inherit" to include followers of the parent task.
  • Use "app" for the application itself to follow (receive notifications).

For app followers, additional syntaxes are supported:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL (e.g., .../standard/soc1/33456/a7).
successors: string[]

(Optional) List of successor task identifiers (OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

start: string

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

task

Search tasks in a folder by folder ID.

GET /task/search-folder/id/{folderId}

Returns tasks that match the specified criteria in the given folder, most recently edited first (best match first with text). Tasks in archived projects are excluded. Pass at least one query parameter; none is rejected with 400. Custom-field filters and sublist aren't supported here (400); search a project for those.

Available for Professional plans and above; on the Free plan it is rejected with 402 (code 469).

Pagination: a page holds up to ?limit= tasks (30 by default). When more matches remain, the page's last item carries a cursor; pass it back as ?cursor= with the same ?limit= and filters for the next page, until a page's last item has none. The token is opaque — use it verbatim. Paging reaches at most 1,000,000 rows deep; a deeper cursor is rejected with 400 — narrow the search with filters instead.

Rate-limit cost: max(1, ceil(N / 100)) units, where N is the number of tasks returned — e.g. 1 for a page of 100 or fewer, 10 for 1,000. See Rate Limits.

folderId: string
in path

Folder ID.

text: string
in query

Full-text query against task name, description, attachments, and the values of the custom fields you can view. At most 256 characters. Note: does not include comment content or comment attachments. Indexing can take ~10 seconds or more after updates.

name: string
in query

Task name filter, matched against the name's Markdown source. A bare value matches the whole name exactly (case-sensitive). Prefix with ~ for a regex, ~* for a case-insensitive regex; an invalid regex is rejected with 400. At most 256 characters. Use text for full-text search.

description: string
in query

Task description filter, matched against the description's Markdown source. A bare value matches the whole description exactly (case-sensitive). Prefix with ~ for a regex, ~* for a case-insensitive regex; an invalid regex is rejected with 400. At most 256 characters.

status: string
in query

Task status filter: active (not completed), completed, or an integer 0..100 for that status, where 100 matches every completed status, like completed. Any other value returns 400.

scheduled: boolean
in query

Return only scheduled tasks (start or due is set). If scheduled=false, returns only tasks where neither start nor due is set.

mine: boolean
in query

Return only "My Tasks" (assigned to me, or created by me and scheduled but unassigned).

assignee: string
in query

Filter by assignee. Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email.

Combine values with , (AND), | (OR), and ! (NOT). AND binds tighter than OR.

Examples:

  • alice — a single user (by ID)
  • alice@example.com — by email
  • alice,bob — assigned to both
  • alice|bob — assigned to either
  • alice,!bob — assigned to alice but not bob
  • alice,bob|carol — (alice AND bob) OR carol
assignor: string
in query

Filter by assignor (the user who set the assignment). Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email. Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT); AND binds tighter than OR.

Examples: alice, alice,!bob, alice|bob.

follower: string
in query

Filter by follower. Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email. Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT); AND binds tighter than OR.

Examples: alice, alice,!bob, alice|bob.

tag: string
in query

Filter by tag. Each value is a tag OID or a tag name (names are resolved within the search's organization).

Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT); AND binds tighter than OR.

Names containing ,, |, !, ", or whitespace must be wrapped in "...". Inside quotes, write \" for a literal " and \\ for a literal \; any other \x is preserved as two literal characters.

Examples:

  • Legal — a single tag
  • Legal,!Draft — has Legal but not Draft
  • "In Progress",!Done — quoted name with space
  • "Foo\"s Go"|Other — quoted with escaped "
modified: string
in query

Return only tasks created or modified within the given period: a number of days (7), or a number with the suffix d (days), h (hours), or m (minutes), e.g. 8h. An empty value means 7 days; false turns the filter off.

commented: string
in query

Return only tasks commented on within the given period: a number of days (7), or a number with the suffix d (days), h (hours), or m (minutes), e.g. 8h. An empty value means 7 days; false turns the filter off.

source-ref: string
in query

Return only tasks whose sourceRef has this key, whatever its value: github finds the tasks created with "sourceRef": {"github": {"repo": "acme/web", "issue": 42}}. sourceRef is a JSON object an app stores when it creates or updates a task: its own data under a key named after the app, plus an optional text that Quire shows as the task's source line. This parameter's former name, sourceRef, still works.

created: string
in query

Filter by the task's createdAt timestamp. Value grammar:

  • Keyword: past, yesterday, today, tomorrow, upcoming, last7d, next7d, lastWeek, thisWeek, nextWeek
  • Value op: {ge|gt|le|lt|eq|ne}:<timestamp> or {between|notBetween}:<timestamp>,<timestamp>
  • <timestamp> is ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (UTC); a date-only operand such as 2026-04-01 is rejected with 400
  • isNull / isNotNull are rejected with 400, since createdAt is never null
  • Day boundaries resolve in the caller's timezone; week start follows the caller's locale
  • past on this field is < now()
  • Tokens and keywords are case-insensitive

Examples: today, last7d, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z, between:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z,2026-04-30T23:59:59Z.

edited: string
in query

Filter by the task's editedAt timestamp. Same grammar as created, timestamps only, and isNull / isNotNull are rejected with 400. Note: editedAt is NULL for tasks that have never been edited after creation; such tasks are excluded by every op (use created to filter by creation time).

Examples: today, last7d, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z.

archived: string
in query

Filter by the task's archivedAt timestamp. Same grammar as created (timestamps only), plus null ops since the field is nullable:

  • isNull — not archived
  • isNotNull — archived (any time)

Examples: isNotNull, today, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z.

unarchived: string
in query

Filter by the task's reshowAt timestamp (scheduled un-archive). Same grammar as archived (timestamps only; supports isNull / isNotNull).

Examples: isNotNull, today, between:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z,2026-04-30T23:59:59Z.

toggled: string
in query

Filter by the task's toggledAt timestamp (when its completion status was last changed). Same grammar as archived (timestamps only; supports isNull / isNotNull).

Examples: today, isNotNull, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z.

start: string
in query

Filter by the task's start date/time. Value grammar:

  • Keyword: past, yesterday, today, tomorrow, upcoming, last7d, next7d, lastWeek, thisWeek, nextWeek
  • Value op: {ge|gt|le|lt|eq|ne}:<value> or {between|notBetween}:<value>,<value>
  • Null op: isNull, isNotNull
  • <value> is either a date (YYYY-MM-DD) or a full ISO 8601 timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ)
  • A date operand expands to a whole-day window in the caller's timezone (ge:2026-04-01 means "on or after Apr 1 in the caller's calendar"); gt:D/le:D use end-of-day, lt:D/ge:D use start-of-day
  • past on start/due is < today 00:00 in the caller's timezone (not < now())
  • upcoming on start/due is the window [tomorrow, today + 7 days)

Examples: today, upcoming, ge:2026-04-01, between:2026-04-01,2026-04-30, isNull.

due: string
in query

Filter by the task's due date/time. Same grammar and semantics as start (accepts date-only operands, isNull/isNotNull, and the same keyword/value ops).

Examples: today, upcoming, le:2026-04-30, isNotNull.

priority: string
in query

Filter by task priority. Each value is an integer (-1..2) or a label (low, medium, high, urgent; case-insensitive): -1 Low, 0 Medium, 1 High, 2 Urgent. Any other value, such as none, is rejected with 400.

Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT). AND of two distinct positives is the empty set (a task has exactly one priority); negation works as expected.

Examples: high, 1, high|urgent, !low.

type: string
in query

Filter by task type. Values: normal (or task), section, milestone. Combine with , / | / !. Useful for structural navigation (e.g., listing only sections in a project).

Examples: section, section|milestone, !section.

created-by: string
in query

Filter by the user who created the task. Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email. Combine with , / | / ! (same grammar as assignee). This parameter's former name, createdBy, still works.

Examples: alice, alice|bob, !alice.

recurring: string
in query

Filter on whether the task has a recurrence configured. true (or empty) returns only recurring tasks; false returns only non-recurring tasks. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

limit: string
in query

Maximum number of tasks per page. Default: 30. Use no to return all matches.

On the Free plan, a limit over 30, or no, is rejected with 402 (code 469).

cursor: string
in query

Continuation token from the previous page's last item. See Pagination in the operation notes for the loop. At most 1,000,000 rows deep.

200 OK
TaskWithProjectParentInfo

OK — matching tasks (may be empty). When more matches remain, the last item carries a cursor field.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — no query parameter, or an invalid or unknown one (incl. a custom field, sublist, or a malformed or too deep cursor).

402 Payment Required

Payment Required (code 469) — the organization is on the Free plan.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to search this folder.

404 Not Found

Not Found — folder does not exist.

task

Search tasks in a folder by folder OID.

GET /task/search-folder/{folderOid}

Returns tasks that match the specified criteria in the given folder, most recently edited first (best match first with text). Tasks in archived projects are excluded. Pass at least one query parameter; none is rejected with 400. Custom-field filters and sublist aren't supported here (400); search a project for those.

Available for Professional plans and above; on the Free plan it is rejected with 402 (code 469).

Pagination: a page holds up to ?limit= tasks (30 by default). When more matches remain, the page's last item carries a cursor; pass it back as ?cursor= with the same ?limit= and filters for the next page, until a page's last item has none. The token is opaque — use it verbatim. Paging reaches at most 1,000,000 rows deep; a deeper cursor is rejected with 400 — narrow the search with filters instead.

Rate-limit cost: max(1, ceil(N / 100)) units, where N is the number of tasks returned — e.g. 1 for a page of 100 or fewer, 10 for 1,000. See Rate Limits.

See also the by-ID form GET /task/search-folder/id/{folderId}.

task

Search tasks in an organization by organization ID.

GET /task/search-organization/id/{organizationId}

Returns tasks that match the specified criteria in the given organization, most recently edited first (best match first with text). Tasks in archived projects are excluded. Pass at least one query parameter; none is rejected with 400. Custom-field filters and sublist aren't supported here (400); search a project for those.

Available for Professional plans and above; on the Free plan it is rejected with 402 (code 469).

Pagination: a page holds up to ?limit= tasks (30 by default). When more matches remain, the page's last item carries a cursor; pass it back as ?cursor= with the same ?limit= and filters for the next page, until a page's last item has none. The token is opaque — use it verbatim. Paging reaches at most 1,000,000 rows deep; a deeper cursor is rejected with 400 — narrow the search with filters instead.

Rate-limit cost: max(1, ceil(N / 100)) units, where N is the number of tasks returned — e.g. 1 for a page of 100 or fewer, 10 for 1,000. See Rate Limits.

organizationId: string
in path

Organization ID.

text: string
in query

Full-text query against task name, description, attachments, and the values of the custom fields you can view. At most 256 characters. Note: does not include comment content or comment attachments. Indexing can take ~10 seconds or more after updates.

name: string
in query

Task name filter, matched against the name's Markdown source. A bare value matches the whole name exactly (case-sensitive). Prefix with ~ for a regex, ~* for a case-insensitive regex; an invalid regex is rejected with 400. At most 256 characters. Use text for full-text search.

description: string
in query

Task description filter, matched against the description's Markdown source. A bare value matches the whole description exactly (case-sensitive). Prefix with ~ for a regex, ~* for a case-insensitive regex; an invalid regex is rejected with 400. At most 256 characters.

status: string
in query

Task status filter: active (not completed), completed, or an integer 0..100 for that status, where 100 matches every completed status, like completed. Any other value returns 400.

scheduled: boolean
in query

Return only scheduled tasks (start or due is set). If scheduled=false, returns only tasks where neither start nor due is set.

mine: boolean
in query

Return only "My Tasks" (assigned to me, or created by me and scheduled but unassigned).

assignee: string
in query

Filter by assignee. Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email.

Combine values with , (AND), | (OR), and ! (NOT). AND binds tighter than OR.

Examples:

  • alice — a single user (by ID)
  • alice@example.com — by email
  • alice,bob — assigned to both
  • alice|bob — assigned to either
  • alice,!bob — assigned to alice but not bob
  • alice,bob|carol — (alice AND bob) OR carol
assignor: string
in query

Filter by assignor (the user who set the assignment). Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email. Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT); AND binds tighter than OR.

Examples: alice, alice,!bob, alice|bob.

follower: string
in query

Filter by follower. Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email. Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT); AND binds tighter than OR.

Examples: alice, alice,!bob, alice|bob.

tag: string
in query

Filter by tag. Each value is a tag OID or a tag name (names are resolved within the search's organization).

Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT); AND binds tighter than OR.

Names containing ,, |, !, ", or whitespace must be wrapped in "...". Inside quotes, write \" for a literal " and \\ for a literal \; any other \x is preserved as two literal characters.

Examples:

  • Legal — a single tag
  • Legal,!Draft — has Legal but not Draft
  • "In Progress",!Done — quoted name with space
  • "Foo\"s Go"|Other — quoted with escaped "
modified: string
in query

Return only tasks created or modified within the given period: a number of days (7), or a number with the suffix d (days), h (hours), or m (minutes), e.g. 8h. An empty value means 7 days; false turns the filter off.

commented: string
in query

Return only tasks commented on within the given period: a number of days (7), or a number with the suffix d (days), h (hours), or m (minutes), e.g. 8h. An empty value means 7 days; false turns the filter off.

source-ref: string
in query

Return only tasks whose sourceRef has this key, whatever its value: github finds the tasks created with "sourceRef": {"github": {"repo": "acme/web", "issue": 42}}. sourceRef is a JSON object an app stores when it creates or updates a task: its own data under a key named after the app, plus an optional text that Quire shows as the task's source line. This parameter's former name, sourceRef, still works.

created: string
in query

Filter by the task's createdAt timestamp. Value grammar:

  • Keyword: past, yesterday, today, tomorrow, upcoming, last7d, next7d, lastWeek, thisWeek, nextWeek
  • Value op: {ge|gt|le|lt|eq|ne}:<timestamp> or {between|notBetween}:<timestamp>,<timestamp>
  • <timestamp> is ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (UTC); a date-only operand such as 2026-04-01 is rejected with 400
  • isNull / isNotNull are rejected with 400, since createdAt is never null
  • Day boundaries resolve in the caller's timezone; week start follows the caller's locale
  • past on this field is < now()
  • Tokens and keywords are case-insensitive

Examples: today, last7d, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z, between:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z,2026-04-30T23:59:59Z.

edited: string
in query

Filter by the task's editedAt timestamp. Same grammar as created, timestamps only, and isNull / isNotNull are rejected with 400. Note: editedAt is NULL for tasks that have never been edited after creation; such tasks are excluded by every op (use created to filter by creation time).

Examples: today, last7d, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z.

archived: string
in query

Filter by the task's archivedAt timestamp. Same grammar as created (timestamps only), plus null ops since the field is nullable:

  • isNull — not archived
  • isNotNull — archived (any time)

Examples: isNotNull, today, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z.

unarchived: string
in query

Filter by the task's reshowAt timestamp (scheduled un-archive). Same grammar as archived (timestamps only; supports isNull / isNotNull).

Examples: isNotNull, today, between:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z,2026-04-30T23:59:59Z.

toggled: string
in query

Filter by the task's toggledAt timestamp (when its completion status was last changed). Same grammar as archived (timestamps only; supports isNull / isNotNull).

Examples: today, isNotNull, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z.

start: string
in query

Filter by the task's start date/time. Value grammar:

  • Keyword: past, yesterday, today, tomorrow, upcoming, last7d, next7d, lastWeek, thisWeek, nextWeek
  • Value op: {ge|gt|le|lt|eq|ne}:<value> or {between|notBetween}:<value>,<value>
  • Null op: isNull, isNotNull
  • <value> is either a date (YYYY-MM-DD) or a full ISO 8601 timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ)
  • A date operand expands to a whole-day window in the caller's timezone (ge:2026-04-01 means "on or after Apr 1 in the caller's calendar"); gt:D/le:D use end-of-day, lt:D/ge:D use start-of-day
  • past on start/due is < today 00:00 in the caller's timezone (not < now())
  • upcoming on start/due is the window [tomorrow, today + 7 days)

Examples: today, upcoming, ge:2026-04-01, between:2026-04-01,2026-04-30, isNull.

due: string
in query

Filter by the task's due date/time. Same grammar and semantics as start (accepts date-only operands, isNull/isNotNull, and the same keyword/value ops).

Examples: today, upcoming, le:2026-04-30, isNotNull.

priority: string
in query

Filter by task priority. Each value is an integer (-1..2) or a label (low, medium, high, urgent; case-insensitive): -1 Low, 0 Medium, 1 High, 2 Urgent. Any other value, such as none, is rejected with 400.

Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT). AND of two distinct positives is the empty set (a task has exactly one priority); negation works as expected.

Examples: high, 1, high|urgent, !low.

type: string
in query

Filter by task type. Values: normal (or task), section, milestone. Combine with , / | / !. Useful for structural navigation (e.g., listing only sections in a project).

Examples: section, section|milestone, !section.

created-by: string
in query

Filter by the user who created the task. Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email. Combine with , / | / ! (same grammar as assignee). This parameter's former name, createdBy, still works.

Examples: alice, alice|bob, !alice.

recurring: string
in query

Filter on whether the task has a recurrence configured. true (or empty) returns only recurring tasks; false returns only non-recurring tasks. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

limit: string
in query

Maximum number of tasks per page. Default: 30. Use no to return all matches.

On the Free plan, a limit over 30, or no, is rejected with 402 (code 469).

cursor: string
in query

Continuation token from the previous page's last item. See Pagination in the operation notes for the loop. At most 1,000,000 rows deep.

200 OK
TaskWithProjectParentInfo

OK — matching tasks (may be empty). When more matches remain, the last item carries a cursor field.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — no query parameter, or an invalid or unknown one (incl. a custom field, sublist, or a malformed or too deep cursor).

402 Payment Required

Payment Required (code 469) — the organization is on the Free plan.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to search this organization.

404 Not Found

Not Found — organization does not exist.

task

Get all root tasks of the given project.

GET /task/list/id/{projectId}

Returns all root tasks of the project as a bare JSON array.

Pagination is opt-in via ?limit=N (1..1000). Without ?limit= or ?cursor=, the response is the full bare array. When ?limit=N is set and more results exist, the LAST item carries "cursor": "<token>" — pass it back as ?cursor=<token> (plus the same ?limit= and any filter like ?status=) to fetch the next page. End of stream is signalled by the absence of cursor on the last item. ?limit=no is an explicit "return everything". Same pagination grammar applies to the subtasks endpoint GET /task/list/id/{projectId}/{taskId}.

Pair with ?return=compact to render each item as {oid, id, cursor?} for navigation/lookup workloads at minimal token cost.

Rate-limit cost: max(1, ceil(N / 100)) units, where N is the number of tasks returned. See Rate Limits.

?depth= isn't available here: only 1, the default, is accepted. To walk a subtree, list a task's subtasks with GET /task/list/id/{projectId}/{taskId}?depth=…. To retrieve all tasks (including all subtasks), use the search API.

projectId: string
in path

ID of the task's project. Specify "-" for personal tasks in My Tasks.

status: string
in query

Task status filter. Specify a status value (an integer 0..100; 100 matches every completed status), or use "active" for active tasks or "completed" for completed tasks. Any other value returns 400.

limit: string
in query

Page size (1..1000). Omit for the default unpaginated full list, or pass no to be explicit. When set and more results exist, the last item in the response carries a cursor field.

cursor: string
in query

Continuation token. Pass back the cursor value from the last item of the previous page to fetch the next page. Re-pass any filter (?status=) and ?limit= on the same call.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) for the standard task records, or compact for identifier-only items, {oid, id, cursor?}. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

200 OK
Task

OK — bare array of root tasks (may be empty). With ?limit=N, the last item may carry a cursor field if more results exist.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — invalid ?status= / ?limit= / ?return= value, ?depth= other than 1, or ?cursor= doesn't belong to this list.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the user can't access it, or didn't authorize it for this app.

404 Not Found

Not Found — project does not exist.

task

Get the subtasks of the given task.

GET /task/list/id/{projectId}/{taskId}

By default returns only the direct subtasks of {taskId} (one level). To fetch a whole subtree in a single call, set ?depth=N or ?depth=full — each task in the response then carries a nested tasks field with its walked children, recursively.

When to use which:

  • Default (no ?depth): you only need the immediate children.
  • ?depth=2 or 3: small subtree where you know the shape.
  • ?depth=full: full subtree snapshot — pair with ?return=compact for navigation/lookup workloads to keep the payload (and LLM-token cost) small.

Per-tier total-nodes cap when ?depth>1: Free → rejected (402), Pro → 500, Premium → 2,000, Enterprise → unlimited (bounded only by the global response-size ceiling). When the cap fires mid-walk, the partial subtree is returned and the last emitted sibling at the cropped level carries "cropped": true. Recovery: list that sibling's parent again without ?depth to fetch the rest of that level — flat single-level lists have no cap.

Tree shape signals for the agent:

  • Node has a tasks array → its children were walked. Empty array means a true leaf.
  • Node has no tasks field → its children were not walked (depth limit reached, or cap fired before reaching it). Drill in if you need them.
  • Node has "cropped": true → more siblings of this node exist at the same level.

?status= with ?depth>1: a task that doesn't match is left out with its whole subtree, so a matching subtask under a non-matching task is not returned. Use the search endpoints to find matches at any depth.

Pagination (flat path only, cannot be combined with ?depth>1): pass ?limit=N (1..1000) to opt into paginated chunks. When more results exist, the LAST item carries "cursor": "<token>" — pass it back as ?cursor=<token> (plus the same ?limit= and ?status=) for the next page. Without ?limit= / ?cursor=, the response is the full bare array. ?limit=no is an explicit "return everything". Composes with ?return=compact.

Notes: Subtree responses (?depth>1) omit the per-task childCount field — the tasks array is the canonical signal. The flat default (?depth=1) and single-task GET /task/{oid} still include childCount. ?depth>1 cannot be combined with ?limit= or ?cursor= (returns 400).

Rate-limit cost: max(1, ceil(N / 100)) units, where N is the number of tasks returned. See Rate Limits. With ?depth>1, N counts every task in the returned subtree.

projectId: string
in path

ID of the task's project. Specify "-" for personal tasks in My Tasks.

taskId: integer
in path

Parent task ID.

status: string
in query

Task status filter. Specify a status value (an integer 0..100; 100 matches every completed status), or use "active" for active tasks or "completed" for completed tasks. Any other value returns 400. With ?depth>1, a task that doesn't match is left out with its whole subtree, even subtasks that match.

depth: string
in query

Subtree depth. Omit or 1 for the default flat single-level list (immediate children only). Any positive integer returns a multi-level subtree capped at the given depth; full walks every level (bounded by the per-tier total-nodes cap). ?depth>1 requires the Professional plan or above and cannot be combined with ?limit/?cursor.

limit: string
in query

Page size for the flat path (1..1000). Omit for the default unpaginated full list. Pass no to be explicit. When set and more results exist, the last item in the response carries a cursor field. Cannot be combined with ?depth>1.

cursor: string
in query

Continuation token. Pass back the cursor value from the last item of the previous page to fetch the next page. Re-pass ?limit= and any filter (?status=) on the same call. Cannot be combined with ?depth>1.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) for the standard task records, or compact for identifier-only items, {oid, id, cursor?}. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request. With ?depth>1, a compact item is {oid, id, tasks?, cropped?}. Pair with ?depth=full (subtree) or ?limit=N (paginated) to fetch a whole subtree's / page's identifier graph at minimal token cost; the agent then GET /task/{oid} for only the items it wants in detail.

200 OK
Task

OK — list of subtasks (may be empty). With ?depth>1, each entry may carry nested tasks + cropped fields.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — invalid ?status= / ?depth= / ?limit= / ?return= value, ?depth>1 combined with ?limit/?cursor, or ?cursor= doesn't belong to this list.

402 Payment Required

Payment Required (code 469) — ?depth>1 requires the Professional plan or above. Use ?depth=1 (or omit ?depth) for unrestricted flat per-level listing.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the user can't access it, or didn't authorize it for this app.

404 Not Found

Not Found — project or parent task does not exist.

task

Get all root tasks of the given project or all subtasks of the given task.

GET /task/list/{oid}

Returns all root tasks of a project or all direct subtasks of a task by OID. If the OID is a project, root tasks are returned. If it is a task, its direct subtasks are returned.

One level is returned by default. When the OID is a task, ?depth=N / ?depth=full walks the subtree in a single call — each task in the response then carries a nested tasks field with its walked children, recursively. ?depth>1 is not available when the OID is a project (there is no parent task to walk from); use the flat list per level instead.

When to use which:

  • Default (no ?depth): you only need the immediate children.
  • ?depth=2 or 3: small subtree where you know the shape.
  • ?depth=full: full subtree snapshot — pair with ?return=compact for navigation/lookup workloads to keep the payload (and LLM-token cost) small.

Per-tier total-nodes cap when ?depth>1: Free → rejected (402), Pro → 500, Premium → 2,000, Enterprise → unlimited (bounded only by the global response-size ceiling). When the cap fires mid-walk, the partial subtree is returned and the last emitted sibling at the cropped level carries "cropped": true. Recovery: list that sibling's parent again without ?depth to fetch the rest of that level — flat single-level lists have no cap.

Tree shape signals for the agent:

  • Node has a tasks array → its children were walked. Empty array means a true leaf.
  • Node has no tasks field → its children were not walked (depth limit reached, or cap fired before reaching it). Drill in if you need them.
  • Node has "cropped": true → more siblings of this node exist at the same level.

?status= with ?depth>1: a task that doesn't match is left out with its whole subtree, so a matching subtask under a non-matching task is not returned. Use the search endpoints to find matches at any depth.

Pagination (flat path only, cannot be combined with ?depth>1): pass ?limit=N (1..1000) to opt into paginated chunks. When more results exist, the LAST item carries "cursor": "<token>" — pass it back as ?cursor=<token> (plus the same ?limit= and ?status=) for the next page. Without ?limit= / ?cursor=, the response is the full bare array. ?limit=no is an explicit "return everything". Composes with ?return=compact.

Notes: Subtree responses (?depth>1) omit the per-task childCount field — the tasks array is the canonical signal. The flat default (?depth=1) and single-task GET /task/{oid} still include childCount. ?depth>1 cannot be combined with ?limit= or ?cursor= (returns 400).

Rate-limit cost: max(1, ceil(N / 100)) units, where N is the number of tasks returned. See Rate Limits. With ?depth>1, N counts every task in the returned subtree.

oid: string
in path

OID of the project or parent task. Specify - for your personal tasks (those in My Tasks that belong to no project).

status: string
in query

Task status filter. Specify a status value (an integer 0..100; 100 matches every completed status), or use "active" for active tasks or "completed" for completed tasks. Any other value returns 400. With ?depth>1, a task that doesn't match is left out with its whole subtree, even subtasks that match.

depth: string
in query

Subtree depth, only when the OID is a task. Omit or 1 for the default flat single-level list. Any positive integer returns a multi-level subtree capped at that depth; full walks every level (bounded by the per-tier total-nodes cap). ?depth>1 requires the Professional plan or above and cannot be combined with ?limit/?cursor.

limit: string
in query

Page size (1..1000). Omit for the default unpaginated full list, or pass no to be explicit. When set and more results exist, the last item in the response carries a cursor field.

cursor: string
in query

Continuation token. Pass back the cursor value from the last item of the previous page to fetch the next page. Re-pass any filter (?status=) and ?limit= on the same call.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) for the standard task records, or compact for identifier-only items, {oid, id, cursor?}. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request. With ?depth>1, a compact item is {oid, id, tasks?, cropped?}.

200 OK
Task

OK — list of tasks (may be empty).

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — invalid ?status= / ?depth= / ?limit= / ?return= value, ?depth>1 when the OID is a project, ?depth>1 combined with ?limit/?cursor, or ?cursor= doesn't belong to this list.

402 Payment Required

Payment Required (code 469) — ?depth>1 requires the Professional plan or above.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the user can't access it, or didn't authorize it for this app.

404 Not Found

Not Found — project or parent task does not exist.
