task

Search tasks in a project by project ID.

GET /task/search/id/{projectId}

Returns tasks that match the specified criteria in the project, most recently edited first (best match first with text). Pass at least one query parameter; none is rejected with 400.

Custom Field Filtering

You can filter by custom fields by passing the field name as a query parameter (case-insensitive). For example, ?cost=13 or ?approvedBy=john.doe. A field you can't view is an unknown query parameter.

Supported field types and value formats:

Operator grammar — Number, Money, Duration, and Date fields share a common set of operators (case-insensitive): ge:<v>, gt:<v>, le:<v>, lt:<v>, eq:<v>, ne:<v>, between:<v1>,<v2> (inclusive on both ends), notBetween:<v1>,<v2>, and isNull / isNotNull. Number, Money, and Duration also accept a bare value as an exact match (same as eq:). Date instead accepts keyword ops (today, past, last7d, ...) and requires an operator or keyword — a bare date is not accepted. The <v> operand format per type is below.

Type Value format Example
Number, Money <v> is a number cost=13, cost=ge:100, cost=between:50,150, cost=isNull
Checkbox true or false done=true
Select Option name stage=Review
User User ID, email, or OID approvedBy=john.doe
Task Task ID (integer) or OID blockedBy=42
Email, Hyperlink Exact value, or prefix with ~ for regex, ~* for case-insensitive regex website=~example\.com
Duration <v> is <n> seconds, or <n> with suffix d (days) / h (hours) / m (minutes) estimate=2h, estimate=ge:2h, estimate=between:8h,40h, estimate=isNull
Date <v> is YYYY-MM-DD or ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (a timestamp operand requires a withTime: true field). Same grammar as the start / due query params. approvedAt=today, approvedAt=ge:2026-04-01, approvedAt=between:2026-04-01,2026-04-30, approvedAt=isNull

Not supported: Text (use text for full-text search instead), Formula, File, Lookup.

A query parameter spelled exactly like a built-in one, e.g. priority, is the built-in filter, even if a custom field has that name.

Pagination

A page holds up to ?limit=N tasks (30 by default). When more matches remain, the last item carries a cursor field; pass its value back as ?cursor=<token> (along with the same ?limit= and any filter) to fetch the next page. End of stream is signalled by the absence of cursor on the last item.

Example loop:

GET /task/search/id/my_project?status=active&limit=30
    → 30 items; last has cursor: "crsr1u"
GET /task/search/id/my_project?status=active&limit=30&cursor=crsr1u
    → 30 items; last has cursor: "crsr11k"
GET /task/search/id/my_project?status=active&limit=30&cursor=crsr11k
    → 12 items; no cursor on last item → stop

With ?sublist=, no item carries a cursor: pass a limit big enough (or no) to get every match. Passing ?cursor= with it is rejected with 400. The cursor token is opaque — use it verbatim from the previous response. Paging reaches at most 1,000,000 rows deep; a deeper cursor is rejected with 400 — narrow the search with filters instead.

Rate-limit cost: max(1, ceil(N / 100)) units, where N is the number of tasks returned — e.g. 1 for a page of 100 or fewer, 10 for 1,000. See Rate Limits.

projectId: string
in path

ID of the task's project. Specify - for your personal tasks (those in My Tasks that belong to no project).

text: string
in query

Full-text query against task name, description, attachments, and the values of the custom fields you can view. At most 256 characters. Note: does not include comment content or comment attachments. Indexing can take ~10 seconds or more after updates.

name: string
in query

Task name filter, matched against the name's Markdown source. A bare value matches the whole name exactly (case-sensitive). Prefix with ~ for a regex, ~* for a case-insensitive regex; an invalid regex is rejected with 400. At most 256 characters. Use text for full-text search.

description: string
in query

Task description filter, matched against the description's Markdown source. A bare value matches the whole description exactly (case-sensitive). Prefix with ~ for a regex, ~* for a case-insensitive regex; an invalid regex is rejected with 400. At most 256 characters.

sublist: string
in query

Return only tasks in this sublist, by its ID or OID. No item then carries a cursor: pass a limit big enough (or no) to get every match.

status: string
in query

Task status filter: active (not completed), completed, or an integer 0..100 for that status, where 100 matches every completed status, like completed. Any other value returns 400.

scheduled: boolean
in query

Return only scheduled tasks (start or due is set). If scheduled=false, returns only tasks where neither start nor due is set.

mine: boolean
in query

Return only "My Tasks" (assigned to me, or created by me and scheduled but unassigned).

assignee: string
in query

Filter by assignee. Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email.

Combine values with , (AND), | (OR), and ! (NOT). AND binds tighter than OR.

Examples:

  • alice — a single user (by ID)
  • alice@example.com — by email
  • alice,bob — assigned to both
  • alice|bob — assigned to either
  • alice,!bob — assigned to alice but not bob
  • alice,bob|carol — (alice AND bob) OR carol
assignor: string
in query

Filter by assignor (the user who set the assignment). Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email. Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT); AND binds tighter than OR.

Examples: alice, alice,!bob, alice|bob.

follower: string
in query

Filter by follower. Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email. Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT); AND binds tighter than OR.

Examples: alice, alice,!bob, alice|bob.

tag: string
in query

Filter by tag. Each value is a tag OID or a tag name (names are resolved within the search's organization).

Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT); AND binds tighter than OR.

Names containing ,, |, !, ", or whitespace must be wrapped in "...". Inside quotes, write \" for a literal " and \\ for a literal \; any other \x is preserved as two literal characters.

Examples:

  • Legal — a single tag
  • Legal,!Draft — has Legal but not Draft
  • "In Progress",!Done — quoted name with space
  • "Foo\"s Go"|Other — quoted with escaped "
modified: string
in query

Return only tasks created or modified within the given period: a number of days (7), or a number with the suffix d (days), h (hours), or m (minutes), e.g. 8h. An empty value means 7 days; false turns the filter off.

commented: string
in query

Return only tasks commented on within the given period: a number of days (7), or a number with the suffix d (days), h (hours), or m (minutes), e.g. 8h. An empty value means 7 days; false turns the filter off.

source-ref: string
in query

Return only tasks whose sourceRef has this key, whatever its value: github finds the tasks created with "sourceRef": {"github": {"repo": "acme/web", "issue": 42}}. sourceRef is a JSON object an app stores when it creates or updates a task: its own data under a key named after the app, plus an optional text that Quire shows as the task's source line. This parameter's former name, sourceRef, still works.

created: string
in query

Filter by the task's createdAt timestamp. Value grammar:

  • Keyword: past, yesterday, today, tomorrow, upcoming, last7d, next7d, lastWeek, thisWeek, nextWeek
  • Value op: {ge|gt|le|lt|eq|ne}:<timestamp> or {between|notBetween}:<timestamp>,<timestamp>
  • <timestamp> is ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (UTC); a date-only operand such as 2026-04-01 is rejected with 400
  • isNull / isNotNull are rejected with 400, since createdAt is never null
  • Day boundaries resolve in the caller's timezone; week start follows the caller's locale
  • past on this field is < now()
  • Tokens and keywords are case-insensitive

Examples: today, last7d, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z, between:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z,2026-04-30T23:59:59Z.

edited: string
in query

Filter by the task's editedAt timestamp. Same grammar as created, timestamps only, and isNull / isNotNull are rejected with 400. Note: editedAt is NULL for tasks that have never been edited after creation; such tasks are excluded by every op (use created to filter by creation time).

Examples: today, last7d, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z.

archived: string
in query

Filter by the task's archivedAt timestamp. Same grammar as created (timestamps only), plus null ops since the field is nullable:

  • isNull — not archived
  • isNotNull — archived (any time)

Examples: isNotNull, today, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z.

unarchived: string
in query

Filter by the task's reshowAt timestamp (scheduled un-archive). Same grammar as archived (timestamps only; supports isNull / isNotNull).

Examples: isNotNull, today, between:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z,2026-04-30T23:59:59Z.

toggled: string
in query

Filter by the task's toggledAt timestamp (when its completion status was last changed). Same grammar as archived (timestamps only; supports isNull / isNotNull).

Examples: today, isNotNull, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z.

start: string
in query

Filter by the task's start date/time. Value grammar:

  • Keyword: past, yesterday, today, tomorrow, upcoming, last7d, next7d, lastWeek, thisWeek, nextWeek
  • Value op: {ge|gt|le|lt|eq|ne}:<value> or {between|notBetween}:<value>,<value>
  • Null op: isNull, isNotNull
  • <value> is either a date (YYYY-MM-DD) or a full ISO 8601 timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ)
  • A date operand expands to a whole-day window in the caller's timezone (ge:2026-04-01 means "on or after Apr 1 in the caller's calendar"); gt:D/le:D use end-of-day, lt:D/ge:D use start-of-day
  • past on start/due is < today 00:00 in the caller's timezone (not < now())
  • upcoming on start/due is the window [tomorrow, today + 7 days)

Examples: today, upcoming, ge:2026-04-01, between:2026-04-01,2026-04-30, isNull.

due: string
in query

Filter by the task's due date/time. Same grammar and semantics as start (accepts date-only operands, isNull/isNotNull, and the same keyword/value ops).

Examples: today, upcoming, le:2026-04-30, isNotNull.

priority: string
in query

Filter by task priority. Each value is an integer (-1..2) or a label (low, medium, high, urgent; case-insensitive): -1 Low, 0 Medium, 1 High, 2 Urgent. Any other value, such as none, is rejected with 400.

Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT). AND of two distinct positives is the empty set (a task has exactly one priority); negation works as expected.

Examples: high, 1, high|urgent, !low.

type: string
in query

Filter by task type. Values: normal (or task), section, milestone. Combine with , / | / !. Useful for structural navigation (e.g., listing only sections in a project).

Examples: section, section|milestone, !section.

created-by: string
in query

Filter by the user who created the task. Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email. Combine with , / | / ! (same grammar as assignee). This parameter's former name, createdBy, still works.

Examples: alice, alice|bob, !alice.

recurring: string
in query

Filter on whether the task has a recurrence configured. true (or empty) returns only recurring tasks; false returns only non-recurring tasks. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

limit: string
in query

Maximum number of tasks per page. Default: 30. Use no to return all matches.

On the Free plan, a limit over 30, or no, is rejected with 402 (code 469).

cursor: string
in query

Continuation token from the previous page's last item. See Pagination in the operation notes for the loop. At most 1,000,000 rows deep. Cannot be combined with ?sublist=.

200 OK
TaskWithParentInfo

OK — matching tasks (may be empty). When more matches remain, the last item carries a cursor field (never with ?sublist=).

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — no query parameter, or an invalid or unknown one (incl. a malformed or too deep cursor, or ?cursor= with ?sublist=).

402 Payment Required

Payment Required (code 469) — on the Free plan, limit is over 30 or no.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to search this project.

404 Not Found

Not Found — project does not exist.

task

Search tasks in a project by project OID.

GET /task/search/{projectOid}

Returns tasks that match the specified criteria in the project, most recently edited first (best match first with text). Pass at least one query parameter; none is rejected with 400.

Custom Field Filtering

You can filter by custom fields by passing the field name as a query parameter (case-insensitive). For example, ?cost=13 or ?approvedBy=john.doe. A field you can't view is an unknown query parameter.

Supported field types and value formats:

Operator grammar — Number, Money, Duration, and Date fields share a common set of operators (case-insensitive): ge:<v>, gt:<v>, le:<v>, lt:<v>, eq:<v>, ne:<v>, between:<v1>,<v2> (inclusive on both ends), notBetween:<v1>,<v2>, and isNull / isNotNull. Number, Money, and Duration also accept a bare value as an exact match (same as eq:). Date instead accepts keyword ops (today, past, last7d, ...) and requires an operator or keyword — a bare date is not accepted. The <v> operand format per type is below.

Type Value format Example
Number, Money <v> is a number cost=13, cost=ge:100, cost=between:50,150, cost=isNull
Checkbox true or false done=true
Select Option name stage=Review
User User ID, email, or OID approvedBy=john.doe
Task Task ID (integer) or OID blockedBy=42
Email, Hyperlink Exact value, or prefix with ~ for regex, ~* for case-insensitive regex website=~example\.com
Duration <v> is <n> seconds, or <n> with suffix d (days) / h (hours) / m (minutes) estimate=2h, estimate=ge:2h, estimate=between:8h,40h, estimate=isNull
Date <v> is YYYY-MM-DD or ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (a timestamp operand requires a withTime: true field). Same grammar as the start / due query params. approvedAt=today, approvedAt=ge:2026-04-01, approvedAt=between:2026-04-01,2026-04-30, approvedAt=isNull

Not supported: Text (use text for full-text search instead), Formula, File, Lookup.

A query parameter spelled exactly like a built-in one, e.g. priority, is the built-in filter, even if a custom field has that name.

Pagination

A page holds up to ?limit=N tasks (30 by default). When more matches remain, the last item carries a cursor field; pass its value back as ?cursor=<token> (along with the same ?limit= and any filter) to fetch the next page. End of stream is signalled by the absence of cursor on the last item.

Example loop:

GET /task/search/id/my_project?status=active&limit=30
    → 30 items; last has cursor: "crsr1u"
GET /task/search/id/my_project?status=active&limit=30&cursor=crsr1u
    → 30 items; last has cursor: "crsr11k"
GET /task/search/id/my_project?status=active&limit=30&cursor=crsr11k
    → 12 items; no cursor on last item → stop

With ?sublist=, no item carries a cursor: pass a limit big enough (or no) to get every match. Passing ?cursor= with it is rejected with 400. The cursor token is opaque — use it verbatim from the previous response. Paging reaches at most 1,000,000 rows deep; a deeper cursor is rejected with 400 — narrow the search with filters instead.

Rate-limit cost: max(1, ceil(N / 100)) units, where N is the number of tasks returned — e.g. 1 for a page of 100 or fewer, 10 for 1,000. See Rate Limits.

See also the by-ID form GET /task/search/id/{projectId}.

projectOid: string
in path

Project OID. Specify - for your personal tasks (those in My Tasks that belong to no project).

text: string
in query

Full-text query against task name, description, attachments, and the values of the custom fields you can view. At most 256 characters. Note: does not include comment content or comment attachments. Indexing can take ~10 seconds or more after updates.

name: string
in query

Task name filter, matched against the name's Markdown source. A bare value matches the whole name exactly (case-sensitive). Prefix with ~ for a regex, ~* for a case-insensitive regex; an invalid regex is rejected with 400. At most 256 characters. Use text for full-text search.

description: string
in query

Task description filter, matched against the description's Markdown source. A bare value matches the whole description exactly (case-sensitive). Prefix with ~ for a regex, ~* for a case-insensitive regex; an invalid regex is rejected with 400. At most 256 characters.

sublist: string
in query

Return only tasks in this sublist, by its ID or OID. No item then carries a cursor: pass a limit big enough (or no) to get every match.

status: string
in query

Task status filter: active (not completed), completed, or an integer 0..100 for that status, where 100 matches every completed status, like completed. Any other value returns 400.

scheduled: boolean
in query

Return only scheduled tasks (start or due is set). If scheduled=false, returns only tasks where neither start nor due is set.

mine: boolean
in query

Return only "My Tasks" (assigned to me, or created by me and scheduled but unassigned).

assignee: string
in query

Filter by assignee. Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email.

Combine values with , (AND), | (OR), and ! (NOT). AND binds tighter than OR.

Examples:

  • alice — a single user (by ID)
  • alice@example.com — by email
  • alice,bob — assigned to both
  • alice|bob — assigned to either
  • alice,!bob — assigned to alice but not bob
  • alice,bob|carol — (alice AND bob) OR carol
assignor: string
in query

Filter by assignor (the user who set the assignment). Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email. Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT); AND binds tighter than OR.

Examples: alice, alice,!bob, alice|bob.

follower: string
in query

Filter by follower. Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email. Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT); AND binds tighter than OR.

Examples: alice, alice,!bob, alice|bob.

tag: string
in query

Filter by tag. Each value is a tag OID or a tag name (names are resolved within the search's organization).

Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT); AND binds tighter than OR.

Names containing ,, |, !, ", or whitespace must be wrapped in "...". Inside quotes, write \" for a literal " and \\ for a literal \; any other \x is preserved as two literal characters.

Examples:

  • Legal — a single tag
  • Legal,!Draft — has Legal but not Draft
  • "In Progress",!Done — quoted name with space
  • "Foo\"s Go"|Other — quoted with escaped "
modified: string
in query

Return only tasks created or modified within the given period: a number of days (7), or a number with the suffix d (days), h (hours), or m (minutes), e.g. 8h. An empty value means 7 days; false turns the filter off.

commented: string
in query

Return only tasks commented on within the given period: a number of days (7), or a number with the suffix d (days), h (hours), or m (minutes), e.g. 8h. An empty value means 7 days; false turns the filter off.

source-ref: string
in query

Return only tasks whose sourceRef has this key, whatever its value: github finds the tasks created with "sourceRef": {"github": {"repo": "acme/web", "issue": 42}}. sourceRef is a JSON object an app stores when it creates or updates a task: its own data under a key named after the app, plus an optional text that Quire shows as the task's source line. This parameter's former name, sourceRef, still works.

created: string
in query

Filter by the task's createdAt timestamp. Value grammar:

  • Keyword: past, yesterday, today, tomorrow, upcoming, last7d, next7d, lastWeek, thisWeek, nextWeek
  • Value op: {ge|gt|le|lt|eq|ne}:<timestamp> or {between|notBetween}:<timestamp>,<timestamp>
  • <timestamp> is ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (UTC); a date-only operand such as 2026-04-01 is rejected with 400
  • isNull / isNotNull are rejected with 400, since createdAt is never null
  • Day boundaries resolve in the caller's timezone; week start follows the caller's locale
  • past on this field is < now()
  • Tokens and keywords are case-insensitive

Examples: today, last7d, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z, between:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z,2026-04-30T23:59:59Z.

edited: string
in query

Filter by the task's editedAt timestamp. Same grammar as created, timestamps only, and isNull / isNotNull are rejected with 400. Note: editedAt is NULL for tasks that have never been edited after creation; such tasks are excluded by every op (use created to filter by creation time).

Examples: today, last7d, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z.

archived: string
in query

Filter by the task's archivedAt timestamp. Same grammar as created (timestamps only), plus null ops since the field is nullable:

  • isNull — not archived
  • isNotNull — archived (any time)

Examples: isNotNull, today, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z.

unarchived: string
in query

Filter by the task's reshowAt timestamp (scheduled un-archive). Same grammar as archived (timestamps only; supports isNull / isNotNull).

Examples: isNotNull, today, between:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z,2026-04-30T23:59:59Z.

toggled: string
in query

Filter by the task's toggledAt timestamp (when its completion status was last changed). Same grammar as archived (timestamps only; supports isNull / isNotNull).

Examples: today, isNotNull, ge:2026-04-01T00:00:00Z.

start: string
in query

Filter by the task's start date/time. Value grammar:

  • Keyword: past, yesterday, today, tomorrow, upcoming, last7d, next7d, lastWeek, thisWeek, nextWeek
  • Value op: {ge|gt|le|lt|eq|ne}:<value> or {between|notBetween}:<value>,<value>
  • Null op: isNull, isNotNull
  • <value> is either a date (YYYY-MM-DD) or a full ISO 8601 timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ)
  • A date operand expands to a whole-day window in the caller's timezone (ge:2026-04-01 means "on or after Apr 1 in the caller's calendar"); gt:D/le:D use end-of-day, lt:D/ge:D use start-of-day
  • past on start/due is < today 00:00 in the caller's timezone (not < now())
  • upcoming on start/due is the window [tomorrow, today + 7 days)

Examples: today, upcoming, ge:2026-04-01, between:2026-04-01,2026-04-30, isNull.

due: string
in query

Filter by the task's due date/time. Same grammar and semantics as start (accepts date-only operands, isNull/isNotNull, and the same keyword/value ops).

Examples: today, upcoming, le:2026-04-30, isNotNull.

priority: string
in query

Filter by task priority. Each value is an integer (-1..2) or a label (low, medium, high, urgent; case-insensitive): -1 Low, 0 Medium, 1 High, 2 Urgent. Any other value, such as none, is rejected with 400.

Combine with , (AND), | (OR), ! (NOT). AND of two distinct positives is the empty set (a task has exactly one priority); negation works as expected.

Examples: high, 1, high|urgent, !low.

type: string
in query

Filter by task type. Values: normal (or task), section, milestone. Combine with , / | / !. Useful for structural navigation (e.g., listing only sections in a project).

Examples: section, section|milestone, !section.

created-by: string
in query

Filter by the user who created the task. Each value is a user OID, user ID, or email. Combine with , / | / ! (same grammar as assignee). This parameter's former name, createdBy, still works.

Examples: alice, alice|bob, !alice.

recurring: string
in query

Filter on whether the task has a recurrence configured. true (or empty) returns only recurring tasks; false returns only non-recurring tasks. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

limit: string
in query

Maximum number of tasks per page. Default: 30. Use no to return all matches.

On the Free plan, a limit over 30, or no, is rejected with 402 (code 469).

cursor: string
in query

Continuation token from the previous page's last item. See Pagination in the operation notes for the loop. At most 1,000,000 rows deep. Cannot be combined with ?sublist=.

200 OK
TaskWithParentInfo

OK — matching tasks (may be empty). When more matches remain, the last item carries a cursor field (never with ?sublist=).

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — no query parameter, or an invalid or unknown one (incl. a malformed or too deep cursor, or ?cursor= with ?sublist=).

402 Payment Required

Payment Required (code 469) — on the Free plan, limit is over 30 or no.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to search this project.

404 Not Found

Not Found — project does not exist.

task

Bulk-move N tasks within a project by ID.

PUT /task/bulk-move/id/{projectId}

Example: PUT /task/bulk-move/id/my_project?task=99&return=compact

Repositions up to 300 tasks (with their subtasks) within a project to the same destination anchor in one transaction. Same query-param grammar as single-task PUT /task/move/...:

  • ?task=root — move items to project root (only valid with default ?position=parent).
  • ?task={ref}&position=parent (default) — items become children of the reference task.
  • ?task={ref}&position=before — items become siblings immediately before the reference.
  • ?task={ref}&position=after — items become siblings immediately after the reference.

{ref} follows the URL grammar (same as single-task move): the by-ID URL form expects an integer task ID (or root); the by-OID form expects a task OID. A {ref} that isn't found, or is in another project, is rejected with 400. Items in the body use the bulk mixed-form convention (OID / integer ID / #<id> string) — same as bulk-remove.

Request body (mixed-form refs):

[ 42, "#17", "iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo" ]

Response (compact mode; slot 1 was already removed by another caller, so it's null):

[
  { "oid": "abc1Foo", "id": 42 },
  null,
  { "oid": "iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo", "id": 88 }
]

Atomic: a per-item validation, permission, or DB error rolls back the whole batch and returns {code, message} with an items[i]: prefix naming the offending item. Fix the value and retry. Moving a task under one of its own subtasks is such an error (400).

Skip-not-found: a ref that doesn't resolve to a live task in the project (already removed, never existed, a mistyped OID, cascade-removed by an earlier item, etc.) is skipped — its response slot is null and the rest of the batch proceeds. This makes the endpoint idempotent for agents — safe to re-submit after a partial network failure without diffing state first. Only a ref that is neither a string nor an integer is rejected with 400. An item in another project is skipped too.

Order preservation (sliding chain): items are moved in submitted order. Items 1..N-1 are positioned after the previous successful move, regardless of the URL ?position= — without this, ?position=after R would reverse the batch.

Dry-run: pass ?dry-run=true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same per-item validation and permission checks as a real call; same response body shape on success and same {code, message} (with items[i]: prefix) on failure. A 200 from a dry-run is a strong signal that re-issuing the identical body without ?dry-run will succeed (subject to concurrent edits between the two calls). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

Rate-limit cost: 1 unit per item, charged upfront — for bulk-add, per task created, nested tasks included. ?dry-run=true costs ceil(N / 2) units (minimum 1). Skipped items are charged too. See Rate Limits.

Batch size: at most 300 items per call, and no more than the plan's per-minute rate limit — e.g. 50 on the Free plan, or 25 in a personal project on the Free plan (see Rate Limits). A batch over the plan's cap is rejected with 402 (code 469), one over 300 with 400; split it.

All items must belong to the project in the URL. Cross-project moves go through bulk-transfer.

projectId: string
in path

Project ID. Specify - for your personal tasks (those in My Tasks that belong to no project).

task: string
in query

Reference task ID (the destination anchor for the whole batch), or root to move items to the project root.

position: string parent, before, after
in query

(Optional) Placement of moved items relative to the reference: parent (default), before, or after. before / after require ?task= to refer to a task (not root).

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) gives each item's full task record; compact gives only {"oid": …, "id": …} per item. Recommended for large batches. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

dry-run: string true, false
in query

(Optional) Set to true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same validation, permissions, and response shape as a real call, at half the rate-limit cost (ceil(N / 2) units). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

Request Example
[
  "object"
]
200 OK
TaskWithParentInfo

OK — array of moved tasks (slots for not-found items are null).

400 Bad Request
ErrorResponse

Bad Request — body not a JSON array, empty, over the 300-item cap, item shape error, ?task= missing, not found, or in another project, invalid ?position=, ?task=root&position=before|after, or an item moved under its own subtask. Whole batch rolled back.

402 Payment Required
ErrorResponse

Payment Required (code 469) — the batch holds more items than the plan allows per call (see Batch size).

403 Forbidden
ErrorResponse

Forbidden — caller lacks permission on the project or any task in the batch (whole batch rolled back).

404 Not Found
ErrorResponse

Not Found — project does not exist. (Item-level not-found is silent skip.)

413 Request Entity Too Large
ErrorResponse

Payload Too Large — body exceeds the API packet size limit.

429 Too Many Requests
ErrorResponse

Too Many Requests — the caller's per-minute / per-hour API quota is already used up (see Rate Limits).

task

Bulk-transfer N tasks across projects by ID.

PUT /task/bulk-transfer/id/{sourceProjectId}

Example: PUT /task/bulk-transfer/id/my_project?project=archive_2026&task=root&return=compact

Transfers up to 300 tasks, with their subtasks, from the source project (URL path) to a different target project (?project=) in one transaction. Same query-param grammar as single-task PUT /task/transfer/...:

  • ?project={target} (required) — target project, or - for your personal tasks.
  • ?task={ref} (optional) — destination anchor in the target project. Omitted, empty, or root → items become root tasks of the target. A {ref} that isn't found there is rejected with 400.
  • ?position= — parent (default), before, or after.
  • ?invite, ?tag, ?status, ?custom-field — auto-remap flags, all on by default; any value but true, 1, or empty turns one off.

In the by-ID URL form, ?project= and ?task= are IDs; in the by-OID form, OIDs. Items in the body use the bulk mixed-form convention (OID / integer ID / #<id> string) — same as bulk-remove / bulk-move.

Request body (mixed-form refs):

[ 42, "#99", "iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo" ]

Response (compact mode; OIDs are preserved across transfer, IDs are reassigned from the target's counter):

[
  { "oid": "abc1Foo",            "id": 7 },
  null,
  { "oid": "iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo", "id": 8 }
]

Atomic: a per-item validation, permission, or DB error rolls back the whole batch and returns {code, message} with an items[i]: prefix naming the offending item. Fix the value and retry. Both projects are rolled back.

Skip-not-found: a ref that doesn't resolve to a live task in the project (already removed, never existed, a mistyped OID, cascade-removed by an earlier item, etc.) is skipped — its response slot is null and the rest of the batch proceeds. This makes the endpoint idempotent for agents — safe to re-submit after a partial network failure without diffing state first. Only a ref that is neither a string nor an integer is rejected with 400. An item not in the source project (already in the target, or in another project) is skipped too.

Source == target: if ?project= resolves to the same project as the URL source, the whole batch is rejected with 400 (use bulk-move for within-project reorder).

Order preservation (sliding chain): items are transferred in submitted order — items 1..N-1 land after the previous successful transfer, regardless of ?position=.

Dry-run: pass ?dry-run=true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same per-item validation and permission checks as a real call; same response body shape on success and same {code, message} (with items[i]: prefix) on failure. A 200 from a dry-run is a strong signal that re-issuing the identical body without ?dry-run will succeed (subject to concurrent edits between the two calls). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write. Nothing is persisted in either project.

Rate-limit cost: 1 unit per item, charged upfront — for bulk-add, per task created, nested tasks included. ?dry-run=true costs ceil(N / 2) units (minimum 1). Skipped items are charged too. See Rate Limits.

Batch size: at most 300 items per call, and no more than the plan's per-minute rate limit — e.g. 50 on the Free plan, or 25 in a personal project on the Free plan (see Rate Limits). A batch over the plan's cap is rejected with 402 (code 469), one over 300 with 400; split it.

sourceProjectId: string
in path

Source project ID. Specify - for your personal tasks (those in My Tasks that belong to no project).

project: string
in query

Target project ID. Specify - for your personal tasks (those in My Tasks that belong to no project).

task: string
in query

(Optional) Reference task ID in the target project (destination anchor for the whole batch), or root to transfer items to the target project's root.

position: string parent, before, after
in query

(Optional) Placement of transferred items relative to the reference: parent (default), before, or after. before / after require ?task= to refer to a task (not root).

invite: string
in query

(Optional) Whether to invite assignees to the target project if they are not already members. It applies only if you are an admin of the target project (never when the target is -, your personal tasks); otherwise nobody is invited.

On by default: omitted, true, 1, or an empty value keeps it on; any other value, e.g. false, turns it off.

tag: string
in query

(Optional) Whether to add tags to the target project if they are not already present.

On by default: omitted, true, 1, or an empty value keeps it on; any other value, e.g. false, turns it off.

status: string
in query

(Optional) Whether to add statuses to the target project if they are not already present.

On by default: omitted, true, 1, or an empty value keeps it on; any other value, e.g. false, turns it off.

custom-field: string
in query

(Optional) Whether to add non-empty custom fields to the target project if they are not already present.

On by default: omitted, true, 1, or an empty value keeps it on; any other value, e.g. false, turns it off.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) gives each item's full task record; compact gives only {"oid": …, "id": …} per item. Recommended for large batches. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

dry-run: string true, false
in query

(Optional) Set to true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same validation, permissions, and response shape as a real call, at half the rate-limit cost (ceil(N / 2) units). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

  "object"
]
200 OK
TaskWithParentInfo

OK — array of transferred tasks (slots for not-found items are null).

400 Bad Request
ErrorResponse

Bad Request — body not a JSON array, empty, over the 300-item cap, item shape error, missing ?project=, ?task= not found in the target, invalid ?position=, ?task=root&position=before|after, ?project= resolves to the URL source project, or any per-item validation failure. Whole batch rolled back.

402 Payment Required
ErrorResponse

Payment Required (code 469) — the batch holds more items than the plan allows per call (see Batch size); the target would go over its plan's task or storage quota; or a task (or a subtask) has reminders and the target's plan doesn't include reminders. Whole batch rolled back.

403 Forbidden
ErrorResponse

Forbidden — caller lacks permission on the source or target project, or on any individual task in the batch. Whole batch rolled back.

404 Not Found
ErrorResponse

Not Found — source or target project does not exist. (Item-level not-found is silent skip.)

413 Request Entity Too Large
ErrorResponse

Payload Too Large — body exceeds the API packet size limit.

429 Too Many Requests
ErrorResponse

Too Many Requests — the caller's per-minute / per-hour API quota is already used up (see Rate Limits).

task

Bulk-update N tasks in a project by ID.

PUT /task/bulk-update/id/{projectId}

Example: PUT /task/bulk-update/id/my_project?return=compact

Updates up to 300 tasks in one transaction. Body is a top-level JSON array of BulkUpdateTaskItem — each item carries exactly one of oid / id — id may be an integer or a "#42" string — plus the UpdateTaskBody-shape fields to apply. Both or neither is rejected with 400.

Request body:

[
  { "id": 42, "status": 100, "addTags": ["done"] },
  { "id": 99, "addAssignees": ["alice@example.com"] },
  { "id": 17, "name": "Renamed" }
]

Tags must exist already in the project (or be global tags of its organization); an unknown tag is rejected with 400.

Response (compact mode; slot for a not-found item is null):

[
  { "oid": "iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo", "id": 42 },
  null,
  { "oid": "defLmnQrSt", "id": 17 }
]

In full mode, each slot is the full updated task record, parent included.

Atomic: a per-item validation, permission, or DB error rolls back the whole batch and returns {code, message} with an items[i]: prefix naming the offending item. Fix the value and retry. Example error:

{ "code": 400, "message": "items[1]: Invalid value for `priority`: 99 (expected -1, 0, 1, or 2 (or one of Low/Medium/High/Urgent))" }

Skip-not-found: a ref that doesn't resolve to a live task in the project (already removed, never existed, a mistyped OID, cascade-removed by an earlier item, etc.) is skipped — its response slot is null and the rest of the batch proceeds. This makes the endpoint idempotent for agents — safe to re-submit after a partial network failure without diffing state first. Only a ref that is neither a string nor an integer is rejected with 400.

Dry-run: pass ?dry-run=true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same per-item validation and permission checks as a real call; same response body shape on success and same {code, message} (with items[i]: prefix) on failure. A 200 from a dry-run is a strong signal that re-issuing the identical body without ?dry-run will succeed (subject to concurrent edits between the two calls). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

Rate-limit cost: 1 unit per item, charged upfront — for bulk-add, per task created, nested tasks included. ?dry-run=true costs ceil(N / 2) units (minimum 1). Skipped items are charged too. See Rate Limits.

Batch size: at most 300 items per call, and no more than the plan's per-minute rate limit — e.g. 50 on the Free plan, or 25 in a personal project on the Free plan (see Rate Limits). A batch over the plan's cap is rejected with 402 (code 469), one over 300 with 400; split it.

projectId: string
in path

Project ID. Specify - for your personal tasks (those in My Tasks that belong to no project).

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape: full (default) gives each item's full task record; compact gives only {"oid": …, "id": …} per item. Recommended for large batches. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

dry-run: string true, false
in query

(Optional) Set to true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same validation, permissions, and response shape as a real call, at half the rate-limit cost (ceil(N / 2) units). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

TaskWithParentInfo

OK — array of updated tasks (slots for not-found items are null).

400 Bad Request
ErrorResponse

Bad Request — body not a JSON array, empty, over the 300-item cap, item shape error (both/neither oid and id, or a ref that is neither a string nor an integer), or any per-item validation failure (whole batch rolled back).

402 Payment Required
ErrorResponse

Payment Required (code 469) — the batch holds more items than the plan allows per call (see Batch size).

403 Forbidden
ErrorResponse

Forbidden — caller lacks permission on the project or any task in the batch (whole batch rolled back).

404 Not Found
ErrorResponse

Not Found — project does not exist. (Item-level not-found is silent skip.)

409 Conflict
ErrorResponse

Conflict — project settings block completing an item (an open predecessor, or a pending approval) (whole batch rolled back).

413 Request Entity Too Large
ErrorResponse

Payload Too Large — body exceeds the API packet size limit.

429 Too Many Requests
ErrorResponse

Too Many Requests — the caller's per-minute / per-hour API quota is already used up (see Rate Limits).

task

Move an existing task by its ID.

PUT /task/move/id/{projectId}/{taskId}

Moves an existing task, with its subtasks, under another task as a subtask, reorders it among siblings, or sends it to the root level, within its project. To move it to another project, use the transfer endpoints.

Use ?task= to name the reference task and ?position= to choose placement (parent / before / after); ?task=root moves it to the root level.

Returns the updated task record. A ?task= that isn't found, or is in another project, is rejected with 400, as is moving a task under one of its own subtasks.

Examples:

  • PUT /task/move/id/my_project/42?task=99 — reparent (default: child of task 99).
  • PUT /task/move/id/my_project/42?task=99&position=before — place task 42 before task 99.
  • PUT /task/move/id/my_project/42?task=99&position=after — place task 42 after task 99.
  • PUT /task/move/id/my_project/42?task=root — move to root level.
  • PUT /task/move/iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo?task=0Mg3VQ8kWeiVbLH1JjvzUcP7&position=after — the same by OID: in this form, ?task= is a task OID.
projectId: string
in path

ID of the task's project. Specify "-" for personal tasks in My Tasks.

taskId: integer
in path

Task ID to be moved.

task: string
in query

Reference task ID. How it's used depends on position:

  • parent (default): the moved task becomes a child of task.
  • before / after: the moved task is placed as a sibling, under task's parent.

Specify root to move to the root level (only valid with the default parent position).

position: string parent, before, after
in query

(Optional) Placement relative to task:

  • parent (default): child of task.
  • before: sibling immediately before task.
  • after: sibling immediately after task.

Omitted or empty → same as parent. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request. before / after require task to refer to a task (not root).

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape:

  • full (default): the full task record.
  • compact: only {"oid": …, "id": …} — the task's OID and ID. Saves payload, tokens, and a server-side reload; enough to chain follow-up calls.

Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

200 OK
TaskWithParentInfo

OK — updated task record.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — task missing, not found, or in another project; invalid position; or the new parent is one of the task's subtasks.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to move this task.

404 Not Found

Not Found — task does not exist.

Response Content-Types: application/json

  "successors": "[\"#135\", \"#26\"]",
  "predecessors": "[\"#17\", \"#66\", \"#91\"]",

      "id": 12,

task

Move an existing task by its OID.

PUT /task/move/{oid}

Moves an existing task, with its subtasks, under another task as a subtask, reorders it among siblings, or sends it to the root level, within its project. To move it to another project, use the transfer endpoints.

Use ?task= to name the reference task and ?position= to choose placement (parent / before / after); ?task=root moves it to the root level.

Returns the updated task record. A ?task= that isn't found, or is in another project, is rejected with 400, as is moving a task under one of its own subtasks.

Examples:

  • PUT /task/move/id/my_project/42?task=99 — reparent (default: child of task 99).
  • PUT /task/move/id/my_project/42?task=99&position=before — place task 42 before task 99.
  • PUT /task/move/id/my_project/42?task=99&position=after — place task 42 after task 99.
  • PUT /task/move/id/my_project/42?task=root — move to root level.
  • PUT /task/move/iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo?task=0Mg3VQ8kWeiVbLH1JjvzUcP7&position=after — the same by OID: in this form, ?task= is a task OID.
oid: string
in path

Task OID to be moved.

task: string
in query

Reference task OID. How it's used depends on position:

  • parent (default): the moved task becomes a child of task.
  • before / after: the moved task is placed as a sibling, under task's parent.

Specify root to move to the root level (only valid with the default parent position).

position: string parent, before, after
in query

(Optional) Placement relative to task:

  • parent (default): child of task.
  • before: sibling immediately before task.
  • after: sibling immediately after task.

Omitted or empty → same as parent. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request. before / after require task to refer to a task (not root).

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape:

  • full (default): the full task record.
  • compact: only {"oid": …, "id": …} — the task's OID and ID. Saves payload, tokens, and a server-side reload; enough to chain follow-up calls.

Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

200 OK
TaskWithParentInfo

OK — updated task record.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — task missing, not found, or in another project; invalid position; or the new parent is one of the task's subtasks.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to move this task.

404 Not Found

Not Found — task does not exist.

Response Content-Types: application/json
Response Example (200 OK)

task

Transfer an existing task by its ID to another project.

PUT /task/transfer/id/{projectId}/{taskId}

Transfers an existing task, with its subtasks, to another project, optionally positioning it relative to an existing task in the target (?task= + ?position=). The task keeps its OID but gets an ID in the target project, usually a new one — read it from the response. The target can't be the task's own project (400; use move instead).

?invite, ?tag, ?status, and ?custom-field (all on by default) bring the assignees, tags, statuses, and custom fields the task uses into the target project.

Reminders on the task and its subtasks move with it. If the target's plan doesn't include reminders, or the transfer would take the target past its plan's task or storage quota, the call is rejected with 402 (code 469) and nothing changes.

Returns the updated task record.

Examples:

  • PUT /task/transfer/id/my_project/42?project=archive — transfer to root of target project.
  • PUT /task/transfer/id/my_project/42?project=archive&task=99 — transfer as a child of task 99 in target.
  • PUT /task/transfer/id/my_project/42?project=archive&task=99&position=before — transfer and place before task 99.
  • PUT /task/transfer/id/my_project/42?project=- — transfer to your personal tasks.
  • PUT /task/transfer/iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo?project=0Mg3VQ8kWeiVbLH1PrjzUc89 — the same by OID: in this form, ?project= and ?task= are OIDs.
projectId: string
in path

ID of the task's project. Specify "-" for personal tasks in My Tasks.

taskId: integer
in path

Task ID to be transferred.

project: string
in query

ID of the target project to which the task will be transferred. Specify - for your personal tasks (those in My Tasks that belong to no project).

task: string
in query

(Optional) ID of a reference task in the target project. How it's used depends on position:

  • parent (default): the transferred task becomes a child of task.
  • before / after: the transferred task is placed as a sibling, under task's parent.

If omitted (or root), the transferred task becomes a root task in the target project.

position: string parent, before, after
in query

(Optional) Placement relative to task in the target project:

  • parent (default): child of task.
  • before: sibling immediately before task.
  • after: sibling immediately after task.

Omitted or empty → same as parent. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request. before / after require task to refer to a task (not omitted, not root).

invite: string
in query

(Optional) Whether to invite assignees to the target project if they are not already members. It applies only if you are an admin of the target project (never when the target is -, your personal tasks); otherwise nobody is invited.

On by default: omitted, true, 1, or an empty value keeps it on; any other value, e.g. false, turns it off.

tag: string
in query

(Optional) Whether to add tags to the target project if they are not already present.

On by default: omitted, true, 1, or an empty value keeps it on; any other value, e.g. false, turns it off.

status: string
in query

(Optional) Whether to add statuses to the target project if they are not already present.

On by default: omitted, true, 1, or an empty value keeps it on; any other value, e.g. false, turns it off.

custom-field: string
in query

(Optional) Whether to add non-empty custom fields to the target project if they are not already present.

On by default: omitted, true, 1, or an empty value keeps it on; any other value, e.g. false, turns it off.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape:

  • full (default): the full task record.
  • compact: only {"oid": …, "id": …} — the task's OID and ID. Saves payload, tokens, and a server-side reload; enough to chain follow-up calls.

Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

200 OK
TaskWithParentInfo

OK — updated task record.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — project missing or the task's own project; task not found in the target project; or invalid position.

402 Payment Required

Payment Required (code 469) — the target would go over its plan's task or storage quota, or the task (or a subtask) has reminders and the target's plan doesn't include reminders.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to transfer this task.

404 Not Found

Not Found — task or target project does not exist.

Response Example (200 OK)

task

Undo the removal of a task by its ID.

PUT /task/undo-remove/id/{projectId}/{taskId}

Restores a previously-removed task, with the subtasks removed along with it, and its removed ancestors. Idempotent: if the task is not currently removed, this is a no-op and returns the current task record.

Restored tasks count toward the plan's task limit, as created ones do: if restoring them (subtasks and ancestors included) would go past it, nothing is restored and the call returns 402 (code 469).

projectId: string
in path

Project ID. Specify - for your personal tasks (those in My Tasks that belong to no project).

taskId: integer
in path

Task ID.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape:

  • full (default): the full task record.
  • compact: only {"oid": …, "id": …} — the task's OID and ID. Saves payload, tokens, and a server-side reload; enough to chain follow-up calls.

Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

200 OK
TaskWithParentInfo

OK — restored task record.

402 Payment Required

Payment Required (code 469) — restoring would go past the plan's task limit; nothing is restored.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — caller lacks permission to restore this task.

404 Not Found

Not Found — task does not exist.

task

Update an existing time log on a task by ID.

PUT /task/update-timelog/id/{projectId}/{taskId}

Updates an existing time log on the task. The log to update is located by the start, end, and (optional) user query parameters — that triple is the log's identity. The body carries new values; any field omitted or set to null preserves the existing value (so an agent that always includes every field with null for unchanged ones is safe). To clear note, send an empty string.

Sub-second precision in time values is truncated to whole seconds (in both query params and body).

On success returns the task's full timelogs array. If the project hides time logs from guests (its default), a guest member or a non-member gets an empty array, as timelogs is omitted from the task records they get. Example:

[
  {
    "start": "2026-04-26T09:15:00.000Z",
    "end": "2026-04-26T10:45:00.000Z",
    "billable": true,
    "note": "Updated note",
    "user": { "oid": "u-123", "name": "John Doe" }
  }
]
projectId: string
in path

Project ID.

taskId: integer
in path

Task ID.

start: string
in query

Start timestamp of the existing log (identifies the log together with end and user). ISO 8601, UTC.

end: string
in query

End timestamp of the existing log. ISO 8601, UTC.

user: string
in query

(Optional) User the existing log is credited to (OID, ID, or email). Omitted defaults to the authenticated caller.

end: string

(Optional) New end timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC). Must be on or after the (new or existing) start. Sub-second precision is truncated to whole seconds. Omit or set null to preserve.

start: string

(Optional) New start timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC). Sub-second precision is truncated to whole seconds. Omit or set null to preserve.

user: string

(Optional) New user the log is credited to (OID, ID, or email). Omit or set null to preserve. Send empty string to reset to the authenticated caller.

billable: boolean

(Optional) New billable flag. Omit or set null to preserve.

note: string

(Optional) New note. Omit or set null to preserve. Send empty string to clear.

Request Example
{
  "end": "2026-04-26T10:45:00Z",
  "start": "2026-04-26T09:15:00Z",
  "user": "john.doe@example.com",
  "billable": false,
  "note": "Updated note"
}
200 OK
Timelog

OK — task's full timelogs array.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — start / end query params missing or malformed, end precedes start (in the query or the new values), a user (in the query or the body) is unknown, or a body field has the wrong type.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the caller can't change this task's time logs (checked before the log is looked up).

404 Not Found

Not Found — no log matches the identifying triple, or the task does not exist.

Response Content-Types: application/json
Response Example (200 OK) 
[
  {
    "start": "2023-02-20T00:00:00.000Z",
    "end": "2023-02-20T00:05:35.000Z",
    "user": {
      "url": "https://quire.io/u/my_id",
      "id": "my_id",
      "iconColor": "37",
      "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",
      "name": "Foo",
      "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
    },
    "billable": true,
    "note": "A piece of cake"
  }
]
task

Update an existing time log on a task by OID.

PUT /task/update-timelog/{oid}

Updates an existing time log on the task. The log to update is located by the start, end, and (optional) user query parameters — that triple is the log's identity. The body carries new values; any field omitted or set to null preserves the existing value (so an agent that always includes every field with null for unchanged ones is safe). To clear note, send an empty string.

Sub-second precision in time values is truncated to whole seconds (in both query params and body).

On success returns the task's full timelogs array. If the project hides time logs from guests (its default), a guest member or a non-member gets an empty array, as timelogs is omitted from the task records they get. Example:

[
  {
    "start": "2026-04-26T09:15:00.000Z",
    "end": "2026-04-26T10:45:00.000Z",
    "billable": true,
    "note": "Updated note",
    "user": { "oid": "u-123", "name": "John Doe" }
  }
]

See also the by-ID form PUT /task/update-timelog/id/{projectId}/{taskId}.

oid: string
in path

Task OID.

start: string
in query

Start timestamp of the existing log (identifies the log together with end and user). ISO 8601, UTC.

end: string
in query

End timestamp of the existing log. ISO 8601, UTC.

user: string
in query

(Optional) User the existing log is credited to (OID, ID, or email). Omitted defaults to the authenticated caller.

end: string

(Optional) New end timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC). Must be on or after the (new or existing) start. Sub-second precision is truncated to whole seconds. Omit or set null to preserve.

start: string

(Optional) New start timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC). Sub-second precision is truncated to whole seconds. Omit or set null to preserve.

user: string

(Optional) New user the log is credited to (OID, ID, or email). Omit or set null to preserve. Send empty string to reset to the authenticated caller.

billable: boolean

(Optional) New billable flag. Omit or set null to preserve.

note: string

(Optional) New note. Omit or set null to preserve. Send empty string to clear.

Request Example
{
  "end": "2026-04-26T10:45:00Z",
  "start": "2026-04-26T09:15:00Z",
  "user": "john.doe@example.com",
  "billable": false,
  "note": "Updated note"
}
200 OK
Timelog

OK — task's full timelogs array.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — start / end query params missing or malformed, end precedes start (in the query or the new values), a user (in the query or the body) is unknown, or a body field has the wrong type.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the caller can't change this task's time logs (checked before the log is looked up).

404 Not Found

Not Found — no log matches the identifying triple, or the task does not exist.

Response Example (200 OK)

  {
    "start": "2023-02-20T00:00:00.000Z",
    "end": "2023-02-20T00:05:35.000Z",
    "user": {
      "url": "https://quire.io/u/my_id",
      "id": "my_id",
      "iconColor": "37",
      "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",

task

Update an existing task by its ID.

PUT /task/id/{projectId}/{taskId}

Updates an existing task and returns the updated record.

Only the fields you include are updated; omitted fields are left unchanged. Example — complete the task, add a tag, and remove an assignee:

{
  "status": 100,
  "addTags": ["done"],
  "removeAssignees": ["alice@example.com"]
}

Tags must exist already, as tags of the project or global tags of its organization: an unknown tag, like done here if the project has none, is rejected with 400, not created.

Note the replace-vs-incremental pattern: tags replaces the entire tag set; addTags / removeTags modify the set in place. Same for assignees / addAssignees / removeAssignees, and followers / successors / etc. Mix whichever suits the intent.

To archive (hide indefinitely) or snooze a task, set the peekaboo field: true hides it indefinitely, a positive integer hides it for that many days, false unhides.

projectId: string
in path

ID of the task's project. Specify "-" for personal tasks in My Tasks.

taskId: integer
in path

Task ID.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape:

  • full (default): the full task record.
  • compact: only {"oid": …, "id": …} — the task's OID and ID. Saves payload, tokens, and a server-side reload; enough to chain follow-up calls.

Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

description: string

(Optional) New task description. An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

tags: string[]

(Optional) Tags to replace the current tags on this task (OID or name). This replaces all existing tags. To modify incrementally, use addTags or removeTags. Tag names are case-insensitive. Each must be an existing tag of the project, or a global tag of its organization; an unknown tag is rejected with 400, not created.

partner: string

(Optional) The external team to share this task with: the name or OID of one of the project's external teams (GET /partner/list/id/{projectId} lists them). The team's members then get access to the task and its subtasks. Setting it takes the right to assign tasks (403 otherwise). A name or OID that matches no team, or a value that isn't a string, is rejected with 400. The API can't remove it: null is rejected too.

recurrence: Recurrence

(Optional) Makes the task repeat, replacing its current recurrence, if any. null stops it repeating.

  • freq (required): daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.
  • interval: a positive integer; 2 with weekly means every 2 weeks. Default: 1.
  • until: end date, e.g. 2026-12-31. Default: never ends.
  • weekly needs byweekday: the days of the week as a list, where 0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday, e.g. [0, 3].
  • monthly needs bydayno, the day of the month (1–31, or "last"), or byweekno, the week of the month (1–5, or "last"), with byweekday as a single day in that week, e.g. 1 for Tuesday. If both byweekno and bydayno are given, byweekno wins.
  • yearly needs bymonth, the month (1–12, 1 = January), plus what monthly needs.
  • dupsubtasks: whether to duplicate subtasks when the task is completed. Default: true.
  • sincelatest: with daily only, whether to repeat from the last completion date. Default: false.

A property that doesn't apply to freq is ignored; an invalid value, or a missing required one, is rejected with 400.

A recurring task always has a due. If the task has none and due is omitted, it is derived from the recurrence: the nearest occurrence since today. The request is rejected if the derived due precedes start; specify due explicitly in that case.

assignees: string[]

(Optional) Assignees to replace the current assignees (OID, ID, or email). This replaces all existing assignees. To modify incrementally, use addAssignees or removeAssignees.

Accepts the same special values as addAssignees: "me" (the current user) and "inherit" (all assignees of the parent task).

Only project members (external-team members included) can be assigned; anyone else is silently left out. An unknown user is rejected with 400.

asUser: boolean

(Optional) If true, marks this update as performed by the app. Read asUser as app-as-user: the app itself is the user, not the authorizing user. Default: false (updated by the authorizing user). In bulk-update, each item has its own.

followers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to replace the current followers (OID, ID, or email).

Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": include followers of the parent task
  • "app": the application follows (receives notifications)

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL (e.g., .../standard/soc1/33456/a7).

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

successors: string[]

(Optional) Successors to replace the current successors (task OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

start: string

(Optional) Start date/time in UTC.

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

Notes:

  • Seconds are not supported.
  • 2020-10-30T00:00:00 is treated as 2020-10-30 (date only).
  • To specify exactly midnight UTC, use 2020-10-30T00:00 (no seconds).
due: string

(Optional) Due date/time in UTC.

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

Notes:

  • Seconds are not supported.
  • 2020-10-30T00:00:00 is treated as 2020-10-30 (date only).
  • To specify exactly midnight UTC, use 2020-10-30T00:00 (no seconds).
  • null clears it. It is rejected if the task is recurring, since a recurring task always has a due; pass recurrence: null in the same request to stop repeating and clear the due together.
yourField: object

PLACEHOLDER — do NOT send a key literally named yourField. Instead, use the custom field's own name (as defined via /project/add-field) as the JSON key, with a value matching the field's type:

  • Text / Email / Hyperlink: string.
  • Number / Money: numeric value (no currency symbol).
  • Checkbox: true or false.
  • Select: option name (string).
  • Date: ISO 8601 timestamp (yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssZ) or date-only (yyyy-MM-dd).
  • Duration: number of seconds.
  • User: user OID, user ID, or email — server resolves to the user's OID.
  • Task: task OID, integer task ID, or #<id> string — server resolves to the task's OID (scoped to this project).
  • File: the attachment list as a task returns it (absolute url accepted); send an entry back unchanged to keep that file.
  • Multi-value (fields configured with multiple: true): provide a list. Pass null to clear the field.

A field you can't view or edit (the definition's viewMembers and editMembers) is rejected with 400; locked stops editing in Quire only, not through the API.

Example body fragment: {"Priority": 3, "Owners": ["alice", "bob@example.com"], "Depends": ["#42"]}.

peekaboo:
boolean
integer

(Optional) Peekaboo setting. Accepts a boolean or a positive integer:

  • true: Hide indefinitely (task and subtasks).
  • positive integer: Number of days to hide.
  • false: Undo previous peekaboo.
section: boolean

(Optional) true makes this task a section; false makes it a normal task. If both section and milestone are sent, only section is applied.

milestone: boolean

(Optional) true makes this task a milestone; false makes it a normal task. Ignored if section is sent too.

addTags: string[]

(Optional) Tags to add to this task (OID or name). Tag names are case-insensitive. Each must be an existing tag of the project, or a global tag of its organization; an unknown tag is rejected with 400, not created.

removeTags: string[]

(Optional) Tags to remove from this task (OID or name). Tag names are case-insensitive. An unknown tag is rejected with 400.

addAssignees: string[]

(Optional) Assignees to add (OID, ID, or email). Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": include all assignees of the parent task

Only project members (external-team members included) can be assigned; anyone else is silently left out. An unknown user is rejected with 400.

removeAssignees: string[]

(Optional) Assignees to remove (OID, ID, or email).

Accepts the same special values as addAssignees: "me" (the current user) and "inherit" (all assignees of the parent task).

addFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to add (OID, ID, or email). Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": include followers of the parent task
  • "app": the application follows (receives notifications)

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL (e.g., .../standard/soc1/33456/a7).

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

removeFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to remove (OID, ID, or email).

Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": remove followers that were inherited from the parent task
  • "app": the application

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL.

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

addSuccessors: string[]

(Optional) Successors to add (task OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

removeSuccessors: string[]

(Optional) Successors to remove (task OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

name: string

(Optional) New task name.

status: integer

(Optional) New status. Must be one of the project's status values (GET /status/list/id/{projectId} lists them); any other value is rejected with 400. Every project has 0, the initial status, and 100, completed; 100 or more means completed. Specify 100 to complete the task. Completion may be rejected (409 Conflict) when project settings require all predecessors to be completed first, or require an approval to be granted.

etc: integer

(Optional) Estimated time to complete, in seconds. Must be 0 to 864,000,000 (10,000 days) or null. Specify null to clear the value.

priority: integer -1, 0, 1, 2

(Optional) New priority: -1 Low, 0 Medium, 1 High, 2 Urgent. (The server also accepts the case-insensitive English names Low, Medium, High, Urgent, but the integer form is recommended for typed callers.)

sourceRef: object

(Optional) A JSON object your app stores with the task, such as where the task came from. Quire keeps it as is and returns it as sourceRef whenever the task is read.

  • text (optional): a Markdown string Quire shows as the task's source line in the task details. Include a link to the source, e.g. Source: [GitHub issue 42](https://github.com/acme/web/issues/42).
  • Any other key: your app's own data, not shown in Quire. Put it under a key named after your app, e.g. github, so it won't clash with another app's.
  • To find these tasks later, search with ?source-ref=github: it returns the tasks whose sourceRef has that key, whatever its value.
  • Size: at most about 2,048 characters, keys and values together, and text must be a string; otherwise 400.
  • It replaces the stored object as a whole: keys you leave out are removed, and null removes sourceRef. Another app may have stored its own key on the task; to keep it, read the task first and send that key back.
