task

Update an existing task by its OID.

PUT /task/{oid}

Updates an existing task and returns the updated record.

Only the fields you include are updated; omitted fields are left unchanged. Example — complete the task, add a tag, and remove an assignee:

{
  "status": 100,
  "addTags": ["done"],
  "removeAssignees": ["alice@example.com"]
}

Tags must exist already, as tags of the project or global tags of its organization: an unknown tag, like done here if the project has none, is rejected with 400, not created.

Note the replace-vs-incremental pattern: tags replaces the entire tag set; addTags / removeTags modify the set in place. Same for assignees / addAssignees / removeAssignees, and followers / successors / etc. Mix whichever suits the intent.

To archive (hide indefinitely) or snooze a task, set the peekaboo field: true hides it indefinitely, a positive integer hides it for that many days, false unhides.

oid: string
in path

Task OID.

return: string full, compact
in query

(Optional) Response shape:

  • full (default): the full task record.
  • compact: only {"oid": …, "id": …} — the task's OID and ID. Saves payload, tokens, and a server-side reload; enough to chain follow-up calls.

Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

description: string

(Optional) New task description. An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

tags: string[]

(Optional) Tags to replace the current tags on this task (OID or name). This replaces all existing tags. To modify incrementally, use addTags or removeTags. Tag names are case-insensitive. Each must be an existing tag of the project, or a global tag of its organization; an unknown tag is rejected with 400, not created.

partner: string

(Optional) The external team to share this task with: the name or OID of one of the project's external teams (GET /partner/list/id/{projectId} lists them). The team's members then get access to the task and its subtasks. Setting it takes the right to assign tasks (403 otherwise). A name or OID that matches no team, or a value that isn't a string, is rejected with 400. The API can't remove it: null is rejected too.

recurrence: Recurrence

(Optional) Makes the task repeat, replacing its current recurrence, if any. null stops it repeating.

  • freq (required): daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.
  • interval: a positive integer; 2 with weekly means every 2 weeks. Default: 1.
  • until: end date, e.g. 2026-12-31. Default: never ends.
  • weekly needs byweekday: the days of the week as a list, where 0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday, e.g. [0, 3].
  • monthly needs bydayno, the day of the month (1–31, or "last"), or byweekno, the week of the month (1–5, or "last"), with byweekday as a single day in that week, e.g. 1 for Tuesday. If both byweekno and bydayno are given, byweekno wins.
  • yearly needs bymonth, the month (1–12, 1 = January), plus what monthly needs.
  • dupsubtasks: whether to duplicate subtasks when the task is completed. Default: true.
  • sincelatest: with daily only, whether to repeat from the last completion date. Default: false.

A property that doesn't apply to freq is ignored; an invalid value, or a missing required one, is rejected with 400.

A recurring task always has a due. If the task has none and due is omitted, it is derived from the recurrence: the nearest occurrence since today. The request is rejected if the derived due precedes start; specify due explicitly in that case.

assignees: string[]

(Optional) Assignees to replace the current assignees (OID, ID, or email). This replaces all existing assignees. To modify incrementally, use addAssignees or removeAssignees.

Accepts the same special values as addAssignees: "me" (the current user) and "inherit" (all assignees of the parent task).

Only project members (external-team members included) can be assigned; anyone else is silently left out. An unknown user is rejected with 400.

asUser: boolean

(Optional) If true, marks this update as performed by the app. Read asUser as app-as-user: the app itself is the user, not the authorizing user. Default: false (updated by the authorizing user). In bulk-update, each item has its own.

followers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to replace the current followers (OID, ID, or email).

Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": include followers of the parent task
  • "app": the application follows (receives notifications)

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL (e.g., .../standard/soc1/33456/a7).

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

successors: string[]

(Optional) Successors to replace the current successors (task OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

start: string

(Optional) Start date/time in UTC.

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

Notes:

  • Seconds are not supported.
  • 2020-10-30T00:00:00 is treated as 2020-10-30 (date only).
  • To specify exactly midnight UTC, use 2020-10-30T00:00 (no seconds).
due: string

(Optional) Due date/time in UTC.

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

Notes:

  • Seconds are not supported.
  • 2020-10-30T00:00:00 is treated as 2020-10-30 (date only).
  • To specify exactly midnight UTC, use 2020-10-30T00:00 (no seconds).
  • null clears it. It is rejected if the task is recurring, since a recurring task always has a due; pass recurrence: null in the same request to stop repeating and clear the due together.
yourField: object

PLACEHOLDER — do NOT send a key literally named yourField. Instead, use the custom field's own name (as defined via /project/add-field) as the JSON key, with a value matching the field's type:

  • Text / Email / Hyperlink: string.
  • Number / Money: numeric value (no currency symbol).
  • Checkbox: true or false.
  • Select: option name (string).
  • Date: ISO 8601 timestamp (yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssZ) or date-only (yyyy-MM-dd).
  • Duration: number of seconds.
  • User: user OID, user ID, or email — server resolves to the user's OID.
  • Task: task OID, integer task ID, or #<id> string — server resolves to the task's OID (scoped to this project).
  • File: the attachment list as a task returns it (absolute url accepted); send an entry back unchanged to keep that file.
  • Multi-value (fields configured with multiple: true): provide a list. Pass null to clear the field.

A field you can't view or edit (the definition's viewMembers and editMembers) is rejected with 400; locked stops editing in Quire only, not through the API.

Example body fragment: {"Priority": 3, "Owners": ["alice", "bob@example.com"], "Depends": ["#42"]}.

peekaboo:
boolean
integer

(Optional) Peekaboo setting. Accepts a boolean or a positive integer:

  • true: Hide indefinitely (task and subtasks).
  • positive integer: Number of days to hide.
  • false: Undo previous peekaboo.
section: boolean

(Optional) true makes this task a section; false makes it a normal task. If both section and milestone are sent, only section is applied.

milestone: boolean

(Optional) true makes this task a milestone; false makes it a normal task. Ignored if section is sent too.

addTags: string[]

(Optional) Tags to add to this task (OID or name). Tag names are case-insensitive. Each must be an existing tag of the project, or a global tag of its organization; an unknown tag is rejected with 400, not created.

removeTags: string[]

(Optional) Tags to remove from this task (OID or name). Tag names are case-insensitive. An unknown tag is rejected with 400.

addAssignees: string[]

(Optional) Assignees to add (OID, ID, or email). Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": include all assignees of the parent task

Only project members (external-team members included) can be assigned; anyone else is silently left out. An unknown user is rejected with 400.

removeAssignees: string[]

(Optional) Assignees to remove (OID, ID, or email).

Accepts the same special values as addAssignees: "me" (the current user) and "inherit" (all assignees of the parent task).

addFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to add (OID, ID, or email). Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": include followers of the parent task
  • "app": the application follows (receives notifications)

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL (e.g., .../standard/soc1/33456/a7).

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

removeFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to remove (OID, ID, or email).

Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": remove followers that were inherited from the parent task
  • "app": the application

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL.

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

addSuccessors: string[]

(Optional) Successors to add (task OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

removeSuccessors: string[]

(Optional) Successors to remove (task OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

name: string

(Optional) New task name.

status: integer

(Optional) New status. Must be one of the project's status values (GET /status/list/id/{projectId} lists them); any other value is rejected with 400. Every project has 0, the initial status, and 100, completed; 100 or more means completed. Specify 100 to complete the task. Completion may be rejected (409 Conflict) when project settings require all predecessors to be completed first, or require an approval to be granted.

etc: integer

(Optional) Estimated time to complete, in seconds. Must be 0 to 864,000,000 (10,000 days) or null. Specify null to clear the value.

priority: integer -1, 0, 1, 2

(Optional) New priority: -1 Low, 0 Medium, 1 High, 2 Urgent. (The server also accepts the case-insensitive English names Low, Medium, High, Urgent, but the integer form is recommended for typed callers.)

sourceRef: object

(Optional) A JSON object your app stores with the task, such as where the task came from. Quire keeps it as is and returns it as sourceRef whenever the task is read.

  • text (optional): a Markdown string Quire shows as the task's source line in the task details. Include a link to the source, e.g. Source: [GitHub issue 42](https://github.com/acme/web/issues/42).
  • Any other key: your app's own data, not shown in Quire. Put it under a key named after your app, e.g. github, so it won't clash with another app's.
  • To find these tasks later, search with ?source-ref=github: it returns the tasks whose sourceRef has that key, whatever its value.

task

Bulk-remove N tasks from a project by ID.

DELETE /task/bulk-remove/id/{projectId}

Example: DELETE /task/bulk-remove/id/my_project

Removes up to 300 tasks, with their subtasks, in one transaction. Restore any of them with PUT /task/undo-remove/.... Body is a top-level JSON array of task references — each element is one of:

  • a task OID (string),
  • an integer task ID, or
  • a "#<id>" string (the ID-with-hash form).

Mixed forms in the same batch are allowed.

Request body (mixed forms — all three reference shapes in one batch):

[ 42, "#99", "iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo" ]

Response — always {oid} per item, whatever ?return= (slot 1 didn't resolve — already removed — so it's null):

[
  { "oid": "abc1Foo" },
  null,
  { "oid": "iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo" }
]

Atomic: a per-item validation, permission, or DB error rolls back the whole batch and returns {code, message} with an items[i]: prefix naming the offending item. Fix the value and retry.

Skip-not-found: a ref that doesn't resolve to a live task in the project (already removed, never existed, a mistyped OID, cascade-removed by an earlier item, etc.) is skipped — its response slot is null and the rest of the batch proceeds. This makes the endpoint idempotent for agents — safe to re-submit after a partial network failure without diffing state first. Only a ref that is neither a string nor an integer is rejected with 400. If the project itself doesn't exist, it returns 204 No Content with no body, like deleting a task.

Dry-run: pass ?dry-run=true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same per-item validation and permission checks as a real call; same response body shape on success and same {code, message} (with items[i]: prefix) on failure. A 200 from a dry-run is a strong signal that re-issuing the identical body without ?dry-run will succeed (subject to concurrent edits between the two calls). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

Rate-limit cost: 1 unit per item, charged upfront — for bulk-add, per task created, nested tasks included. ?dry-run=true costs ceil(N / 2) units (minimum 1). Skipped items are charged too. See Rate Limits.

Batch size: at most 300 items per call, and no more than the plan's per-minute rate limit — e.g. 50 on the Free plan, or 25 in a personal project on the Free plan (see Rate Limits). A batch over the plan's cap is rejected with 402 (code 469), one over 300 with 400; split it.

projectId: string
in path

Project ID. Specify - for your personal tasks (those in My Tasks that belong to no project).

dry-run: string true, false
in query

(Optional) Set to true to preview the call without persisting any changes. Same validation, permissions, and response shape as a real call, at half the rate-limit cost (ceil(N / 2) units). Only true, 1, or an empty value turns it on; any other value, even yes, makes a real write.

Request Example
[
  "object"
]
200 OK

OK — array of {oid} elements (slots for not-found items are null).

204 No Content

No Content — the project does not exist; nothing is removed. (Item-level not-found is silent skip.)

400 Bad Request
ErrorResponse

Bad Request — body not a JSON array, empty, over the 300-item cap, or any item is neither a string nor an integer (whole batch rolled back).

402 Payment Required
ErrorResponse

Payment Required (code 469) — the batch holds more items than the plan allows per call (see Batch size).

403 Forbidden
ErrorResponse

Forbidden — caller lacks permission on the project or any task in the batch (whole batch rolled back).

413 Request Entity Too Large
ErrorResponse

Payload Too Large — body exceeds the API packet size limit.

429 Too Many Requests
ErrorResponse

Too Many Requests — the caller's per-minute / per-hour API quota is already used up (see Rate Limits).

Response Content-Types: application/json
Response Example (200 OK) 
"object"
Response Example (400 Bad Request) 
{
  "code": 429,
  "message": "Something went wrong."
}
Response Example (402 Payment Required) 
{
  "code": 429,
  "message": "Something went wrong."
}
Response Example (403 Forbidden) 
{
  "code": 429,
  "message": "Something went wrong."
}
Response Example (413 Request Entity Too Large) 
{
  "code": 429,
  "message": "Something went wrong."
}
Response Example (429 Too Many Requests) 
{
  "code": 429,
  "message": "Something went wrong."
}

task

Remove a time log from a task by ID.

DELETE /task/remove-timelog/id/{projectId}/{taskId}

Removes the time log identified by the (user, start, end) triple from the task. Sub-second precision in the query params is truncated to whole seconds before matching.

On success returns the task's remaining timelogs array (empty when no logs remain). If the project hides time logs from guests (its default), a guest member or a non-member gets an empty array, as timelogs is omitted from the task records they get. Example after removing the only log:

[]

Note: Like deleting a task, returns 204 No Content if the task or the project doesn't exist, or the task has been deleted. Nothing is changed. Unlike deleting a task, it returns 404 if the task exists but no log matches the triple.

projectId: string
in path

Project ID.

taskId: integer
in path

Task ID.

start: string
in query

Start timestamp of the log to remove. ISO 8601, UTC.

end: string
in query

End timestamp of the log to remove. ISO 8601, UTC.

user: string
in query

(Optional) User the existing log is credited to (OID, ID, or email). Omitted defaults to the authenticated caller.

200 OK
Timelog

OK — task's remaining timelogs array (empty when none remain).

204 No Content

No Content — the task doesn't exist, or has been deleted; nothing is changed.

400 Bad Request

Bad Request — start / end query params missing or malformed, end precedes start, or user is unknown.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the caller can't change this task's time logs (checked before the log is looked up).

404 Not Found

Not Found — no log matches the triple.

Response Content-Types: application/json
Response Example (200 OK) 
[
  {
    "start": "2023-02-20T00:00:00.000Z",
    "end": "2023-02-20T00:05:35.000Z",
    "user": {
      "url": "https://quire.io/u/my_id",
      "id": "my_id",
      "iconColor": "37",
      "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",
      "name": "Foo",
      "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
    },
    "billable": true,
    "note": "A piece of cake"
  }
]

task

Cancel a task's approval.

DELETE /task/revoke-approval/id/{projectId}/{taskId}

Revokes the task's current approval. The effect depends on the current state:

  • approved / rejected → rolls the decision back to awaiting. Only an approver of the category can do it; the caller becomes the approval's approver, and the original requester is preserved. The approval can then be decided again via POST /task/approve/....
  • awaiting / changes → clears the approval entirely. Only the requester can do it, and only while a claimer of the category; once the requester has left the project, any claimer can.

A category's approvers and claimers are its approvers / claimers: anyone in the project if unset, admins only if [], or the listed users. Anyone else gets 403.

Idempotent: returns 204 No Content even when no approval is set, or the task doesn't exist.

projectId: string
in path

Project ID.

taskId: integer
in path

Task ID.

204 No Content

No Content — approval revoked (or already absent).

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the caller can't revoke this approval (see the rules above).

Response Content-Types: application/json
task

  • awaiting / changes → clears the approval entirely. Only the requester can do it, and only while a claimer of the category; once the requester has left the project, any claimer can.

user

Represents a Quire account that can access organizations, projects, and tasks.

user

Get a user by ID or email address.

GET /user/id/{id}

Returns the full user record for the given user ID, email address, or "me" (the current user). A colleague (someone sharing an organization, project or external team with the user) who hasn't authorized this app is returned with only oid, id and the name fields, unless the user granted the app access to contacts. Anyone else returns 403.

id: string
in path

User ID, email address, or "me".

200 OK
User

OK — user record.

403 Forbidden

Forbidden — the user is neither the current user nor a colleague.

404 Not Found

Not Found — user does not exist.

Get all user records.

GET /user/list

Returns all colleagues of the current user if the user granted the app access to contacts. Otherwise, returns only colleagues who also authorized the same app. If the user did not grant contact access and none of the user’s colleagues authorized this app, only the current user is returned. The first record is always the current user.

200 OK
User

OK — list of user records; first entry is always the current user.

Schema Definitions

AddAppvCatBody: object

claimers: string[]

(Optional) Users allowed to request approval in this category.

  • Omit or null: anyone can request.
  • [] (empty list): admins only.
  • List of user OIDs: those specific users.
string
approvers: string[]

(Optional) Users allowed to approve, reject, or request changes in this category.

  • Omit or null: anyone can respond.
  • [] (empty list): admins only.
  • List of user OIDs: those specific users.
string
name: string

Display name.

id: string

Category identifier (URL-safe). Must be unique within the project. The identifier "" is reserved for the implicit default category.

Example
{
  "claimers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "approvers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "name": "Legal Review",
  "id": "legal"
}

AddFieldBody: object

currency: string

(Optional, money/formula only) Currency symbol. When omitted on a money field, defaults to $.

percent: boolean

(Optional, number only) Format the value as a percentage.

private: boolean

(Optional) Hide this field and its values from guests and from the visitors of a public project or of a share link. A choice only without viewMembers; with it, the field is always hidden from them, so false is rejected with 400.

lookup: object

(Optional, lookup only) Map from lookup key to numeric value. Keys are OIDs of the configured lookupType entity (e.g. user OIDs when lookupType=User). Values are numbers.

options: FieldOption

(Optional, select only) Options, each an object with name and an optional color — not a plain string. Example: [{"name": "High", "color": "13"}, {"name": "Low"}].

FieldOption
hidden: boolean

(Optional) Hide this field from the task detail panel.

clearOnDup: boolean

(Optional) Clear this field when duplicating a task.

viewMembers: string[]

(Optional) Users who can view this field's values; an admin not named sees the definition, not the values. Each entry is a user ID, OID, or email, or "me" for the authenticated user, and must be a member of the field's owner, an external team's member included. Pass [] for the admins only, or null for everyone private allows.

string
editMembers: string[]

(Optional) Users who can edit the values, in the same form as viewMembers; an admin not named can't. Editing also requires viewing the field. Pass [] for the admins only, or null for anyone who can edit the task. locked stops editing in Quire regardless of this list; the API ignores the lock, so this list still applies to API writes.

string
locked: boolean

(Optional) Lock the values: no one can edit them in Quire, admins included, while the API still can, e.g., to push values from another system.

withTime: boolean

(Optional, date only) Include time-of-day in addition to the date.

ndecimal: integer -1, 0, 1, 2, 3

(Optional, number/money only) Number of decimal digits. -1 means no rounding.

durationFormat: string hh:mm:ss, hh:mm, 1h1m, 1h, 1d1h, dd:hh:mm:ss, dd:hh:mm, dd:hh

(Optional, duration/formula only) Duration display format.

formula: string

(Optional, formula only) Formula expression, at most 5,120 characters.

resultType: string text, number, money, date, duration, checkbox

(Optional, formula only) Expected result type.

lookupType: string User, Task, Project, Organization

(Optional, lookup only) Source type for lookup keys. Default: User.

multiple: boolean

(Optional) Allow multiple values. Applies to select, user, task, and file (always true for file).

conditionFormat: FieldConditionFormat

(Optional) Conditional-format rules. Applicable to date, number, money, duration, lookup, and formula fields whose resultType resolves to one of those.

FieldConditionFormat
name: string

Unique name for this field. Must be a non-empty string of at most 1,280 characters, and must not contain }, ", or \.

type: string text, number, money, date, duration, select, checkbox, user, task, hyperlink, email, formula, file, lookup

Field type. A project's field is one of text, number, money, date, duration, select, checkbox, user, task, hyperlink, email, formula and file; an insight's field is formula or lookup. A key for another type, such as options on a number field, returns 400.

Example
{
  "currency": "USD",
  "percent": false,
  "private": false,
  "lookup": "object",
  "options": [
    {
      "color": "13",
      "name": "High"
    }
  ],
  "hidden": false,
  "clearOnDup": false,
  "viewMembers": "[\"me\", \"john\"]",
  "editMembers": "[\"me\"]",
  "locked": false,
  "withTime": false,
  "ndecimal": 2,
  "durationFormat": "hh:mm",
  "formula": "SUM(Subtask.Amount)",
  "resultType": "number",
  "lookupType": "User",
  "multiple": true,
  "conditionFormat": [
    {
      "color": "42",
      "second": "200",
      "when": "today",
      "op": ">=",
      "first": "#/definitions/Number"
    }
  ],
  "name": "Priority",
  "type": "number"
}

AddTimelogBody: object

end: string

End timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC). Must be on or after start. Sub-second precision is truncated to whole seconds.

start: string

Start timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC). Sub-second precision is truncated to whole seconds.

user: string

(Optional) User identifier (OID, ID, or email) the log is credited to. Omitted, null, or empty defaults to the authenticated caller. Unknown users return 400 Bad Request.

billable: boolean

(Optional) Whether this log is billable. Omitted or null defaults to true.

note: string

(Optional) Free-form note for the log. Omitted, null, or empty stores no note.

Example
{
  "end": "2026-04-26T10:30:00Z",
  "start": "2026-04-26T09:00:00Z",
  "user": "john.doe@example.com",
  "billable": true,
  "note": "Pair-programming session"
}

Approval: object

toggledAt: string

Timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601) of the last state transition.

category: string

Identifier of the approval category this approval belongs to. The default category has id "".

requester: string

OID of the user who originally requested approval. Preserved across subsequent approve / reject / change transitions.

For ID-based access, prefer requesterRef, which returns {oid, id}.

approver: string

OID of the user who most recently approved / rejected / requested changes — or, after a revoke rolled that decision back to awaiting, the user who revoked it. Omitted after a request.

For ID-based access, prefer approverRef, which returns {oid, id}.

requesterRef: SimpleEntityWithId

Requester as {oid, id} — same shape as ?return=compact. Recommended over requester for callers using ID-based access.

approverRef: SimpleEntityWithId

Approver as {oid, id} — same shape as ?return=compact. Recommended over approver for callers using ID-based access. Present when approver is.

state: string awaiting, approved, rejected, changes

Current approval state. Derived from the last POST to /task/approve/id/{projectId}/{taskId} (or the OID form):

  • awaiting — request was posted (initial or rolled-back).
  • approved — approve was posted.
  • rejected — reject was posted.
  • changes — change (request-for-changes) was posted.
Example
{
  "toggledAt": "2026-04-24T10:05:00.000Z",
  "category": "legal",
  "requester": "string",
  "approver": "string",
  "requesterRef": {
    "id": "my_id",
    "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
  },
  "approverRef": "#/definitions/SimpleEntityWithId",
  "state": "awaiting"
}

ApproveTaskBody: object

description: string

Content of the companion comment (Markdown supported). An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead. Required if the body is supplied. The server prepends a <category>: <status> line (status in the authorizing user's language; no category name for the default category) and a blank line before this text, so this field should contain only the human-written message — do not include the header yourself.

asUser: boolean

(Optional) If true, the comment is attributed to the app rather than the authorizing user ( app-as-user, as the asUser flag on POST /comment). Default: false. Either way, the authorizing user, not the app, follows the task, as for any comment.

pinned: boolean

(Optional) Whether to pin the companion comment on the task. Default: false.

Example
{
  "description": "Please tweak the wording.",
  "asUser": false,
  "pinned": false
}

AppvCat: object

name: string

Display name.

id: string

Category identifier (URL-safe). The implicit default category has an empty id.

claimers: string[]

Users allowed to request approval in this category.

  • Omitted from the response: anyone can request.
  • [] (empty list): admins only.
  • List of user OIDs: those specific users.

For ID-based access, prefer claimerRefs, which returns {oid, id} pairs.

string
approvers: string[]

Users allowed to approve, reject, or request changes in this category.

  • Omitted from the response: anyone can respond.
  • [] (empty list): admins only.
  • List of user OIDs: those specific users.

For ID-based access, prefer approverRefs, which returns {oid, id} pairs.

string
claimerRefs: SimpleEntityWithId

Claimers as {oid, id} pairs — same shape as ?return=compact. Recommended over claimers for callers using ID-based access. Tri-state semantics match claimers: omitted = anyone; [] = admins only; list = those specific users.

SimpleEntityWithId
approverRefs: SimpleEntityWithId

Approvers as {oid, id} pairs — same shape as ?return=compact. Recommended over approvers for callers using ID-based access. Tri-state semantics match approvers.

SimpleEntityWithId
createdAt: string

Timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601) when this category was created.

createdBy: SimpleIdentity

User who created this category.

Example
{
  "name": "Legal Review",
  "id": "legal",
  "claimers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "approvers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "claimerRefs": [
    {
      "id": "my_id",
      "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
    }
  ],
  "approverRefs": [
    "#/definitions/SimpleEntityWithId"
  ],
  "createdAt": "2026-04-24T10:00:00.000Z",
  "createdBy": {
    "url": "https://quire.io/u/my_id",
    "id": "my_id",
    "iconColor": "37",
    "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",
    "name": "Foo",
    "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
  }
}

Attachment: object

type: integer

Where the attachment is stored: 1 Google Drive, 2 Quire storage, 3 OneDrive, 4 Dropbox, 5 Box.

url: string

Absolute URL of this attachment. A file stored in Quire is under https://quire.io/att/; a file from an external storage, such as Google Drive, links to that service.

length: integer

Size of the attachment in bytes.

name: string

File name of the attachment.

createdAt: string

Creation timestamp in UTC (ISO 8601).

createdBy: SimpleIdentity

User who created this record.

Example
{
  "type": 2,
  "url": "https://quire.io/att/Ta/sdcQOGgeUtyaFFzb9p0IwAgi/qfqVmUtC/image.png",
  "length": 20000,
  "name": "file.txt",
  "createdAt": "2018-12-22T02:06:58.158Z",
  "createdBy": {
    "url": "https://quire.io/u/my_id",
    "id": "my_id",
    "iconColor": "37",
    "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",
    "name": "Foo",
    "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
  }
}

BulkUpdateTaskItem: object

oid: string

Target task OID. Exactly one of oid / id must be supplied per item; both or neither is rejected with 400. If it doesn't match a live task in the project, the item is skipped and its response slot is null.

id: integer

Target task ID, an integer; a "#42" string works too. Exactly one of oid / id must be supplied per item; both or neither is rejected with 400. If it doesn't match a live task in the project, the item is skipped and its response slot is null.

description: string

(Optional) New task description. An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

tags: string[]

(Optional) Tags to replace the current tags on this task (OID or name). This replaces all existing tags. To modify incrementally, use addTags or removeTags. Tag names are case-insensitive. Each must be an existing tag of the project, or a global tag of its organization; an unknown tag is rejected with 400, not created.

string
partner: string

(Optional) The external team to share this task with: the name or OID of one of the project's external teams (GET /partner/list/id/{projectId} lists them). The team's members then get access to the task and its subtasks. Setting it takes the right to assign tasks (403 otherwise). A name or OID that matches no team, or a value that isn't a string, is rejected with 400. The API can't remove it: null is rejected too.

recurrence: Recurrence

(Optional) Makes the task repeat, replacing its current recurrence, if any. null stops it repeating.

  • freq (required): daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.
  • interval: a positive integer; 2 with weekly means every 2 weeks. Default: 1.
  • until: end date, e.g. 2026-12-31. Default: never ends.
  • weekly needs byweekday: the days of the week as a list, where 0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday, e.g. [0, 3].
  • monthly needs bydayno, the day of the month (1–31, or "last"), or byweekno, the week of the month (1–5, or "last"), with byweekday as a single day in that week, e.g. 1 for Tuesday. If both byweekno and bydayno are given, byweekno wins.
  • yearly needs bymonth, the month (1–12, 1 = January), plus what monthly needs.
  • dupsubtasks: whether to duplicate subtasks when the task is completed. Default: true.
  • sincelatest: with daily only, whether to repeat from the last completion date. Default: false.

A property that doesn't apply to freq is ignored; an invalid value, or a missing required one, is rejected with 400.

A recurring task always has a due. If the task has none and due is omitted, it is derived from the recurrence: the nearest occurrence since today. The request is rejected if the derived due precedes start; specify due explicitly in that case.

assignees: string[]

(Optional) Assignees to replace the current assignees (OID, ID, or email). This replaces all existing assignees. To modify incrementally, use addAssignees or removeAssignees.

Accepts the same special values as addAssignees: "me" (the current user) and "inherit" (all assignees of the parent task).

Only project members (external-team members included) can be assigned; anyone else is silently left out. An unknown user is rejected with 400.

string
asUser: boolean

(Optional) If true, marks this update as performed by the app. Read asUser as app-as-user: the app itself is the user, not the authorizing user. Default: false (updated by the authorizing user). In bulk-update, each item has its own.

followers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to replace the current followers (OID, ID, or email).

Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": include followers of the parent task
  • "app": the application follows (receives notifications)

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL (e.g., .../standard/soc1/33456/a7).

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

string
successors: string[]

(Optional) Successors to replace the current successors (task OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

string
start: string

(Optional) Start date/time in UTC.

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

Notes:

  • Seconds are not supported.
  • 2020-10-30T00:00:00 is treated as 2020-10-30 (date only).
  • To specify exactly midnight UTC, use 2020-10-30T00:00 (no seconds).
due: string

(Optional) Due date/time in UTC.

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

Notes:

  • Seconds are not supported.
  • 2020-10-30T00:00:00 is treated as 2020-10-30 (date only).
  • To specify exactly midnight UTC, use 2020-10-30T00:00 (no seconds).
  • null clears it. It is rejected if the task is recurring, since a recurring task always has a due; pass recurrence: null in the same request to stop repeating and clear the due together.
yourField: object

PLACEHOLDER — do NOT send a key literally named yourField. Instead, use the custom field's own name (as defined via /project/add-field) as the JSON key, with a value matching the field's type:

  • Text / Email / Hyperlink: string.
  • Number / Money: numeric value (no currency symbol).
  • Checkbox: true or false.
  • Select: option name (string).
  • Date: ISO 8601 timestamp (yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssZ) or date-only (yyyy-MM-dd).
  • Duration: number of seconds.
  • User: user OID, user ID, or email — server resolves to the user's OID.
  • Task: task OID, integer task ID, or #<id> string — server resolves to the task's OID (scoped to this project).
  • File: the attachment list as a task returns it (absolute url accepted); send an entry back unchanged to keep that file.
  • Multi-value (fields configured with multiple: true): provide a list. Pass null to clear the field.

A field you can't view or edit (the definition's viewMembers and editMembers) is rejected with 400; locked stops editing in Quire only, not through the API.

Example body fragment: {"Priority": 3, "Owners": ["alice", "bob@example.com"], "Depends": ["#42"]}.

peekaboo: object

(Optional) Peekaboo setting. Accepts a boolean or a positive integer:

  • true: Hide indefinitely (task and subtasks).
  • positive integer: Number of days to hide.
  • false: Undo previous peekaboo.
section: boolean

(Optional) true makes this task a section; false makes it a normal task. If both section and milestone are sent, only section is applied.

milestone: boolean

(Optional) true makes this task a milestone; false makes it a normal task. Ignored if section is sent too.

addTags: string[]

(Optional) Tags to add to this task (OID or name). Tag names are case-insensitive. Each must be an existing tag of the project, or a global tag of its organization; an unknown tag is rejected with 400, not created.

string
removeTags: string[]

(Optional) Tags to remove from this task (OID or name). Tag names are case-insensitive. An unknown tag is rejected with 400.

string
addAssignees: string[]

(Optional) Assignees to add (OID, ID, or email). Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": include all assignees of the parent task

Only project members (external-team members included) can be assigned; anyone else is silently left out. An unknown user is rejected with 400.

string
removeAssignees: string[]

(Optional) Assignees to remove (OID, ID, or email).

Accepts the same special values as addAssignees: "me" (the current user) and "inherit" (all assignees of the parent task).

string
addFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to add (OID, ID, or email). Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": include followers of the parent task
  • "app": the application follows (receives notifications)

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL (e.g., .../standard/soc1/33456/a7).

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

string
removeFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to remove (OID, ID, or email).

Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": remove followers that were inherited from the parent task
  • "app": the application

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL.

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

string
addSuccessors: string[]

(Optional) Successors to add (task OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

string
removeSuccessors: string[]

(Optional) Successors to remove (task OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

string
name: string

(Optional) New task name.

status: integer

(Optional) New status. Must be one of the project's status values (GET /status/list/id/{projectId} lists them); any other value is rejected with 400. Every project has 0, the initial status, and 100, completed; 100 or more means completed. Specify 100 to complete the task. Completion may be rejected (409 Conflict) when project settings require all predecessors to be completed first, or require an approval to be granted.

etc: integer

(Optional) Estimated time to complete, in seconds. Must be 0 to 864,000,000 (10,000 days) or null. Specify null to clear the value.

priority: integer -1, 0, 1, 2

(Optional) New priority: -1 Low, 0 Medium, 1 High, 2 Urgent. (The server also accepts the case-insensitive English names Low, Medium, High, Urgent, but the integer form is recommended for typed callers.)

sourceRef: object

(Optional) A JSON object your app stores with the task, such as where the task came from. Quire keeps it as is and returns it as sourceRef whenever the task is read.

  • text (optional): a Markdown string Quire shows as the task's source line in the task details. Include a link to the source, e.g. Source: [GitHub issue 42](https://github.com/acme/web/issues/42).
  • Any other key: your app's own data, not shown in Quire. Put it under a key named after your app, e.g. github, so it won't clash with another app's.
  • To find these tasks later, search with ?source-ref=github: it returns the tasks whose sourceRef has that key, whatever its value.
  • Size: at most about 2,048 characters, keys and values together, and text must be a string; otherwise 400.
  • It replaces the stored object as a whole: keys you leave out are removed, and null removes sourceRef. Another app may have stored its own key on the task; to keep it, read the task first and send that key back.
Example
{
  "oid": "iuRRiKoyrxdBFhFTTo",
  "id": 42,
  "description": "This is a **cool** task.",
  "tags": "[\"urgent\", \"design\"]",
  "partner": "UI design team",
  "recurrence": {
    "freq": "weekly",
    "interval": 1,
    "byweekday": "[1,3]",
    "byweekno": 2,
    "bydayno": 25,
    "bymonth": 10,
    "dupsubtasks": false,
    "sincelatest": true,
    "until": "2020-12-22"
  },
  "assignees": "[\"me\", \"alice@example.com\"]",
  "asUser": true,
  "followers": "[\"bob@example.com\"]",
  "successors": "[\"#13\"]",
  "start": "2026-05-01",
  "due": "2026-05-10T17:00Z",
  "yourField": "object",
  "peekaboo": "true",
  "section": true,
  "milestone": true,
  "addTags": "[\"urgent\"]",
  "removeTags": "[\"draft\"]",
  "addAssignees": "[\"me\"]",
  "removeAssignees": "[\"alice@example.com\"]",
  "addFollowers": "[\"me\"]",
  "removeFollowers": "[\"bob@example.com\"]",
  "addSuccessors": "[\"#13\"]",
  "removeSuccessors": "[\"#13\"]",
  "name": "New idea",
  "status": 100,
  "etc": 0,
  "priority": 0,
  "sourceRef": "{\"github\": {\"repo\": \"acme/web\", \"issue\": 42}, \"text\": \"Source: [GitHub issue 42](https://github.com/acme/web/issues/42)\"}"
}

Change: object

task: string

OID of the task to include or exclude. A task is skipped if it doesn't exist, if it isn't under the sublist's owner, or, for a sublist shared with an external team, if it isn't shared with that team.

exclude: boolean

Whether to exclude the task. Default: false (include).

single: boolean

Whether the operation applies only to the specified task. Default: false — the task and all its descendants are included or excluded, and earlier includes or excludes of its descendants are cleared. With true, only the task itself changes; its subtasks keep their current state.

Example
{
  "task": "2MmYOpJH_ZLeehIjjytH1Rwr",
  "exclude": false,
  "single": false
}

Chat: object

url: string

URL of this chat on the Quire website.

nameHtml: string

Name rendered as an HTML fragment converted from Markdown.

nameText: string

Name with Markdown removed.

name: string

Display name (Markdown supported).

id: string

ID.

description: string

Description (Markdown supported).

descriptionHtml: string

Description rendered as an HTML fragment converted from Markdown.

descriptionText: string

Description with Markdown removed.

iconColor: string

Color index for the icon from Quire’s predefined palette. Two-digit code: first digit 0–5, second digit 0–7 (e.g., 37).

image: string

Image URL representing this record.

oid: string

Object identifier (OID), a UUID-like unique string.

partner: SimpleTaggingEntity

External team this record is shared with. Omitted if none.

archivedAt: string

Timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601) when this record was archived. Omitted if not archived.

followers: SimpleIdentity

The list of users following this chat channel.

SimpleIdentity
mutes: SimpleIdentity

The list of users who have muted this chat channel and will not receive notifications about it.

SimpleIdentity
members: SimpleIdentity

Users who can see this record, and the only ones it is shown to.

  • null — every member of the owner can see it; private tells whether guests and the visitors of a public project or of a share link can too.
  • [] — only the owner's admins can.
  • a list — only those users can.

All three are returned explicitly, so the states can be told apart. Set it when creating the record; it cannot be changed afterwards.

SimpleIdentity
private: boolean

Whether this record is hidden from guests and from the visitors of a public project or of a share link, like a custom field's private. Present only when members is null and partner is null — the one case where it is a choice. A record shared with an external team, with selected members or with the admins only is always hidden from them.

owner: ChatOwner

Project this chat channel belongs to.

createdAt: string

Creation timestamp in UTC (ISO 8601).

createdBy: SimpleIdentity

User who created this record.

Example
{
  "url": "https://quire.io/w/my_project?chat=Highlight101",
  "nameHtml": "Highlight 101",
  "nameText": "Highlight 101",
  "name": "Highlight 101",
  "id": "Highlight101",
  "description": "This is *cool*!",
  "descriptionHtml": "This is <i>cool</i>!",
  "descriptionText": "This is cool!",
  "iconColor": "37",
  "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",
  "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld",
  "partner": {
    "color": "35",
    "name": "Foo",
    "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
  },
  "archivedAt": "2020-02-22T02:06:58.158Z",
  "followers": [
    {
      "url": "https://quire.io/u/my_id",
      "id": "my_id",
      "iconColor": "37",
      "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",
      "name": "Foo",
      "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
    }
  ],
  "mutes": [
    "#/definitions/SimpleIdentity"
  ],
  "members": [
    "#/definitions/SimpleIdentity"
  ],
  "private": true,
  "owner": {
    "url": "https://quire.io/w/prj_id",
    "type": "Project",
    "id": "my_id",
    "iconColor": "37",
    "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",
    "name": "Foo",
    "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
  },
  "createdAt": "2018-12-22T02:06:58.158Z",
  "createdBy": "#/definitions/SimpleIdentity"
}

Comment: object

oid: string

Object identifier (OID), a UUID-like unique string.

description: string

Comment content (Markdown supported).

descriptionHtml: string

Comment content rendered as an HTML fragment converted from Markdown.

descriptionText: string

Comment content with Markdown removed.

attachments: Attachment

Attachments associated with this comment.

Attachment
emojis: CommentEmoji

Emoji reactions to this comment, in the order they were first added. Omitted if none. To add or remove the caller's reactions, use POST /comment/add-emoji/{commentOid}/{emojis} and DELETE /comment/remove-emoji/{commentOid}/{emojis}.

CommentEmoji
url: string

URL of this comment on the Quire website.

editedAt: string

Timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601) when this comment was last edited. Omitted if never edited.

pinAt: string

Timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601) when this comment was pinned. Omitted if not pinned.

pinBy: SimpleIdentity

User who pinned this comment. Omitted if not pinned.

editedBy: SimpleIdentity

User who last edited this comment. Omitted if never edited.

owner: CommentOwner

Task or chat channel this comment was added to.

createdAt: string

Creation timestamp in UTC (ISO 8601).

createdBy: SimpleIdentity

User who created this record.

Example
{
  "oid": "iDsPd.QP_qM.hN.Trymukn8b",
  "description": "It is *cool*!",
  "descriptionHtml": "It is <i>cool</i>!",
  "descriptionText": "It is cool!",
  "attachments": [
    {
      "type": 2,
      "url": "https://quire.io/att/Ta/sdcQOGgeUtyaFFzb9p0IwAgi/qfqVmUtC/image.png",
      "length": 20000,
      "name": "file.txt",
      "createdAt": "2018-12-22T02:06:58.158Z",
      "createdBy": {
        "url": "https://quire.io/u/my_id",
        "id": "my_id",
        "iconColor": "37",
        "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",
        "name": "Foo",
        "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
      }
    }
  ],
  "emojis": [
    {
      "emoji": "👍",
      "users": [
        "#/definitions/SimpleIdentity"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "url": "string",
  "editedAt": "2018-12-22T02:06:58.158Z",
  "pinAt": "2018-12-22T02:06:58.158Z",
  "pinBy": "#/definitions/SimpleIdentity",
  "editedBy": "#/definitions/SimpleIdentity",
  "owner": {
    "url": "https://quire.io/w/my_project/42",
    "id": "42",
    "type": "Task",
    "name": "Foo",
    "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
  },
  "createdAt": "2018-12-22T02:06:58.158Z",
  "createdBy": "#/definitions/SimpleIdentity"
}

CommentEmoji: object

An emoji reaction to a comment, with the users who reacted with it.

emoji: string

The emoji, as a Unicode character. To add or remove it, pass this character or its name (see Emojis) to POST /comment/add-emoji/{commentOid}/{emojis} or DELETE /comment/remove-emoji/{commentOid}/{emojis}.

users: SimpleIdentity

Users who reacted with this emoji.

SimpleIdentity
Example
{
  "emoji": "👍",
  "users": [
    {
      "url": "https://quire.io/u/my_id",
      "id": "my_id",
      "iconColor": "37",
      "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",
      "name": "Foo",
      "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
    }
  ]
}

CommentOwner: object

url: string

URL of this owner on the Quire website.

id: object

ID of the owner: for a task, its ID (an integer, unique within its project); for a chat channel, its ID (a string).

type: string Task, Chat

Type of the owner: Task or Chat.

name: string

Display name.

oid: string

Object identifier (OID), a UUID-like unique string.

Example
{
  "url": "https://quire.io/w/my_project/42",
  "id": "42",
  "type": "Task",
  "name": "Foo",
  "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
}

CreateChatBody: object

followers: string[]

(Optional) Users (OID, ID, or email) who follow this chat channel. Only those listed follow it, so include "me" for the current user to follow.

  • "me" — the current user.
  • "app" — the application follows (receives notifications).

For app followers, additional syntaxes are supported:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL.
string
description: string

(Optional) Description of the record (Markdown supported). An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

iconColor: string

(Optional) Icon color index from Quire's predefined palette. Two-digit code [0-5][0-7]: first digit 0-5, second digit 0-7 (e.g. 00, 37, 57). NOT a CSS hex color.

image: string icon-view-list, icon-view-kanban, icon-grid, icon-view-timeline, icon-calendar, icon-timer, icon-briefcase-o, icon-rocket-o, icon-bug-o, icon-user-o, icon-colleagues-o, icon-lightbulb-o, icon-leaf-o, icon-clapperboard, icon-sitemap-o, icon-list, icon-flash-on-o, icon-piggy-bank-o, icon-graduation-cap-o, icon-paper-plane-o, icon-globe-o, icon-music-o, icon-detail, icon-beach-o, icon-paper, icon-home-o, icon-building, icon-database-o, icon-microscope-o, icon-hamburger-o, icon-trophy-o, icon-thumbs-o-up, icon-thumbs-o-down, icon-smile-o, icon-frown-o, icon-meh-o, icon-bullseye, icon-incomplete, icon-filter-o, icon-comment, icon-view-insight, icon-view-dashboard, icon-square-dotted-o

(Optional) Icon image identifier, one of the listed values.

name: string

Display name of the record (Markdown supported).

id: string

(Optional) ID for this record, unique among the owner's records of the same kind (e.g. a project's sublists). If omitted or invalid, Quire derives one from name; if already taken, Quire changes it by appending characters. Neither is an error, so read the id back from the response.

partner: string

(Optional) OID of the external team to share this record with; it is then shared with the members of the project and of that team, and is always private.

Only a project's record can carry one — an organization, a folder or a smart folder has no external team — and it must be one of the project's external teams; any other value is 400. It cannot be combined with members either (400).

An external team member shares a record with every member only through their own team: with members omitted or null, they must set partner to one of their teams. Otherwise 400 names their teams, as it does for a team of the project that isn't theirs.

Settable only when creating the record.

private: boolean

(Optional) Hide this record from guests and from the visitors of a public project or of a share link, like a custom field's private. A choice only when members is null and partner is null; defaults to false (everyone). Otherwise it is always true: a record shared with an external team, with selected members or with the admins only is hidden from them, so false is rejected with 400.

members: string[]

(Optional) Users who can see this record, and the only ones it is shown to. Each entry is a user ID, OID, or email, or "me" for the authenticated user.

  • Omit the field, or pass null — every member of the owner can see it, and so can guests and the visitors of a public project or of a share link unless private. This is the default. (A reminder differs: omitting its members means only the authenticated user.) An external team member must also set partner to one of their teams.
  • Pass [] — only the owner's admins can see it.
  • Pass a list — only those users can see it.

Rejected with 400 when:

  • a listed user is not a member of the owner. Unlike a task's assignees, which silently drops a non-member, this is an error: dropping the last one would leave [], which means something else entirely.
  • the list is non-empty and does not include the authenticated user — you would not be able to see what you just created.
  • partner is also set, since an external-team record is already shared with all members of the project and of the team.

Settable only when creating the record. It cannot be changed afterwards, so recreate the record to change who can see it.

string
Example
{
  "followers": "[\"me\"]",
  "description": "**Great** record to start with.",
  "iconColor": "37",
  "image": "icon-view-kanban",
  "name": "Highlight 101",
  "id": "Highlight101",
  "partner": "rcBHBYXZSiyDRrHrWPutatfF",
  "private": false,
  "members": "[\"me\", \"john\"]"
}

CreateCommentBody: object

description: string

Content of the new comment (Markdown supported). An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

asUser: boolean

(Optional) If true, marks this comment as created by the app. Read asUser as app-as-user: the app itself is the user, not the authorizing user. Default: false (created by the authorizing user). Either way, the authorizing user, not the app, follows the task or chat commented on.

pinned: boolean

(Optional) Whether to pin this comment. Default: false.

Example
{
  "description": "Adjust style",
  "asUser": true,
  "pinned": false
}

CreateNotificationBody: object

url: string

(Optional) URL associated with the message. When provided, the client may render the message as a hyperlink.

A javascript: URL is rejected with 400. Without a scheme, such as example.com/sync, https:// is assumed; a path starting with / points into Quire.

recipients: string[]

(Optional) Recipients of the notification (OID, ID, or email of a user). Omit or send an empty list to notify only the authorizing user (default).

Each entry must be the authorizing user or a colleague visible to this app — exactly the set returned by GET /user/list. Entries that do not exist or are not visible are rejected with 404 Not Found; the response is identical regardless of the reason, so this endpoint cannot be used to probe whether a user exists.

Special value:

  • ["*"] — broadcast to every user visible to this app (same set as GET /user/list, including the authorizing user). * must be the sole entry; mixing it with other entries returns 400 Bad Request.

Rate-limit cost: one unit per 10 recipients, rounded up (at least 1), counted after * is expanded. A call made once the caller's per-minute or per-hour API budget is used up is rejected with 429 Too Many Requests and no notification is sent.

string
message: string

Notification message. Required; an empty one is rejected with 400.

Example
{
  "url": "https://superheros.com/sync",
  "recipients": "[\"bob@example.com\"]",
  "message": "Unable to synchronize"
}

CreateReminderBody: object

when: string

When this reminder fires (UTC, ISO 8601). A plain instant — there is no all-day reminder, so a bare date is midnight UTC.

Required for a reminder that has no task, or whose task has neither a start nor a due date.

Rejected with 400 when the task already has a start or due date: the reminder then fires from the task's own schedule, and a when of its own would be ignored. Send leads alone in that case.

recurrence: Recurrence

(Optional) How this reminder repeats; when is the first occurrence.

Rejected with 400 on a reminder whose task has a start or due date — it then repeats with its task's schedule, so a rule of its own would be ignored.

leads: ReminderLead

(Optional) When to notify before the fire time, one notification each. Omit it for a single notification at the fire time, which is the default ([{"minutes": 0}]).

Each entry is an object naming exactly one of minutes (an absolute offset) and days (calendar days, so a lead spanning a daylight-saving transition keeps its wall-clock time), the latter taking an optional at clock.

Neither may be negative — a lead counts back from the fire time, and nothing fires after it — nor exceed 10,000 days ahead of it, and there may be at most 30 of them.

ReminderLead
name: string

(Optional) Text to show instead of the default message. Only inline Markdown applies: **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, `code` and links; anything else, such as a list or a heading, stays literal text. At most 1,280 characters, not counting the markup (400 otherwise).

partner: string

(Optional) OID of the external team to share this reminder with; it then reaches every member of the project and of that team.

Only a project's reminder can carry one, and it cannot be combined with a members list ([] included) — both are 400. Without a task, it must be one of the project's external teams (400 otherwise). On a reminder attached to a task, it must be the team the task is shared with — the task's partner, or the nearest parent task's if it has none — or be omitted; any other value, and any value for a task not shared with a team, is 400.

An external team member shares a reminder with every member only through their own team. With members null, they must set partner to one of their teams; on a reminder attached to a task, that is the task's team. Otherwise 400 says what to send, as it does for a team of the project that isn't theirs.

Sharing with a team is part of Shared reminders, which needs the Premium plan or above (402 otherwise). Settable only when creating the reminder.

members: string[]

(Optional) Users who can see this reminder, and the only ones it notifies. Each entry is a user ID, OID, or email, or "me" for the authenticated user.

  • Omit the field — only the authenticated user. This is the default, except with partner: then every member of the project and of that team.
  • Pass null — every member of the owner. An external team member must also set partner to one of their teams.
  • Pass [] — only the owner's admins.
  • Pass a list — only those users.

Unlike a work's members, omitting the field does not mean every member: pass null explicitly for that.

Omitting it without partner, or naming only yourself (such as ["me"]), keeps the reminder yours; anything else shares it — the Shared reminders feature, which needs the Premium plan or above (402 otherwise).

Rejected with 400 when a listed user is not a member of the owner, when a non-empty list does not include the authenticated user, or when partner is also set. On a reminder attached to a task, every listed user must also be able to see the task (400 naming those who can't): a project member sees every task, but an external team member only the tasks shared with their team. A guest sees only the reminders naming them, and creates none (403: a reminder takes write access).

Settable only when creating the reminder. It cannot be changed afterwards, so recreate the reminder to change who can see it. A personal reminder (created under -) is always its owner's alone, so no one else can be named.

string
Example
{
  "when": "2027-01-15T09:00:00.000Z",
  "recurrence": {
    "freq": "weekly",
    "interval": 1,
    "byweekday": "[1,3]",
    "byweekno": 2,
    "bydayno": 25,
    "bymonth": 10,
    "dupsubtasks": false,
    "sincelatest": true,
    "until": "2020-12-22"
  },
  "leads": [
    {
      "minutes": 30,
      "days": 1,
      "at": "09:00"
    }
  ],
  "name": "Pay the **bill**",
  "partner": "rcBHBYXZSiyDRrHrWPutatfF",
  "members": "[\"me\", \"john\"]"
}

CreateStatusBody: object

color: string

(Optional) Status color index from Quire’s predefined palette. If omitted, a color will be generated automatically. Two-digit code: first digit 0–5, second digit 0–7 (e.g., 35).

name: string

Display name of the status.

value: integer

Non-negative integer indicating progress. Must be unique within its context (e.g., project); a value already in use returns 409. Values ≥ 100 are treated as completed. When listing or searching tasks, ?status=100 (or completed) matches every completed status; values above 100 can't be filtered individually.

Example
{
  "color": "35",
  "name": "Doing",
  "value": 50
}

CreateSublistBody: object

all: boolean

(Optional) Whether every task belongs to the sublist by default. Default: false — only the tasks in includes are in it, with their subtasks. With true, every task of the owner is in it; leave tasks out afterwards by updating the sublist with changes ("exclude": true). Settable only when creating the sublist.

includes: string[]

(Optional) List of task OIDs to include in this sublist. All descendants of the specified tasks will be included as well.

string
description: string

(Optional) Description of the record (Markdown supported). An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

iconColor: string

(Optional) Icon color index from Quire's predefined palette. Two-digit code [0-5][0-7]: first digit 0-5, second digit 0-7 (e.g. 00, 37, 57). NOT a CSS hex color.

image: string icon-view-list, icon-view-kanban, icon-grid, icon-view-timeline, icon-calendar, icon-timer, icon-briefcase-o, icon-rocket-o, icon-bug-o, icon-user-o, icon-colleagues-o, icon-lightbulb-o, icon-leaf-o, icon-clapperboard, icon-sitemap-o, icon-list, icon-flash-on-o, icon-piggy-bank-o, icon-graduation-cap-o, icon-paper-plane-o, icon-globe-o, icon-music-o, icon-detail, icon-beach-o, icon-paper, icon-home-o, icon-building, icon-database-o, icon-microscope-o, icon-hamburger-o, icon-trophy-o, icon-thumbs-o-up, icon-thumbs-o-down, icon-smile-o, icon-frown-o, icon-meh-o, icon-bullseye, icon-incomplete, icon-filter-o, icon-comment, icon-view-insight, icon-view-dashboard, icon-square-dotted-o

(Optional) Icon image identifier, one of the listed values.

name: string

Display name of the record (Markdown supported).

id: string

(Optional) ID for this record, unique among the owner's records of the same kind (e.g. a project's sublists). If omitted or invalid, Quire derives one from name; if already taken, Quire changes it by appending characters. Neither is an error, so read the id back from the response.

partner: string

(Optional) OID of the external team to share this record with; it is then shared with the members of the project and of that team, and is always private.

Only a project's record can carry one — an organization, a folder or a smart folder has no external team — and it must be one of the project's external teams; any other value is 400. It cannot be combined with members either (400).

An external team member shares a record with every member only through their own team: with members omitted or null, they must set partner to one of their teams. Otherwise 400 names their teams, as it does for a team of the project that isn't theirs.

Settable only when creating the record.

private: boolean

(Optional) Hide this record from guests and from the visitors of a public project or of a share link, like a custom field's private. A choice only when members is null and partner is null; defaults to false (everyone). Otherwise it is always true: a record shared with an external team, with selected members or with the admins only is hidden from them, so false is rejected with 400.

start: string

(Optional) Target start date: a date only, e.g. 2024-01-02; a value with a time of day returns 400.

due: string

(Optional) Target due date: a date only, e.g. 2024-05-25; a value with a time of day returns 400.

members: string[]

(Optional) Users who can see this record, and the only ones it is shown to. Each entry is a user ID, OID, or email, or "me" for the authenticated user.

  • Omit the field, or pass null — every member of the owner can see it, and so can guests and the visitors of a public project or of a share link unless private. This is the default. (A reminder differs: omitting its members means only the authenticated user.) An external team member must also set partner to one of their teams.
  • Pass [] — only the owner's admins can see it.
  • Pass a list — only those users can see it.

Rejected with 400 when:

  • a listed user is not a member of the owner. Unlike a task's assignees, which silently drops a non-member, this is an error: dropping the last one would leave [], which means something else entirely.
  • the list is non-empty and does not include the authenticated user — you would not be able to see what you just created.
  • partner is also set, since an external-team record is already shared with all members of the project and of the team.

Settable only when creating the record. It cannot be changed afterwards, so recreate the record to change who can see it.

string
Example
{
  "all": false,
  "includes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "description": "**Great** record to start with.",
  "iconColor": "37",
  "image": "icon-view-kanban",
  "name": "Highlight 101",
  "id": "Highlight101",
  "partner": "rcBHBYXZSiyDRrHrWPutatfF",
  "private": false,
  "start": "2024-01-02",
  "due": "2024-05-25",
  "members": "[\"me\", \"john\"]"
}

CreateTagBody: object

color: string

(Optional) Tag color index from Quire’s predefined palette. If omitted, a color will be generated automatically. Two-digit code: first digit 0–5, second digit 0–7 (e.g., 35).

global: boolean

(Optional) Whether this tag is global (available in all projects of the project's organization). If omitted, the tag is not global. true requires the right to manage the organization's tags; otherwise 403.

name: string

Display name of the tag.

Example
{
  "color": "35",
  "global": true,
  "name": "Later"
}

CreateTaskBody: object

description: string

(Optional) A description of the task. An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

tasks: CreateTaskBody

(Optional) List of subtasks to create along with this task. Each one, at any depth, costs 1 rate-limit unit and counts toward the per-call cap of 300 tasks and the plan's per-minute limit; see Rate Limits.

CreateTaskBody
tags: string[]

(Optional) A list of tag OIDs or names to be added to the new task. Tag names are case-insensitive. Each must be an existing tag of the project, or a global tag of its organization; an unknown tag is rejected with 400, not created.

string
partner: string

(Optional) The external team to share this task with: the name or OID of one of the project's external teams (GET /partner/list/id/{projectId} lists them). The team's members then get access to the task and its subtasks. Setting it takes the right to assign tasks (403 otherwise). A name or OID that matches no team, or a value that isn't a string, such as null, is rejected with 400.

recurrence: Recurrence

(Optional) Makes the task repeat. Omit it for a task that doesn't repeat.

  • freq (required): daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.
  • interval: a positive integer; 2 with weekly means every 2 weeks. Default: 1.
  • until: end date, e.g. 2026-12-31. Default: never ends.
  • weekly needs byweekday: the days of the week as a list, where 0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday, e.g. [0, 3].
  • monthly needs bydayno, the day of the month (1–31, or "last"), or byweekno, the week of the month (1–5, or "last"), with byweekday as a single day in that week, e.g. 1 for Tuesday. If both byweekno and bydayno are given, byweekno wins.
  • yearly needs bymonth, the month (1–12, 1 = January), plus what monthly needs.
  • dupsubtasks: whether to duplicate subtasks when the task is completed. Default: true.
  • sincelatest: with daily only, whether to repeat from the last completion date. Default: false.

A property that doesn't apply to freq is ignored; an invalid value, or a missing required one, is rejected with 400.

A recurring task always has a due. If due is omitted, it is derived from the recurrence: the nearest occurrence since today. The request is rejected if the derived due precedes start; specify due explicitly in that case.

assignees: string[]

(Optional) A list of user identifiers (OID, ID, or email) to assign this task to.

  • Use "me" to indicate the current user.
  • Use "inherit" to include all assignees of the parent task.

Only project members (external-team members included) can be assigned; anyone else is silently left out. An unknown user is rejected with 400.

string
asUser: boolean

(Optional) If true, marks this task as created by the app. Read asUser as app-as-user: the app itself is the user, not the authorizing user. Default: false (created by the authorizing user). In bulk-add, each item has its own. A nested task's asUser must match its top-level task's (a tree is created by one author); otherwise the call is rejected with 400.

followers: string[]

(Optional) List of user identifiers (OID, ID, or email) who follow this task. Only those listed, and anyone @mentioned in the description, follow it, so include "me" for the current user to follow.

  • Use "me" for the current user.
  • Use "inherit" to include followers of the parent task.
  • Use "app" for the application itself to follow (receive notifications).

For app followers, additional syntaxes are supported:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL (e.g., .../standard/soc1/33456/a7).
string
successors: string[]

(Optional) List of successor task identifiers (OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

string
start: string

(Optional) Start date/time in UTC.

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

Notes:

  • Seconds are not supported.
  • 2020-10-30T00:00:00 is treated as 2020-10-30 (date only).
  • To specify exactly midnight UTC, use 2020-10-30T00:00 (no seconds).
due: string

(Optional) Due date/time in UTC.

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

Notes:

  • Seconds are not supported.
  • 2020-10-30T00:00:00 is treated as 2020-10-30 (date only).
  • To specify exactly midnight UTC, use 2020-10-30T00:00 (no seconds).
yourField: object

PLACEHOLDER — do NOT send a key literally named yourField. Instead, use the custom field's own name (as defined via /project/add-field) as the JSON key, with a value matching the field's type:

  • Text / Email / Hyperlink: string.
  • Number / Money: numeric value (no currency symbol).
  • Checkbox: true or false.
  • Select: option name (string).
  • Date: ISO 8601 timestamp (yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssZ) or date-only (yyyy-MM-dd).
  • Duration: number of seconds.
  • User: user OID, user ID, or email — server resolves to the user's OID.
  • Task: task OID, integer task ID, or #<id> string — server resolves to the task's OID (scoped to this project).
  • File: the attachment list as a task returns it (absolute url accepted).
  • Multi-value (fields configured with multiple: true): provide a list.

Example body fragment: {"Priority": 3, "Owners": ["alice", "bob@example.com"], "Depends": ["#42"]}.

peekaboo:
boolean
integer

(Optional) Peekaboo setting. Accepts a boolean or a positive integer:

  • true: Hide indefinitely.
  • positive integer: Number of days to hide.
  • false: Cancel previous peekaboo.

Default: false.

section: boolean

(Optional) Whether this task is a section. Default: false.

milestone: boolean

(Optional) Whether this task is a milestone. Default: false.

name: string

The name of the task.

status: integer

(Optional) Task status. Must be one of the project's status values (GET /status/list/id/{projectId} lists them); any other value is rejected with 400. Every project has 0, the initial status, and 100, completed; 100 or more means completed. Default: 0.

etc: integer

(Optional) Estimated time to complete, in seconds: an integer from 0 to 864,000,000 (10,000 days). null is the same as leaving it out.

priority: integer -1, 0, 1, 2

(Optional) Task priority: -1 Low, 0 Medium, 1 High, 2 Urgent. (The server also accepts the case-insensitive English names Low, Medium, High, Urgent, but the integer form is recommended for typed callers.) Default: 0 (Medium).

sourceRef: object

(Optional) A JSON object your app stores with the task, such as where the task came from. Quire keeps it as is and returns it as sourceRef whenever the task is read.

  • text (optional): a Markdown string Quire shows as the task's source line in the task details. Include a link to the source, e.g. Source: [GitHub issue 42](https://github.com/acme/web/issues/42).
  • Any other key: your app's own data, not shown in Quire. Put it under a key named after your app, e.g. github, so it won't clash with another app's.
  • To find these tasks later, search with ?source-ref=github: it returns the tasks whose sourceRef has that key, whatever its value.
  • Size: at most about 2,048 characters, keys and values together, and text must be a string; otherwise 400.
Example
{
  "description": "This is a *cool* task.",
  "tasks": [
    {
      "description": "This is a *cool* task.",
      "tasks": [
        "#/definitions/CreateTaskBody"
      ],
      "tags": [
        "X6nmx9XjEO2wKbqeB1pRT43C"
      ],
      "partner": "UI design team",
      "recurrence": {
        "freq": "weekly",
        "interval": 1,
        "byweekday": "[1,3]",
        "byweekno": 2,
        "bydayno": 25,
        "bymonth": 10,
        "dupsubtasks": false,
        "sincelatest": true,
        "until": "2020-12-22"
      },
      "assignees": [
        "6QMKkEPBVWETLWrXqws94ALU"
      ],
      "asUser": true,
      "followers": [
        "tzufRLqCnud74dARyDSvjWDl"
      ],
      "successors": "[\"#13\"]",
      "start": "2026-05-01",
      "due": "2026-05-10T17:00Z",
      "yourField": "object",
      "peekaboo": true,
      "section": true,
      "milestone": true,
      "name": "Design new **logo**",
      "status": 0,
      "etc": 0,
      "priority": 0,
      "sourceRef": "{\"github\": {\"repo\": \"acme/web\", \"issue\": 42}, \"text\": \"Source: [GitHub issue 42](https://github.com/acme/web/issues/42)\"}"
    }
  ],
  "tags": [
    "X6nmx9XjEO2wKbqeB1pRT43C"
  ],
  "partner": "UI design team",
  "recurrence": "#/definitions/Recurrence",
  "assignees": [
    "6QMKkEPBVWETLWrXqws94ALU"
  ],
  "asUser": true,
  "followers": [
    "tzufRLqCnud74dARyDSvjWDl"
  ],
  "successors": "[\"#13\"]",
  "start": "2026-05-01",
  "due": "2026-05-10T17:00Z",
  "yourField": "object",
  "peekaboo": true,
  "section": true,
  "milestone": true,
  "name": "Design new **logo**",
  "status": 0,
  "etc": 0,
  "priority": 0,
  "sourceRef": "{\"github\": {\"repo\": \"acme/web\", \"issue\": 42}, \"text\": \"Source: [GitHub issue 42](https://github.com/acme/web/issues/42)\"}"
}

Dashboard: object

url: string

URL of this dashboard on the Quire website.

nameHtml: string

Name rendered as an HTML fragment converted from Markdown.

nameText: string

Name with Markdown removed.

name: string

Display name (Markdown supported).

id: string

ID.

description: string

Description (Markdown supported).

descriptionHtml: string

Description rendered as an HTML fragment converted from Markdown.

descriptionText: string

Description with Markdown removed.

iconColor: string

Color index for the icon from Quire’s predefined palette. Two-digit code: first digit 0–5, second digit 0–7 (e.g., 37).

image: string

Image URL representing this record.

oid: string

Object identifier (OID), a UUID-like unique string.

partner: SimpleTaggingEntity

External team this record is shared with. Omitted if none.

archivedAt: string

Timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601) when this record was archived. Omitted if not archived.

members: SimpleIdentity

Users who can see this record, and the only ones it is shown to.

  • null — every member of the owner can see it; private tells whether guests and the visitors of a public project or of a share link can too.
  • [] — only the owner's admins can.
  • a list — only those users can.

All three are returned explicitly, so the states can be told apart. Set it when creating the record; it cannot be changed afterwards.

SimpleIdentity
private: boolean

Whether this record is hidden from guests and from the visitors of a public project or of a share link, like a custom field's private. Present only when members is null and partner is null — the one case where it is a choice. A record shared with an external team, with selected members or with the admins only is always hidden from them.

owner: DashboardOwner

Owner this dashboard belongs to.
