Creation timestamp in UTC (ISO 8601).

createdBy: SimpleIdentity

User who created this record.

ErrorResponse: object

Represents an error response.

code: integer

The error code: the HTTP status, echoed — such as 400, 404, 408 or 409 — except these, which tell apart cases that share a status:

  • 469: a plan quota or limit has been reached (HTTP 402).
  • 470: the subscription has expired (HTTP 402).
  • 471: temporarily blocked; try again later (HTTP 403).
  • 100: the Authorization header is missing or malformed (HTTP 403).
message: string

Human-readable error message.

Example
{
  "code": 429,
  "message": "Something went wrong."
}

FieldConditionFormat: object

color: string

Palette color index. Format: two digits [0-5][0-7] (first = row 0-5, second = column 0-7). Examples: 00, 13, 57. NOT a CSS hex color.

second: Number

(Value fields, between/notBetween only) Second operand. For duration, must be an integer number of seconds.

when: string past, yesterday, today, tomorrow, upcoming, last7d, next7d, lastWeek, thisWeek, nextWeek

(Date fields) Date condition.

op: string >=, >, <=, <, =, !=, between, notBetween

(Value fields) Comparison operator.

first: Number

(Value fields) First operand. For duration, must be an integer number of seconds.

Example
{
  "color": "42",
  "second": "200",
  "when": "today",
  "op": ">=",
  "first": "#/definitions/Number"
}

FieldDefinition: object

currency: string

(Optional, money or formula only) Currency symbol. When omitted on a money field, defaults to $.

percent: boolean

(Optional, number only) Format the value as a percentage.

private: boolean

(Optional) Whether guests and the visitors of a public project or of a share link can't view this field and its values. Present only when viewMembers is absent, the one case where it is a choice; with viewMembers, the field is always hidden from them.

lookup: object

(lookup only) Map from lookup key to numeric value. Keys are OIDs of the configured lookupType entity (e.g. user OIDs when lookupType=User). Values are numbers. Example: {"abc123": 1, "def456": 2}.

options: FieldOption

(select only) Option list.

FieldOption
hidden: boolean

(Optional) Hide this field from the task detail panel.

clearOnDup: boolean

(Optional) Clear this field when duplicating a task.

viewMembers: SimpleIdentity

(Optional) The users who can view this field's values; an admin not named sees the definition, not the values. An empty list means the admins only. Absent means everyone private allows. The API returns only the fields the caller can view, and only their values on a task.

SimpleIdentity
editMembers: SimpleIdentity

(Optional) The users who can edit the values; an admin not named can't. An empty list means the admins only. Absent means anyone who can edit the task. Editing also requires viewing the field. locked stops editing in Quire regardless of this list; the API ignores the lock, so this list still applies to API writes.

SimpleIdentity
locked: boolean

(Optional) Whether the values are locked: no one can edit them in Quire, admins included, while the API still can, e.g., to push values from another system.

withTime: boolean

(Optional, date only) Include time-of-day in addition to the date.

ndecimal: integer -1, 0, 1, 2, 3

(Optional, number/money only) Number of decimal digits. -1 means no rounding.

durationFormat: string hh:mm:ss, hh:mm, 1h1m, 1h, 1d1h, dd:hh:mm:ss, dd:hh:mm, dd:hh

(Optional, duration or formula only) Duration display format.

formula: string

(formula only) Formula expression.

resultType: string text, number, money, date, duration, checkbox

(Optional, formula only) Expected result type.

lookupType: string User, Task, Project, Organization

(Optional, lookup only) Source type for lookup keys. Default: User.

multiple: boolean

(Optional) Allow multiple values. Applies to select, user, task, and file (always true for file).

conditionFormat: FieldConditionFormat

(Optional) Conditional-format rules. Applicable to date (date rules use when) and to number/money/duration/lookup (value rules use op/first/second). A formula is resolved by its resultType: date → date rules, number/money/duration → value rules.

FieldConditionFormat
type: string text, number, money, date, duration, select, checkbox, user, task, hyperlink, email, formula, file, lookup

Field type. A project's field is one of text, number, money, date, duration, select, checkbox, user, task, hyperlink, email, formula and file; an insight's field is formula or lookup.

Example
{
  "currency": "USD",
  "percent": false,
  "private": false,
  "lookup": "object",
  "options": [
    {
      "color": "13",
      "name": "High"
    }
  ],
  "hidden": false,
  "clearOnDup": false,
  "viewMembers": "[{\"oid\":\"iDsPd.QP_qM.hN.Trymukn8b\",\"id\":\"john\",\"name\":\"John\"}]",
  "editMembers": "[]",
  "locked": false,
  "withTime": false,
  "ndecimal": 2,
  "durationFormat": "hh:mm",
  "formula": "SUM(Subtask.Amount)",
  "resultType": "number",
  "lookupType": "User",
  "multiple": true,
  "conditionFormat": [
    {
      "color": "42",
      "second": "200",
      "when": "today",
      "op": ">=",
      "first": "#/definitions/Number"
    }
  ],
  "type": "number"
}

FieldDefinitionWithName: object

name: string

Field name (equals the name query parameter for update/move, new-name for rename, or the name supplied in the body for add).

currency: string

(Optional, money or formula only) Currency symbol. When omitted on a money field, defaults to $.

percent: boolean

(Optional, number only) Format the value as a percentage.

private: boolean

(Optional) Whether guests and the visitors of a public project or of a share link can't view this field and its values. Present only when viewMembers is absent, the one case where it is a choice; with viewMembers, the field is always hidden from them.

lookup: object

(lookup only) Map from lookup key to numeric value. Keys are OIDs of the configured lookupType entity (e.g. user OIDs when lookupType=User). Values are numbers. Example: {"abc123": 1, "def456": 2}.

options: FieldOption

(select only) Option list.

FieldOption
hidden: boolean

(Optional) Hide this field from the task detail panel.

clearOnDup: boolean

(Optional) Clear this field when duplicating a task.

viewMembers: SimpleIdentity

(Optional) The users who can view this field's values; an admin not named sees the definition, not the values. An empty list means the admins only. Absent means everyone private allows. The API returns only the fields the caller can view, and only their values on a task.

SimpleIdentity
editMembers: SimpleIdentity

(Optional) The users who can edit the values; an admin not named can't. An empty list means the admins only. Absent means anyone who can edit the task. Editing also requires viewing the field. locked stops editing in Quire regardless of this list; the API ignores the lock, so this list still applies to API writes.

SimpleIdentity
locked: boolean

(Optional) Whether the values are locked: no one can edit them in Quire, admins included, while the API still can, e.g., to push values from another system.

withTime: boolean

(Optional, date only) Include time-of-day in addition to the date.

ndecimal: integer -1, 0, 1, 2, 3

(Optional, number/money only) Number of decimal digits. -1 means no rounding.

durationFormat: string hh:mm:ss, hh:mm, 1h1m, 1h, 1d1h, dd:hh:mm:ss, dd:hh:mm, dd:hh

(Optional, duration or formula only) Duration display format.

formula: string

(formula only) Formula expression.

resultType: string text, number, money, date, duration, checkbox

(Optional, formula only) Expected result type.

lookupType: string User, Task, Project, Organization

(Optional, lookup only) Source type for lookup keys. Default: User.

multiple: boolean

(Optional) Allow multiple values. Applies to select, user, task, and file (always true for file).

conditionFormat: FieldConditionFormat

(Optional) Conditional-format rules. Applicable to date (date rules use when) and to number/money/duration/lookup (value rules use op/first/second). A formula is resolved by its resultType: date → date rules, number/money/duration → value rules.

FieldConditionFormat
type: string text, number, money, date, duration, select, checkbox, user, task, hyperlink, email, formula, file, lookup

FieldOption: object

color: string

(Optional) Palette color index for the option's chip. Format: two digits [0-5][0-7] (first = row 0-5, second = column 0-7). Examples: 00, 13, 57. NOT a CSS hex color. If omitted on creation, a color is auto-assigned.

name: string

Option name, unique within the field, and at most 1,280 characters; otherwise 400.

Example
{
  "color": "13",
  "name": "High"
}

Insight: object

url: string

URL of this insight view on the Quire website.

nameHtml: string

Name rendered as an HTML fragment converted from Markdown.

nameText: string

Name with Markdown removed.

name: string

Display name (Markdown supported).

id: string

ID.

description: string

Description (Markdown supported).

descriptionHtml: string

Description rendered as an HTML fragment converted from Markdown.

descriptionText: string

Description with Markdown removed.

iconColor: string

Color index for the icon from Quire’s predefined palette. Two-digit code: first digit 0–5, second digit 0–7 (e.g., 37).

image: string

Image URL representing this record.

oid: string

Object identifier (OID), a UUID-like unique string.

partner: SimpleTaggingEntity

External team this record is shared with. Omitted if none.

archivedAt: string

Timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601) when this record was archived. Omitted if not archived.

members: SimpleIdentity

Users who can see this record, and the only ones it is shown to.

  • null — every member of the owner can see it; private tells whether guests and the visitors of a public project or of a share link can too.
  • [] — only the owner's admins can.
  • a list — only those users can.

All three are returned explicitly, so the states can be told apart. Set it when creating the record; it cannot be changed afterwards.

SimpleIdentity
private: boolean

Whether this record is hidden from guests and from the visitors of a public project or of a share link, like a custom field's private. Present only when members is null and partner is null — the one case where it is a choice. A record shared with an external team, with selected members or with the admins only is always hidden from them.

fields: object

Custom-field definitions for this insight view, keyed by field name. Use the add-field, update-field, remove-field, rename-field, and move-field extensions to mutate entries.

owner: InsightOwner

Owner this insight belongs to.

createdAt: string

Creation timestamp in UTC (ISO 8601).

createdBy: SimpleIdentity

User who created this record.

Example

RateLimit: object

hour: RateLimitBucket

Hourly rate-limit bucket.

minute: RateLimitBucket

Per-minute rate-limit bucket.

organization: string

OID of the organization these limits apply to.

plan: string

The plan whose limits are enforced: Free, Professional, Premium, or Enterprise. During a trial, it is the plan before the trial, not the trial's: a trial doesn't change the rate limits.

Example
{
  "hour": {
    "remaining": 1208,
    "limit": 1250,
    "reset": 1774863600,
    "used": 42
  },
  "minute": "#/definitions/RateLimitBucket",
  "organization": "YxjapXXRCOYxoaiCT4tT3OQm",
  "plan": "Enterprise"
}

RateLimitBucket: object

remaining: integer

Remaining calls: max(limit - used, 0), or -1 if unlimited.

limit: integer

Maximum number of calls allowed in this window, as enforced: during a trial, that of the plan before the trial. -1 indicates no limit.

reset: integer

Unix epoch (seconds) of the next wall-clock boundary at which the used counter will reset.

used: integer

Number of calls consumed so far in the current window.

Example
{
  "remaining": 1208,
  "limit": 1250,
  "reset": 1774863600,
  "used": 42
}

Recurrence: object

freq: string daily, weekly, monthly, yearly

Recurrence frequency. Besides it:

  • weekly needs byweekday.
  • monthly needs bydayno, or byweekno with byweekday.
  • yearly needs bymonth, plus what monthly needs.

A property that doesn't apply to freq is ignored.

Examples: {"freq": "daily"} repeats every day; {"freq": "weekly", "byweekday": [0, 3]} every Monday and Thursday; {"freq": "monthly", "interval": 2, "byweekno": 2, "byweekday": 1} on the second Tuesday of every other month.

interval: integer

Interval between occurrences, a positive integer. For example, 2 with weekly means every 2 weeks. Default: 1 when omitted or null. 0 or a negative value is 400.

byweekday: integer[]

Days of the week, as integers where 0=Mon, 1=Tue, …, 6=Sun.

  • With weekly: required, the days it occurs on, as a list (e.g., [1], [0,3]).
  • With monthly or yearly and byweekno: required, a single integer — the day in that week (e.g., 1 for Tuesday), and returned as one too.

Ignored otherwise.

integer
byweekno: integer

With monthly or yearly: the week of the month, 1–5, or "last" (also 6) for the month's last week. Requires byweekday for the day in that week. If both byweekno and bydayno are given, byweekno wins.

bydayno: integer

With monthly or yearly: the day of the month, 1–31. 31, or "last", means the month's last day, and is returned as 31. Ignored if byweekno is given.

bymonth: integer

With yearly: required, the month, 1–12 (1 = January). Ignored otherwise.

dupsubtasks: boolean

Whether to duplicate subtasks when the task is completed. Default: true.

sincelatest: boolean

With daily: whether to repeat relative to the last completion date. Default: false when omitted or null. Ignored otherwise.

until: string

End date for the recurrence (UTC, ISO 8601). If not specified, the series never ends.

Example
{
  "freq": "weekly",
  "interval": 1,
  "byweekday": "[1,3]",
  "byweekno": 2,
  "bydayno": 25,
  "bymonth": 10,
  "dupsubtasks": false,
  "sincelatest": true,
  "until": "2020-12-22"
}

RecurrenceX: object

seriesId: string

Identifier for the recurrence series this task belongs to. Tasks that share the same seriesId are part of the same recurring series.

freq: string daily, weekly, monthly, yearly

Recurrence frequency. Besides it:

  • weekly needs byweekday.
  • monthly needs bydayno, or byweekno with byweekday.
  • yearly needs bymonth, plus what monthly needs.

A property that doesn't apply to freq is ignored.

Examples: {"freq": "daily"} repeats every day; {"freq": "weekly", "byweekday": [0, 3]} every Monday and Thursday; {"freq": "monthly", "interval": 2, "byweekno": 2, "byweekday": 1} on the second Tuesday of every other month.

interval: integer

Interval between occurrences, a positive integer. For example, 2 with weekly means every 2 weeks. Default: 1 when omitted or null. 0 or a negative value is 400.

byweekday: integer[]

Days of the week, as integers where 0=Mon, 1=Tue, …, 6=Sun.

  • With weekly: required, the days it occurs on, as a list (e.g., [1], [0,3]).
  • With monthly or yearly and byweekno: required, a single integer — the day in that week (e.g., 1 for Tuesday), and returned as one too.

Ignored otherwise.

integer
byweekno: integer

With monthly or yearly: the week of the month, 1–5, or "last" (also 6) for the month's last week. Requires byweekday for the day in that week. If both byweekno and bydayno are given, byweekno wins.

bydayno: integer

With monthly or yearly: the day of the month, 1–31. 31, or "last", means the month's last day, and is returned as 31. Ignored if byweekno is given.

bymonth: integer

With yearly: required, the month, 1–12 (1 = January). Ignored otherwise.

dupsubtasks: boolean

Whether to duplicate subtasks when the task is completed. Default: true.

sincelatest: boolean

With daily: whether to repeat relative to the last completion date. Default: false when omitted or null. Ignored otherwise.

until: string

End date for the recurrence (UTC, ISO 8601). If not specified, the series never ends.

Example
{
  "seriesId": "j47xvxul26",
  "freq": "weekly",
  "interval": 1,
  "byweekday": "[1,3]",
  "byweekno": 2,
  "bydayno": 25,
  "bymonth": 10,
  "dupsubtasks": false,
  "sincelatest": true,
  "until": "2020-12-22"
}

Reminder: object

oid: string

Object identifier (OID), a UUID-like unique string.

task: ReminderTask

Task this reminder is attached to. Omitted if it stands on its own. A reminder cannot be moved to another task.

Only oid, id, name and url are returned here; fetch the task itself for its dates.

when: string

When this reminder fires, if it fires at a time of its own (UTC, ISO 8601).

Omitted whenever task has a start or due date: the reminder then fires from that date instead, and leads counts back from it. The dates are not part of this response, so to show when a reminder will fire, fetch its task and use its due date, or its start date if it has no due date.

recurrence: RecurrenceX

How this reminder repeats. Omitted if it does not repeat, which is always so while the reminder is anchored: it then repeats with its task's own schedule.

leads: ReminderLead

When to notify before the fire time, one notification each. [{"minutes": 0}] means a single notification at the fire time, and is what a reminder created without leads has.

Each entry is an object naming exactly one of minutes (an absolute offset) and days (calendar days, so a lead spanning a daylight-saving transition keeps its wall-clock time), the latter taking an optional at clock.

Neither may be negative — a lead counts back from the fire time, and nothing fires after it — nor exceed 10,000 days ahead of it, and there may be at most 30 of them.

ReminderLead
nameHtml: string

Name rendered as an HTML fragment converted from Markdown.

nameText: string

Name with Markdown removed.

name: string

Text shown instead of the default message (Markdown supported). Omitted when the default is used, and so are nameText and nameHtml.

partner: SimpleTaggingEntity

External team this reminder is shared with. Omitted if none. When set, it reaches every member of the project and of that team.

members: SimpleIdentity

Users who can see this reminder, and the only ones it notifies.

  • null — every member of the owner.
  • [] — only the owner's admins.
  • a list — only those users.

All three are returned explicitly, so the states can be told apart. Set it when creating the reminder; it cannot be changed afterwards.

SimpleIdentity
owner: ReminderOwner

Project, organization, folder or smart folder this reminder belongs to. Fixed when the reminder is created: a reminder on a task always belongs to that task's project, and one created under - belongs to its creator's My Tasks.

url: string

URL of the page this reminder is shown on.

createdAt: string

Creation timestamp in UTC (ISO 8601).

createdBy: SimpleIdentity

User who created this record.

Example
{
  "oid": "iDsPd.QP_qM.hN.Trymukn8b",
  "task": {
    "url": "https://quire.io/w/my_project/42",
    "id": 42,
    "name": "Foo",
    "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
  },
  "when": "2027-01-15T09:00:00.000Z",
  "recurrence": {
    "seriesId": "j47xvxul26",
    "freq": "weekly",
    "interval": 1,
    "byweekday": "[1,3]",
    "byweekno": 2,
    "bydayno": 25,
    "bymonth": 10,
    "dupsubtasks": false,
    "sincelatest": true,
    "until": "2020-12-22"
  },
  "leads": [
    {
      "minutes": 30,
      "days": 1,
      "at": "09:00"
    }
  ],
  "nameHtml": "Pay the <strong>bill</strong>",
  "nameText": "Pay the bill",
  "name": "Pay the **bill**",
  "partner": {
    "color": "35",
    "name": "Foo",
    "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
  },
  "members": [
    {
      "url": "https://quire.io/u/my_id",
      "id": "my_id",
      "iconColor": "37",
      "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",
      "name": "Foo",
      "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
    }
  ],
  "owner": {
    "type": "Project",
    "url": "https://quire.io/w/prj_id",
    "id": "my_id",
    "iconColor": "37",
    "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",
    "name": "Foo",
    "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
  },
  "url": "https://quire.io/w/my_project?reminder=iDsPd.QP_qM.hN.Trymukn8b",
  "createdAt": "2018-12-22T02:06:58.158Z",
  "createdBy": "#/definitions/SimpleIdentity"
}

ReminderLead: object

minutes: integer

How many minutes before the fire time to notify — an absolute offset, so 30 stays 30 real minutes wherever the clocks move in between.

Exactly one of minutes and days must be given. An hour is simply 60 minutes: there is no hours, and a lead is stored and returned in whichever of the two forms it was sent.

days: integer

How many calendar days before the fire time to notify. Unlike minutes, this counts days, not 24-hour spans, so a lead spanning a daylight-saving transition still notifies at the same wall-clock time.

Exactly one of minutes and days must be given. A week is simply 7 days: there is no weeks.

at: string

(Optional, and only with days) The time of day to notify at, as HH:mm on a 24-hour clock — "09:00", "23:30". A 12-hour clock is rejected with 400.

Omit it to notify at the fire time's own time of day, which then follows that time if it later moves.

The clock is read in the time zone of the member who created the reminder, since one notification serves its whole audience and some one zone has to be chosen.

Example
{
  "minutes": 30,
  "days": 1,
  "at": "09:00"
}

Status: object

color: string

Color index from Quire’s predefined palette. Two-digit code: first digit 0–5, second digit 0–7 (e.g., 35).

name: string

Display name of the status.

value: integer

Non-negative integer indicating progress. Must be unique within its context (e.g., project). Values ≥ 100 are treated as completed. When listing or searching tasks, ?status=100 (or completed) matches every completed status; values above 100 can't be filtered individually.

Example
{
  "color": "35",
  "name": "Doing",
  "value": 50
}

StorageEntries: object

Stored entries as one JSON object: each key maps to its value, as it was stored. At most 20 entries, by key ascending; {} if none.

Example: {"latest": {"project": "my_project"}, "theme": "dark"}.

Example
"object"

StorageValue: object

A stored value: any JSON value, such as an object, array, string or number, at most 4 KiB as JSON. GET /storage/{name} returns it exactly as PUT /storage/{name} stored it.

Example: after PUT /storage/latest with the body {"project": "my_project"}, GET /storage/latest returns {"project": "my_project"}.

Example
"object"

Task: object

tags: SimpleTaggingEntity

Tags applied to this task.

SimpleTaggingEntity
successors: string[]

IDs of tasks that depend on this task, as #<id> strings. Omitted if none.

For ID-based access, prefer successorRefs, which returns {oid, id} pairs.

string
predecessors: string[]

IDs of tasks that this task depends on, as #<id> strings. Omitted if none.

For ID-based access, prefer predecessorRefs, which returns {oid, id} pairs.

string
successorRefs: TaskRef

Successors as {oid, id} pairs — same shape as ?return=compact. Recommended over successors for callers using ID-based access.

TaskRef
predecessorRefs: TaskRef

Predecessors as {oid, id} pairs — same shape as ?return=compact. Recommended over predecessors for callers using ID-based access.

TaskRef
oid: string

Object identifier (OID), a UUID-like unique string.

id: integer

Task id.

nameHtml: string

Task name rendered as an HTML fragment converted from Markdown.

nameText: string

Task name with Markdown removed.

name: string

Task name (Markdown supported).

description: string

Task description (Markdown supported).

descriptionHtml: string

Task description rendered as an HTML fragment converted from Markdown.

descriptionText: string

Task description with Markdown removed.

recurrence: RecurrenceX

Contains the recurrence details of this task. Omitted if the task does not repeat.

etc: integer

The estimated time to complete the task, expressed in seconds. Omitted if no estimate has been specified.

timelogs: Timelog

The time log entries associated with this task. Omitted for a guest member, and for a non-member of a public project, when the project hides time logs from guests (its default).

Timelog
status: TaskStatus

Task status as {value, name, color}, e.g. {"value": 0, "name": "To-do", "color": "50"}. A value of 100 or more means the task is completed.

start: string

Start date, in UTC: yyyy-MM-dd for a date without a time, or yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm'Z' with one (e.g. 2026-05-01T09:30Z). Omitted if not set.

due: string

priority: TaskPriority

Task priority as {value, name}, e.g. {"value": 0, "name": "Medium"}: -1 Low, 0 Medium, 1 High, 2 Urgent.

partner: SimpleTaggingEntity

The external team to which this task belongs. Omitted if this task is not associated with any external team.

assignors: TaskUser

A list of users who assigned this task, each as {oid, id, name}. Each item in assignors corresponds by index to the matching item in assignees (e.g., the first assignee was assigned by the first assignor).

yourField: object

A field you can't view is left out, and so is a field with no value, except a formula, which is always present. Values by field type:

  • Select: a list of option names, e.g. ["High"].
  • User: a list of {oid, id, name}.
  • Task: a list of {oid, id}.
  • Date: yyyy-MM-dd, or yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss'Z' with a time.
  • Duration: a number of seconds.
  • Formula: its computed value.
  • File: a list of attachments, each with an absolute url (as in attachments), plus type and createdAt (epoch milliseconds), which you send back unchanged when you keep a file.
  • Others (Text, Number, Money, Checkbox, Email, Hyperlink, …): the value as set.

TaskInfo: object

id: integer

Task id.

oid: string

Object identifier (OID), a UUID-like unique string.

parent: TaskInfo

The parent task as {oid, id, parent}, nested up to 10 ancestors. On the task itself, null if it has no parent; in the chain, the top-level ancestor has no parent key.

Past 10 ancestors, the 10th ancestor's parent is {"parent": "<OID>"}, holding the OID of the 11th, with no oid or id, to mark the cut-off.

Example
{
  "id": 12,
  "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld",
  "parent": {
    "id": 12,
    "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld",
    "parent": "#/definitions/TaskInfo"
  }
}

TaskPriority: object

A task's priority: its value and name.

value: integer -1, 0, 1, 2

Priority value: -1 Low, 0 Medium, 1 High, 2 Urgent.

name: string

Name of the priority in the authorizing user's language, e.g. Medium in English.

Example
{
  "value": 0,
  "name": "Medium"
}

TaskRef: object

id: integer

Task id.

oid: string

Object identifier (OID), a UUID-like unique string.

Example
{
  "id": 12,
  "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
}

TaskStatus: object

A task's status: its value, name, and color.

value: integer

Status value, one of the project's statuses. 0 is the initial status; 100 or more means completed.

name: string

Display name of the status. A built-in status without a custom name gets its default name in the authorizing user's language.

color: string

Palette index for the status color. Two-digit code: first digit 0–5, second digit 0–7 (e.g., 35). Matches the predefined colors shown in Quire’s color picker.

Example
{
  "value": 0,
  "name": "To-do",
  "color": "50"
}

TaskUser: object

A user as a task gives it: {oid, id, name}.

name: string

Display name of the user.

id: string

User ID.

oid: string

Object identifier (OID), a UUID-like unique string.

Example
{
  "name": "John Doe",
  "id": "john_doe",
  "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
}

Since comments can be removed, this value may not always match the current set of comments.

approval: Approval

The task's current approval state. Omitted if no approval has been requested. Mutate via POST /task/approve/id/{projectId}/{taskId} (request / approve / reject / change) and DELETE /task/revoke-approval/id/{projectId}/{taskId} (cancel), or their OID forms POST /task/approve/{oid} and DELETE /task/revoke-approval/{oid}.

archivedAt: string

When the task was archived (hidden by peekaboo). Omitted if it isn't archived.

archivedBy: TaskUser

The user who archived the task, as {oid, id, name}. null or omitted if it isn't archived.

reshowAt: string

When an archived task shows again: set if it was hidden for a number of days (peekaboo with a positive integer). Omitted otherwise.

parent: TaskInfo

The parent task as {oid, id, parent}, nested up to 10 ancestors. On the task itself, null if it has no parent; in the chain, the top-level ancestor has no parent key.

Past 10 ancestors, the 10th ancestor's parent is {"parent": "<OID>"}, holding the OID of the 11th, with no oid or id, to mark the cut-off.

project: SimpleEntityWithId

The project to which this task belongs.

yourField: object

PLACEHOLDER — no key is literally named yourField. Each custom field with a value on the task appears as a top-level key named after the field (as defined via /project/add-field), e.g. "Cost": 120. A field you can't view is left out, and so is a field with no value, except a formula, which is always present. Values by field type:

  • Select: a list of option names, e.g. ["High"].
  • User: a list of {oid, id, name}.
  • Task: a list of {oid, id}.
  • Date: yyyy-MM-dd, or yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss'Z' with a time.
  • Duration: a number of seconds.
  • Formula: its computed value.
  • File: a list of attachments, each with an absolute url (as in attachments), plus type and createdAt (epoch milliseconds), which you send back unchanged when you keep a file.
  • Others (Text, Number, Money, Checkbox, Email, Hyperlink, …): the value as set.
createdAt: string

Creation timestamp in UTC (ISO 8601).

createdBy: TaskUser

User who created this task, as {oid, id, name}.

Example

UpdateChatBody: object

Request body for updating a chat channel. Extends UpdateWorkBody and adds follower management; omitted fields preserve existing values.

followers: string[]

(Optional) Followers (OID, ID, or email) to replace the current followers.

  • "me" — the current user.
  • "app" — the application follows (receives notifications).

App follower syntax: app|team, app|team|channel, or app|/path.

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

string
addFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers (OID, ID, or email) to add. Adding a user also takes them off mutes.

  • "me" — the current user.
  • "app" — the application follows.

App follower syntax: app|team, app|team|channel, or app|/path.

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

string
removeFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers (OID, ID, or email) to remove. A removed user who follows the project is also muted (added to mutes), so they stop getting notifications about it.

  • "me" — the current user.
  • "app" — the application.

App follower syntax: app|team, app|team|channel, or app|/path.

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

UpdateFieldBody: object

currency: string

(Optional, money/formula only) Currency symbol. Pass $ to reset a money field to its default.

percent: boolean

(Optional, number only) Format the value as a percentage.

private: boolean

(Optional) Hide this field and its values from guests and from the visitors of a public project or of a share link. A choice only without viewMembers; with it, the field is always hidden from them, so false is rejected with 400.

lookup: object

(Optional, lookup only) Map from lookup key to numeric value. Keys are OIDs of the configured lookupType entity. Replaces the entire map.

options: UpdateFieldOption

(Optional, select only) Replacement option list, each an object with name, an optional color, and an optional from. It replaces the entire set; [] removes every option. To rename an option, give its current name in from, e.g. {"name": "Critical", "from": "High"}; tasks set to it get the new name. Without from, nothing is treated as a rename: a current option that no entry names, in name or from, is removed, and tasks set to it lose that value. An entry without color keeps the current color of the option it matches (by from, else by name).

UpdateFieldOption
hidden: boolean

(Optional) Hide this field from the task detail panel.

clearOnDup: boolean

(Optional) Clear this field when duplicating a task.

viewMembers: string[]

(Optional) Users who can view this field's values; an admin not named sees the definition, not the values. Each entry is a user ID, OID, or email, or "me" for the authenticated user, and must be a member of the field's owner, an external team's member included. Pass [] for the admins only, or null for everyone private allows.

string
editMembers: string[]

(Optional) Users who can edit the values, in the same form as viewMembers; an admin not named can't. Editing also requires viewing the field. Pass [] for the admins only, or null for anyone who can edit the task. locked stops editing in Quire regardless of this list; the API ignores the lock, so this list still applies to API writes.

string
locked: boolean

(Optional) Lock the values: no one can edit them in Quire, admins included, while the API still can, e.g., to push values from another system.

withTime: boolean

(Optional, date only) Include time-of-day in addition to the date.

ndecimal: integer -1, 0, 1, 2, 3

(Optional, number/money only) Number of decimal digits. -1 means no rounding.

durationFormat: string hh:mm:ss, hh:mm, 1h1m, 1h, 1d1h, dd:hh:mm:ss, dd:hh:mm, dd:hh

(Optional, duration/formula only) Duration display format.

formula: string

(Optional, formula only) Formula expression, at most 5,120 characters.

resultType: string text, number, money, date, duration, checkbox

(Optional, formula only) Expected result type.

lookupType: string User, Task, Project, Organization

(Optional, lookup only) Source type for lookup keys.

multiple: boolean

(Optional) Allow multiple values. Applies to select, user, task, and file (always true for file).

conditionFormat: FieldConditionFormat

(Optional) Replacement conditional-format rules. It replaces the entire list; [] removes every rule.

FieldConditionFormat
type: string text, number, money, date, duration, select, checkbox, user, task, hyperlink, email, formula, file, lookup

(Optional) Field type. Immutable on update — if supplied, must match the existing field's type. Usually omitted; include only to verify the stored type. A project's field is one of text, number, money, date, duration, select, checkbox, user, task, hyperlink, email, formula and file; an insight's field is formula or lookup. A key for another type, such as options on a number field, returns 400.

Example
{
  "currency": "USD",
  "percent": false,
  "private": false,
  "lookup": "object",
  "options": [
    {
      "from": "High",
      "color": "13",
      "name": "High"
    }
  ],
  "hidden": false,
  "clearOnDup": false,
  "viewMembers": "[\"me\", \"john\"]",
  "editMembers": "[\"me\"]",
  "locked": false,
  "withTime": false,
  "ndecimal": 2,
  "durationFormat": "hh:mm",
  "formula": "SUM(Subtask.Amount)",
  "resultType": "number",
  "lookupType": "User",
  "multiple": true,
  "conditionFormat": [
    {
      "color": "42",
      "second": "200",
      "when": "today",
      "op": ">=",
      "first": "#/definitions/Number"
    }
  ],
  "type": "number"
}

UpdateFieldOption: object

from: string

(Optional) The current name of the option this entry renames to name; tasks set to that option get name instead. Without it, the entry is the current option of the same name, or a new option if there is none. It must name a current option, and no two entries may match the same option (by name or from); otherwise 400.

color: string

(Optional) Palette color index for the option's chip. Format: two digits [0-5][0-7] (first = row 0-5, second = column 0-7). Examples: 00, 13, 57. NOT a CSS hex color. If omitted on creation, a color is auto-assigned.

name: string

Option name, unique within the field, and at most 1,280 characters; otherwise 400.

Example
{
  "from": "High",
  "color": "13",
  "name": "High"
}

description: string

(Optional) New description for this organization (Markdown supported). An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead. Needs an admin of the organization.

followers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to replace the current followers of this organization (OID, ID, or email). This replaces all existing followers. To modify incrementally, use addFollowers or removeFollowers.

Accepts the same special values as addFollowers: "me" (the current user) and "app" / "app|team" / "app|team|channel" / "app|/path" (the application).

Needs edit access to the organization, even for only "me": unlike a project, an organization can't be followed with read access.

string
addFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to add to this organization (OID, ID, or email). Special values:

  • "me": the current user follows the organization
  • "app": the application follows (receives notifications)

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL when invoking the registered hook. Example: hook https://super.app/hooks/standard + follower app|/soc1/33456/a7 → https://super.app/hooks/standard/soc1/33456/a7

Needs edit access to the organization, even for only "me": unlike a project, an organization can't be followed with read access.

string
removeFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to remove from this organization (OID, ID, or email). Accepts the same special values as addFollowers: "me" (the current user) and "app" / "app|team" / "app|team|channel" / "app|/path" (the application).

Needs edit access to the organization, even for only "me": unlike a project, an organization can't be followed with read access.

string
name: string

(Optional) New display name for this organization (Markdown supported). Needs an admin of the organization.

Example
{
  "description": "**Great** organization to start with.",
  "followers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "addFollowers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "removeFollowers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "name": "My Organization"
}

UpdateProjectBody: object

public: boolean

(Optional) Public toggle. Specify true to make this project public; specify false to make it private. Making it public needs a plan with public projects; otherwise 402 (code 469).

description: string

(Optional) New description for this project (Markdown supported). An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

followers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to replace the current followers of this project (OID, ID, or email). This replaces all existing followers. To modify incrementally, use addFollowers or removeFollowers.

Accepts the same special values as addFollowers: "me" (the current user) and "app" / "app|team" / "app|team|channel" / "app|/path" (the application).

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"].

string
archived: boolean

(Optional) Archive toggle. Specify true to archive this project; specify false to unarchive.

start: string

(Optional) Target start date for this project: a date only, e.g. 2024-01-02; a value with a time of day returns 400. null clears it. Needs a project admin.

due: string

(Optional) Target due date for this project: a date only, e.g. 2024-05-25; a value with a time of day returns 400. null clears it. Needs a project admin.

addFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to add to this project (OID, ID, or email). Special values:

  • "me": the current user follows the project
  • "app": the application follows (receives notifications)

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL when invoking the registered hook. Example: hook https://super.app/hooks/standard + follower app|/soc1/33456/a7 → https://super.app/hooks/standard/soc1/33456/a7

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"].

string
removeFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to remove from this project (OID, ID, or email). Accepts the same special values as addFollowers: "me" (the current user) and "app" / "app|team" / "app|team|channel" / "app|/path" (the application).

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"].

string
name: string

(Optional) New display name for this project (Markdown supported).

Example
{
  "public": true,
  "description": "**Great** project to start with.",
  "followers": [
    "tzufRLqCnud74dARyDSvjWDl",
    "app"
  ],
  "archived": true,
  "start": "2024-01-02",
  "due": "2024-05-25",
  "addFollowers": [
    "sfsvLbDVPvi1QMf2GkDn7VSy"
  ],
  "removeFollowers": [
    "aBuz4MwfZ5CasOae6stnFa2f"
  ],
  "name": "My Project"
}

UpdateReminderBody: object

when: string

(Optional) When this reminder fires (UTC, ISO 8601).

Rejected with 400 on a reminder whose task has a start or due date — it fires from the task's schedule, so a when of its own would be ignored — and also when set to null on one that has no other time to fire from.

recurrence: Recurrence

(Optional) How this reminder repeats; null stops it repeating.

Rejected with 400 on a reminder whose task has a start or due date, for the same reason as when.

leads: ReminderLead

(Optional) When to notify before the fire time, one notification each. Replaces the current list.

Each entry is an object naming exactly one of minutes (an absolute offset) and days (calendar days, so a lead spanning a daylight-saving transition keeps its wall-clock time), the latter taking an optional at clock.

Neither may be negative — a lead counts back from the fire time, and nothing fires after it — nor exceed 10,000 days ahead of it, and there may be at most 30 of them.

ReminderLead
name: string

(Optional) Text to show instead of the default message. Pass null to fall back to the default.

Only inline Markdown applies: **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, `code` and links; anything else, such as a list or a heading, stays literal text. At most 1,280 characters, not counting the markup (400 otherwise).

Example
{
  "when": "2027-03-20T18:30:00.000Z",
  "recurrence": {
    "freq": "weekly",
    "interval": 1,
    "byweekday": "[1,3]",
    "byweekno": 2,
    "bydayno": 25,
    "bymonth": 10,
    "dupsubtasks": false,
    "sincelatest": true,
    "until": "2020-12-22"
  },
  "leads": [
    {
      "minutes": 30,
      "days": 1,
      "at": "09:00"
    }
  ],
  "name": "Pay the **bill** today"
}

UpdateStatusBody: object

color: string

(Optional) Status color index from Quire’s predefined palette (two digits: first 0–5, second 0–7; e.g., 35).

name: string

(Optional) New display name for the status.

value: integer

(Optional) New numeric status value. Non-negative integer indicating progress. Must be unique within the project; a value already in use returns 409. Values ≥ 100 are treated as completed. When listing or searching tasks, ?status=100 (or completed) matches every completed status; values above 100 can't be filtered individually. The value of 0 (the initial status) and 100 (completed) can't change.

Example
{
  "color": "35",
  "name": "Later",
  "value": 50
}

UpdateSublistBody: object

start: string

(Optional) Target start date for this record: a date only, e.g. 2024-01-02; a value with a time of day returns 400.

due: string

(Optional) Target due date for this record: a date only, e.g. 2024-05-25; a value with a time of day returns 400.

changes: Change

(Optional) Tasks to add to or remove from this sublist, applied in order. Each item is {"task": "<task OID>", "exclude": false, "single": false}:

  • exclude: true removes the task instead of adding it.
  • single: true changes only the task itself; by default its subtasks follow it.

A task that doesn't exist is skipped. Example — add one task with its subtasks and leave another out:

[
  {"task": "2MmYOpJH_ZLeehIjjytH1Rwr"},
  {"task": "q8Rn1zX5bKcT0wGvJmLd3PaE", "exclude": true}
]
Change
private: boolean

(Optional) Hide this record from guests and from the visitors of a public project or of a share link, like a custom field's private. A choice only when members is null and partner is null; otherwise it is always true, and false is rejected with 400.

description: string

(Optional) New description for this record (Markdown supported). An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

iconColor: string

(Optional) Icon color index from Quire's predefined palette. Two-digit code [0-5][0-7]: first digit 0-5, second digit 0-7 (e.g. 00, 37, 57). NOT a CSS hex color.

image: string icon-view-list, icon-view-kanban, icon-grid, icon-view-timeline, icon-calendar, icon-timer, icon-briefcase-o, icon-rocket-o, icon-bug-o, icon-user-o, icon-colleagues-o, icon-lightbulb-o, icon-leaf-o, icon-clapperboard, icon-sitemap-o, icon-list, icon-flash-on-o, icon-piggy-bank-o, icon-graduation-cap-o, icon-paper-plane-o, icon-globe-o, icon-music-o, icon-detail, icon-beach-o, icon-paper, icon-home-o, icon-building, icon-database-o, icon-microscope-o, icon-hamburger-o, icon-trophy-o, icon-thumbs-o-up, icon-thumbs-o-down, icon-smile-o, icon-frown-o, icon-meh-o, icon-bullseye, icon-incomplete, icon-filter-o, icon-comment, icon-view-insight, icon-view-dashboard, icon-square-dotted-o

(Optional) Icon image for this record, one of the listed values.

archived: boolean

(Optional) Archive toggle. Specify true to archive this record; specify false to unarchive.

name: string

(Optional) New display name for this record.

id: string

(Optional) New ID for this record, unique among the owner's records of the same kind. If invalid, Quire derives one from the name; if already taken, Quire changes it by appending characters. Neither is an error, so read the id back from the response.

Example
{
  "start": "2024-01-02",
  "due": "2024-05-25",
  "changes": "[{\"task\": \"2MmYOpJH_ZLeehIjjytH1Rwr\"}, {\"task\": \"q8Rn1zX5bKcT0wGvJmLd3PaE\", \"exclude\": true}]",
  "private": false,
  "description": "**Great** record to start with.",
  "iconColor": "37",
  "image": "icon-view-kanban",
  "archived": true,
  "name": "Highlight 101",
  "id": "Highlight101"
}

UpdateTagBody: object

color: string

(Optional) Tag color index from Quire's predefined palette. Two-digit code [0-5][0-7]: first digit 0-5, second digit 0-7 (e.g. 00, 35, 57). NOT a CSS hex color.

global: boolean

(Optional) Whether the tag is global (available across projects). If set to false, you must also provide project.

project: string

(Optional) Project OID that this tag is limited to. Used only when global is explicitly set to false; ignored otherwise.

name: string

(Optional) New display name for the tag.

Example
{
  "color": "35",
  "global": true,
  "project": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld",
  "name": "Later"
}

UpdateTaskBody: object

description: string

(Optional) New task description. An embedded data: image is rejected — upload the image as an attachment instead.

tags: string[]

(Optional) Tags to replace the current tags on this task (OID or name). This replaces all existing tags. To modify incrementally, use addTags or removeTags. Tag names are case-insensitive. Each must be an existing tag of the project, or a global tag of its organization; an unknown tag is rejected with 400, not created.

string
partner: string

(Optional) The external team to share this task with: the name or OID of one of the project's external teams (GET /partner/list/id/{projectId} lists them). The team's members then get access to the task and its subtasks. Setting it takes the right to assign tasks (403 otherwise). A name or OID that matches no team, or a value that isn't a string, is rejected with 400. The API can't remove it: null is rejected too.

recurrence: Recurrence

(Optional) Makes the task repeat, replacing its current recurrence, if any. null stops it repeating.

  • freq (required): daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.
  • interval: a positive integer; 2 with weekly means every 2 weeks. Default: 1.
  • until: end date, e.g. 2026-12-31. Default: never ends.
  • weekly needs byweekday: the days of the week as a list, where 0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday, e.g. [0, 3].
  • monthly needs bydayno, the day of the month (1–31, or "last"), or byweekno, the week of the month (1–5, or "last"), with byweekday as a single day in that week, e.g. 1 for Tuesday. If both byweekno and bydayno are given, byweekno wins.
  • yearly needs bymonth, the month (1–12, 1 = January), plus what monthly needs.
  • dupsubtasks: whether to duplicate subtasks when the task is completed. Default: true.
  • sincelatest: with daily only, whether to repeat from the last completion date. Default: false.

A property that doesn't apply to freq is ignored; an invalid value, or a missing required one, is rejected with 400.

A recurring task always has a due. If the task has none and due is omitted, it is derived from the recurrence: the nearest occurrence since today. The request is rejected if the derived due precedes start; specify due explicitly in that case.

assignees: string[]

(Optional) Assignees to replace the current assignees (OID, ID, or email). This replaces all existing assignees. To modify incrementally, use addAssignees or removeAssignees.

Accepts the same special values as addAssignees: "me" (the current user) and "inherit" (all assignees of the parent task).

Only project members (external-team members included) can be assigned; anyone else is silently left out. An unknown user is rejected with 400.

string
asUser: boolean

(Optional) If true, marks this update as performed by the app. Read asUser as app-as-user: the app itself is the user, not the authorizing user. Default: false (updated by the authorizing user). In bulk-update, each item has its own.

followers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to replace the current followers (OID, ID, or email).

Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": include followers of the parent task
  • "app": the application follows (receives notifications)

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL (e.g., .../standard/soc1/33456/a7).

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

string
successors: string[]

(Optional) Successors to replace the current successors (task OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

string
start: string

(Optional) Start date/time in UTC.

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

Notes:

  • Seconds are not supported.
  • 2020-10-30T00:00:00 is treated as 2020-10-30 (date only).
  • To specify exactly midnight UTC, use 2020-10-30T00:00 (no seconds).
due: string

(Optional) Due date/time in UTC.

  • With time: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mmZ (e.g., 2020-10-30T09:30Z).
  • Date only: yyyy-MM-dd (e.g., 2020-10-30).

Notes:

  • Seconds are not supported.
  • 2020-10-30T00:00:00 is treated as 2020-10-30 (date only).
  • To specify exactly midnight UTC, use 2020-10-30T00:00 (no seconds).
  • null clears it. It is rejected if the task is recurring, since a recurring task always has a due; pass recurrence: null in the same request to stop repeating and clear the due together.
yourField: object

PLACEHOLDER — do NOT send a key literally named yourField. Instead, use the custom field's own name (as defined via /project/add-field) as the JSON key, with a value matching the field's type:

  • Text / Email / Hyperlink: string.
  • Number / Money: numeric value (no currency symbol).
  • Checkbox: true or false.
  • Select: option name (string).
  • Date: ISO 8601 timestamp (yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssZ) or date-only (yyyy-MM-dd).
  • Duration: number of seconds.
  • User: user OID, user ID, or email — server resolves to the user's OID.
  • Task: task OID, integer task ID, or #<id> string — server resolves to the task's OID (scoped to this project).
  • File: the attachment list as a task returns it (absolute url accepted); send an entry back unchanged to keep that file.
  • Multi-value (fields configured with multiple: true): provide a list. Pass null to clear the field.

A field you can't view or edit (the definition's viewMembers and editMembers) is rejected with 400; locked stops editing in Quire only, not through the API.

Example body fragment: {"Priority": 3, "Owners": ["alice", "bob@example.com"], "Depends": ["#42"]}.

peekaboo:
boolean
integer

(Optional) Peekaboo setting. Accepts a boolean or a positive integer:

  • true: Hide indefinitely (task and subtasks).
  • positive integer: Number of days to hide.
  • false: Undo previous peekaboo.
section: boolean

(Optional) true makes this task a section; false makes it a normal task. If both section and milestone are sent, only section is applied.

milestone: boolean

(Optional) true makes this task a milestone; false makes it a normal task. Ignored if section is sent too.

addTags: string[]

(Optional) Tags to add to this task (OID or name). Tag names are case-insensitive. Each must be an existing tag of the project, or a global tag of its organization; an unknown tag is rejected with 400, not created.

string
removeTags: string[]

(Optional) Tags to remove from this task (OID or name). Tag names are case-insensitive. An unknown tag is rejected with 400.

string
addAssignees: string[]

(Optional) Assignees to add (OID, ID, or email). Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": include all assignees of the parent task

Only project members (external-team members included) can be assigned; anyone else is silently left out. An unknown user is rejected with 400.

string
removeAssignees: string[]

(Optional) Assignees to remove (OID, ID, or email).

Accepts the same special values as addAssignees: "me" (the current user) and "inherit" (all assignees of the parent task).

string
addFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to add (OID, ID, or email). Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": include followers of the parent task
  • "app": the application follows (receives notifications)

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL (e.g., .../standard/soc1/33456/a7).

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

string
removeFollowers: string[]

(Optional) Followers to remove (OID, ID, or email).

Special values:

  • "me": the current user
  • "inherit": remove followers that were inherited from the parent task
  • "app": the application

App follower syntax:

  • app|team or app|team|channel
  • app|/path → appended to the hook URL.

With read access only, addFollowers and removeFollowers may name only yourself: "me", or "app" to add the app on your behalf. Adding or removing anyone else returns 403, even along with yourself. followers replaces every follower, so it needs edit access even as ["me"]. An update that only follows or unfollows doesn't change editedAt.

string
addSuccessors: string[]

(Optional) Successors to add (task OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

string
removeSuccessors: string[]

(Optional) Successors to remove (task OID or ID).

IDs can be specified as #id or id. Integer IDs are also accepted.

string
name: string

(Optional) New task name.

status: integer

(Optional) New status. Must be one of the project's status values (GET /status/list/id/{projectId} lists them); any other value is rejected with 400. Every project has 0, the initial status, and 100, completed; 100 or more means completed. Specify 100 to complete the task. Completion may be rejected (409 Conflict) when project settings require all predecessors to be completed first, or require an approval to be granted.

etc: integer

(Optional) Estimated time to complete, in seconds. Must be 0 to 864,000,000 (10,000 days) or null. Specify null to clear the value.

priority: integer -1, 0, 1, 2

(Optional) New priority: -1 Low, 0 Medium, 1 High, 2 Urgent. (The server also accepts the case-insensitive English names Low, Medium, High, Urgent, but the integer form is recommended for typed callers.)

sourceRef: object

(Optional) A JSON object your app stores with the task, such as where the task came from. Quire keeps it as is and returns it as sourceRef whenever the task is read.

  • text (optional): a Markdown string Quire shows as the task's source line in the task details. Include a link to the source, e.g. Source: [GitHub issue 42](https://github.com/acme/web/issues/42).
  • Any other key: your app's own data, not shown in Quire. Put it under a key named after your app, e.g. github, so it won't clash with another app's.
  • To find these tasks later, search with ?source-ref=github: it returns the tasks whose sourceRef has that key, whatever its value.
  • Size: at most about 2,048 characters, keys and values together, and text must be a string; otherwise 400.
  • It replaces the stored object as a whole: keys you leave out are removed, and null removes sourceRef. Another app may have stored its own key on the task; to keep it, read the task first and send that key back.
Example
{
  "description": "This is a **cool** task.",
  "tags": [
    "ITaVbkhh3iVcEcV3vuSLeE2k"
  ],
  "partner": "UI design team",
  "recurrence": {
    "freq": "weekly",
    "interval": 1,
    "byweekday": "[1,3]",
    "byweekno": 2,
    "bydayno": 25,
    "bymonth": 10,
    "dupsubtasks": false,
    "sincelatest": true,
    "until": "2020-12-22"
  },
  "assignees": [
    "6QMKkEPBVWETLWrXqws94ALU"
  ],
  "asUser": true,
  "followers": [
    "tzufRLqCnud74dARyDSvjWDl",
    "app"
  ],
  "successors": "[\"#13\"]",
  "start": "2026-05-01",
  "due": "2026-05-10T17:00Z",
  "yourField": "object",
  "peekaboo": true,
  "section": true,
  "milestone": true,
  "addTags": [
    "X6nmx9XjEO2wKbqeB1pRT43C"
  ],
  "removeTags": [
    "mPAQrYU1qt8wAYAInKRlTnvl"
  ],
  "addAssignees": [
    "6QMKkEPBVWETLWrXqws94ALU"
  ],
  "removeAssignees": [
    "Job4NSW9xK6Owcke8iKj7zyH"
  ],
  "addFollowers": [
    "sfsvLbDVPvi1QMf2GkDn7VSy"
  ],
  "removeFollowers": [
    "aBuz4MwfZ5CasOae6stnFa2f"
  ],
  "addSuccessors": "[\"#13\"]",
  "removeSuccessors": "[\"#13\"]",
  "name": "New idea",
  "status": 100,
  "etc": 0,
  "priority": 0,
  "sourceRef": "{\"github\": {\"repo\": \"acme/web\", \"issue\": 42}, \"text\": \"Source: [GitHub issue 42](https://github.com/acme/web/issues/42)\"}"
}

UpdateTimelogBody: object

end: string

(Optional) New end timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC). Must be on or after the (new or existing) start. Sub-second precision is truncated to whole seconds. Omit or set null to preserve.

start: string

(Optional) New start timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC). Sub-second precision is truncated to whole seconds. Omit or set null to preserve.

user: string

(Optional) New user the log is credited to (OID, ID, or email). Omit or set null to preserve. Send empty string to reset to the authenticated caller.

billable: boolean

(Optional) New billable flag. Omit or set null to preserve.

note: string

(Optional) New note. Omit or set null to preserve. Send empty string to clear.

Example
{
  "end": "2026-04-26T10:45:00Z",
  "start": "2026-04-26T09:15:00Z",
  "user": "john.doe@example.com",
  "billable": false,
  "note": "Updated note"
}

User: object

timeZone: object

The time zone of the current user: name, and offset from UTC in minutes. Omitted for other users.

locale: string

The locale of the current user. Omitted for other users.

url: string

URL of this user on the Quire website.

nameHtml: string

User name rendered as an HTML fragment converted from Markdown.

nameText: string

User name with Markdown removed.

name: string

Display name of the user (Markdown supported).

id: string

User ID.

email: string

Email address.

website: string

Website URL.

description: string

Description (Markdown supported).

descriptionHtml: string

Description rendered as an HTML fragment converted from Markdown.

descriptionText: string

Description with Markdown removed.

iconColor: string

Color index for the icon from Quire’s predefined palette. Two-digit code: first digit 0–5, second digit 0–7 (e.g., 37).

image: string

Image URL representing this record.

oid: string

Object identifier (OID), a UUID-like unique string.

Example
{
  "timeZone": "{\"offset\": 480, \"name\": \"Asia/Taipei\"}",
  "locale": "en_GB",
  "url": "https://quire.io/u/john",
  "nameHtml": "John",
  "nameText": "John",
  "name": "John",
  "id": "john",
  "email": "john@gmail.com",
  "website": "https://coolwebsites.com",
  "description": "This is *cool*!",
  "descriptionHtml": "This is <i>cool</i>!",
  "descriptionText": "This is cool!",
  "iconColor": "37",
  "image": "https://quire.s3.amazonaws.com/oid/image.jpg",
  "oid": "Dyh2YkFcu9uLgLFIeN1kB4Ld"
}

Recurring:

byweekday: object
Example
{
  "byweekday": [
    1,
    4
  ]
}
